FILE 1/217: README.md
====================================================================================================
# lenOS

A personal LineageOS 24.0 build for the Nothing Phone (3a) and (3a) Pro
(`asteroids`).

This repo is not a ROM distribution. It is the patch set and small apps that
make up the build. The LineageOS tree stays clean and every change is carried
as an ordinary git patch, so the build can be reproduced and reviewed. If you
have the same phone, you can build it too, or take only the changes you want.

lenOS is not affiliated with LineageOS, Nothing, or GrapheneOS. It is a
personal project, not a supported product.

The experimental series is optional and even less tested. A normal build never
applies it.

## What it changes

- strict DNS-over-TLS, non-Google time and captive-portal endpoints
- hardened first-boot defaults, PIN scrambling, duress wipe, and memory clearing
  on lock
- fewer bundled apps; no Google apps or services added
- optional extras behind `LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1`

The full list, including what does not work, is in
[`docs/features.md`](docs/features.md).

## Root and verified boot

The default image is rootless: no `su`, BakaSU, KernelSU, or Magisk is
included. Root is an explicit post-build option:

```bash
LENOS_ROOT=bakasu ./lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh root-prepare
LENOS_ROOT=bakasu ./lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh package
```

`bakasu` is the preferred profile and `kernelsu` is the fallback. The build
itself stays rootless. The post-build step verifies the base OTA against your
configured OTA/AVB keys, patches `init_boot`, re-signs the OS AVB partitions with
your key, and keeps the root manager as a separate APK. The default rootless
packaging path verifies that the final `init_boot` is stock, so a pre-rooted base
cannot be shipped accidentally. Root has not been boot-tested; see
[`docs/root.md`](docs/root.md) for the exact pins and limitations.

The helper re-signs the OS AVB chain with your AVB/OTA keys via avbroot.
Bootloader locking is manual and unsupported by the helper; the scripts never
flash, wipe, or lock. Root does not make locking supported. The lock checklist
is in [`docs/flash-and-lock.md`](docs/flash-and-lock.md).

## Build

You need a LineageOS 24.0 tree for `asteroids`, a working Android build
environment, and your own signing setup. The patches were developed against the
`6.6/lineage-24.0` device trees in the
[NullDebris manifest](https://github.com/NullDebris/manifest). A tree that has
drifted may need patch updates; the patch tool is strict and stops rather than
applies with fuzz.

Clone this repo into `vendor/lenos`, then check and apply the series:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ntrop6/lenos-patches.git vendor/lenos
python3 vendor/lenos/tools/lenos-patch.py --tree . --check
python3 vendor/lenos/tools/lenos-patch.py --tree . --apply
```

Build with your normal LineageOS flow, for example:

```bash
source build/envsetup.sh
lunch lenos_asteroids-user
mka bacon
```

The helper script in the repo root is optional. It automates a particular
build/signing setup and is not required to use the patches. Details are in
[`docs/build.md`](docs/build.md).

To return the tree to its pinned state:

```bash
python3 vendor/lenos/tools/lenos-patch.py --tree . --reset
```

## What is here

- `patches/` — the default patch series, grouped by upstream project
- `patches-experimental/` — optional second series, applied after the default one
- `app/LenosSecurity/` — small settings app for controls the stock UI lacks
- `config/`, `rro/`, `release/` — product configuration and build inputs
- `docs/` — build notes, feature list, porting notes, flashing safety
- `experimental/` — opt-in app source, checks, and status notes
- `tools/` — patch application, read-only verification helpers, and the pinned
  opt-in root preparer
- `tests/` — source-level and host-side tests for the patches

The feature list and its honest limits are in
[`docs/features.md`](docs/features.md). The long, rough porting notes are in
[`docs/graphene-porting.md`](docs/graphene-porting.md).

## Experimental work

The optional series contains features that are source-complete but still need a
build and a device to validate. It applies only after the default series and is
selected with `LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1`. The bionic hardened-thread-stack
experiment is part of this series; the stable/default build keeps the stock
thread mapping. See
[`docs/experimental.md`](docs/experimental.md) for the order, reset rules, and
what remains untested.

## Tests

From the patchkit checkout, set `LENOS_WORKSPACE` to a pristine LineageOS tree
and run:

```bash
LENOS_WORKSPACE=/path/to/lineage bash tests/run-tests.sh
```

The suite checks that every patch applies to the pinned sources and asserts the
resulting code and resources. It does not build or boot Android.

## Flashing

Nothing here flashes, wipes, or locks a phone. Flashing is destructive and can
brick the device. Read [`docs/flash-and-lock.md`](docs/flash-and-lock.md) before
using any build.

## License

Apache-2.0. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). Some patches are adapted from GrapheneOS;
the sources and deviations are recorded in
[`docs/graphene-porting.md`](docs/graphene-porting.md),
[`experimental/docs/provenance.md`](experimental/docs/provenance.md), and the
per-patch notes.

// lenOS companion app. Built with the platform API surface (not the public
// SDK): the app uses @SystemApi/@hide surface such as WifiManager's DHCP
// hostname restriction and the keyguard credential paths. Soong rejects
// sdk_version together with platform_apis, so only the latter is set.
android_app {
    name: "LenosSecurity",
    srcs: ["src/**/*.java"],
    resource_dirs: ["res"],
    manifest: "AndroidManifest.xml",
    platform_apis: true,
    privileged: true,
    certificate: "platform",
}

<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    package="org.lenos.security"
    android:versionCode="4"
    android:versionName="1.0.0">

    <uses-sdk android:minSdkVersion="34" android:targetSdkVersion="36" />

    <!-- signature|privileged|development: platform signature satisfies it if the
         APK is signed with the ROM's platform key. All writes still fall back to
         root (su) when the direct path is denied, so this is belt-and-suspenders. -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_KEYGUARD_SECURE_STORAGE" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS" />
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_PRIVILEGED_PHONE_STATE" />

    <application
        android:name=".CrashApp"
        android:label="@string/app_name"
        android:icon="@drawable/logo"
        android:allowBackup="false"
        android:supportsRtl="true"
        android:theme="@android:style/Theme.DeviceDefault.NoActionBar">

            </intent-filter>
            <intent-filter>
                <action android:name="org.lenos.security.SETTINGS" />
                <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
            </intent-filter>
        </activity>
    </application>
</manifest>

package org.lenos.security;

import android.app.Application;
import android.util.Log;

/**
 * Logs any uncaught throwable to a file so a crash is diagnosable even when
 * the user can't see logcat. The Activity itself also renders its own stack.
 */
public class CrashApp extends Application {
    @Override
    public void onCreate() {
        super.onCreate();
        // Capture the real handler before installing this one. Reading the
        // default inside the lambda would return this lambda and recurse.
        final Thread.UncaughtExceptionHandler previous =
                Thread.getDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler();
        Thread.setDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler((t, e) -> {
            Log.e("lenOS-security", "uncaught in " + t, e);
            try {
                java.io.File f = new java.io.File(getFilesDir(), "last-crash.txt");
                java.io.PrintWriter pw = new java.io.PrintWriter(f);
                e.printStackTrace(pw);
                pw.close();
            } catch (Exception ignored) {
            }
            // Delegate to the real default handler so the process still dies
            // and Android shows the system crash dialog rather than hanging.
            if (previous != null) {
                previous.uncaughtException(t, e);
            }
        });
    }
}

package org.lenos.security;

import android.content.Context;

import java.io.BufferedReader;
import java.io.InputStreamReader;
import java.lang.reflect.Method;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;

/**
 * Runs as root via {@code app_process} so Binder calls are uid 0.
 *
 * Stdin protocol (one field per line; secrets never on argv):
 *   HAS\n<ownerPin>\n
 *   SET\n<ownerPin>\n<duressPin>\n<duressPassword>\n
 *   DELETE\n<ownerPin>\n
 */
public final class DuressCli {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int code = 1;
        try {
            Context ctx = systemContext();
            LockBridge lock = new LockBridge(ctx);
            BufferedReader in = new BufferedReader(
                    new InputStreamReader(System.in, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            String cmd = line(in);
            if ("HAS".equals(cmd)) {
                Object owner = lock.createPin(line(in));
                try {
                    boolean has = lock.hasDuress(owner);
                    System.out.println(has ? "HAS=1" : "HAS=0");
                } finally {
                    lock.zeroize(owner);
                }
                code = 0;
            } else if ("SET".equals(cmd)) {
                Object owner = lock.createPin(line(in));
                Object pin = lock.createPin(line(in));
                Object pass = lock.createPassword(line(in));
                try {
                    lock.setDuress(owner, pin, pass);
                    System.out.println("SET=OK");
                } finally {
                    lock.zeroize(owner);
                    lock.zeroize(pin);
                    lock.zeroize(pass);
                }
                code = 0;
            } else if ("DELETE".equals(cmd)) {
                Object owner = lock.createPin(line(in));
                try {
                    lock.deleteDuress(owner);
                    System.out.println("DELETE=OK");
                } finally {
                    lock.zeroize(owner);
                }
                code = 0;
            } else {
                System.err.println("unknown command");
            }
        } catch (Throwable t) {
            System.err.println(t.getClass().getSimpleName() + ": " + t.getMessage());
            code = 2;
        }
        System.exit(code);
    }

    private static Context systemContext() throws Exception {
        Class<?> looper = Class.forName("android.os.Looper");
        looper.getMethod("prepareMainLooper").invoke(null);
        Class<?> at = Class.forName("android.app.ActivityThread");
        at.getMethod("systemMain").invoke(null);
        Object thread = at.getMethod("currentActivityThread").invoke(null);
        Method get = at.getMethod("getSystemContext");
        return (Context) get.invoke(thread);
    }

    private static String line(BufferedReader in) throws Exception {
        String s = in.readLine();
        if (s == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("short input");
        }
        return s;
    }
}

FILE 10/217: app/LenosSecurity/src/org/lenos/security/LockBridge.java
====================================================================================================
package org.lenos.security;

import android.content.Context;

import java.lang.reflect.Constructor;
import java.lang.reflect.Method;

/**
 * Reflection wrapper over the hidden
 * {@code com.android.internal.widget.LockPatternUtils} and
 * {@code com.android.internal.widget.LockscreenCredential}, so the app builds
 * against the public android.jar only.
 *
 * Backed by the lenOS 1.0 framework patch
 * (frameworks/base/0005-lenos-duress-credentials), which adds:
 *   setDuressCredentials(LockscreenCredential, LockscreenCredential, LockscreenCredential)
 *   hasDuressCredentials(LockscreenCredential) -> boolean
 *   deleteDuressCredentials(LockscreenCredential)
 */
final class LockBridge {
    private static final String LPU = "com.android.internal.widget.LockPatternUtils";
    private static final String LC = "com.android.internal.widget.LockscreenCredential";

    private final Object lpu;

    LockBridge(Context ctx) throws Exception {
        Class<?> c = Class.forName(LPU);
        Constructor<?> ctor = c.getConstructor(Context.class);
        lpu = ctor.newInstance(ctx);
    }

    boolean isSecure() {
        try {
            Method m = lpu.getClass().getMethod("isSecure", int.class);
            return (Boolean) m.invoke(lpu, 0);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    Object createPin(String pin) throws Exception {
        Class<?> c = Class.forName(LC);
        Method m = c.getMethod("createPin", CharSequence.class);
        return m.invoke(null, pin);
    }

    Object createPassword(String pass) throws Exception {
        Class<?> c = Class.forName(LC);
        Method m = c.getMethod("createPassword", CharSequence.class);
        return m.invoke(null, pass);
    }

    void setDuress(Object owner, Object pin, Object pass) throws Exception {
        Class<?> lc = Class.forName(LC);
        Method m = lpu.getClass().getMethod("setDuressCredentials", lc, lc, lc);
        m.invoke(lpu, owner, pin, pass);
    }

    boolean hasDuress(Object owner) throws Exception {
        Class<?> lc = Class.forName(LC);
        Method m = lpu.getClass().getMethod("hasDuressCredentials", lc);
        return (Boolean) m.invoke(lpu, owner);
    }

    void deleteDuress(Object owner) throws Exception {
        Class<?> lc = Class.forName(LC);
        Method m = lpu.getClass().getMethod("deleteDuressCredentials", lc);
        m.invoke(lpu, owner);
    }

    void zeroize(Object cred) {
        if (cred == null) {
            return;
        }
        try {
            Method m = cred.getClass().getMethod("zeroize");
            m.invoke(cred);
        } catch (Exception ignored) {
        }
    }
}

package org.lenos.security;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.app.AlertDialog;
import android.graphics.Color;
import android.graphics.Typeface;
import android.graphics.drawable.GradientDrawable;
import android.os.Bundle;
import android.provider.Settings;
import android.text.InputType;
import android.util.Log;
import android.util.TypedValue;
import android.view.Gravity;
import android.view.View;
import android.view.ViewGroup;
import android.view.WindowManager;
import android.widget.AdapterView;
import android.widget.ArrayAdapter;
import android.widget.Button;
import android.widget.CompoundButton;
import android.widget.EditText;
import android.widget.ImageView;
import android.widget.LinearLayout;
import android.widget.ScrollView;
import android.widget.Spinner;
import android.widget.Switch;
import android.widget.TextView;
import android.widget.Toast;

import java.io.PrintWriter;
import java.io.StringWriter;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * Stand-in Settings page for lenOS 1.0 where the stock Settings APK never
 * grew the "lenOS security" category. Backed by the hardening backend that IS
 * in this build (auto-BFU timer in init, duress in LockSettingsService,
 * etc.).
 *
 * Every privileged write tries the direct Settings/LockPatternUtils path first
 * and falls back to root (BakaSU su) on denial. Secrets travel on stdin only.
 */
public class MainActivity extends Activity {
    static final String BFU_SETTING = "settings_reboot_after_timeout";
    static final int BFU_DEFAULT_MS = 64_800_000; // 18h, matches init default
    static final int BFU_12H_MS = 43_200_000;
    // Settings.Secure key read by the SystemUI and Settings scramble readers
    // (android.ext.settings.ExtSettings, GrapheneOS port). lenOS default: on.
    static final String SCRAMBLE_KEY = "lockscreen_scramble_pin_layout";

    private static final int BG = Color.parseColor("#111318");
    private static final int CARD = Color.parseColor("#1C1F26");
    private static final int TEXT = Color.parseColor("#E8EAED");
    private static final int MUTED = Color.parseColor("#9AA0A6");
    private static final int ACCENT = Color.parseColor("#8AB4F8");
    private static final int DANGER = Color.parseColor("#F28B82");
    private static final int STROKE = Color.parseColor("#3C4043");

    private static final LinkedHashMap<Integer, String> BFU_CHOICES = new LinkedHashMap<Integer, String>();
    static {
        BFU_CHOICES.put(0, "Off");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(600_000, "10 minutes");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(1_800_000, "30 minutes");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(3_600_000, "1 hour");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(7_200_000, "2 hours");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(14_400_000, "4 hours");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(28_800_000, "8 hours");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(43_200_000, "12 hours");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(64_800_000, "18 hours (ROM default)");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(86_400_000, "1 day");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(129_600_000, "36 hours");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(172_800_000, "2 days");
        BFU_CHOICES.put(259_200_000, "3 days");
    }

    private LockBridge lock;
    private TextView statusBody;
    private TextView bfuSummary;
    private TextView duressStatus;
    private Switch scrambleSwitch;
    private Spinner bfuSpinner;

    // Last-committed values, used to ignore programmatic UI sync.
    // (A plain boolean suppress flag is racy for Spinner: setSelection()
    //  posts onItemSelected to the next looper tick, so the flag is already
    //  reset by the time the listener runs.)
    private int currentBfu = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
    private int currentScramble = Integer.MIN_VALUE;

    private EditText ownerPin;
    private EditText duressPin;
    private EditText duressPin2;
    private EditText duressPass;
    private EditText duressPass2;

    @Override
    protected void onCreate(Bundle savedInstanceState) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState);
        try {
            getWindow().addFlags(WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE);
            buildUi();
        } catch (Throwable t) {
            Log.e("lenOS-security", "onCreate failed", t);
            try {
                setContentView(errorScreen(stack(t)));
            } catch (Throwable ignored) {
            }
        }
    }

    private void buildUi() {
        try {
            lock = new LockBridge(this);
        } catch (Throwable t) {
            Log.w("lenOS-security", "LockBridge deferred", t);
            lock = null;
        }

        ScrollView scroll = new ScrollView(this);
        scroll.setFillViewport(true);
        scroll.setBackgroundColor(BG);

        LinearLayout root = column();
        root.setPadding(dp(16), dp(20), dp(16), dp(32));
        scroll.addView(root);

        // Logo (branding/logo.png) — decorative header.
        ImageView logo = new ImageView(this);
        logo.setImageResource(R.drawable.logo);
        logo.setAdjustViewBounds(true);
        logo.setMaxWidth(dp(120));
        logo.setMaxHeight(dp(130));
        logo.setScaleType(ImageView.ScaleType.FIT_CENTER);
        LinearLayout.LayoutParams logoLp = new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(
                ViewGroup.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT, ViewGroup.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT);
        logoLp.topMargin = dp(8);
        logo.setLayoutParams(logoLp);
        root.addView(logo);

        root.addView(text("lenOS security", 26, TEXT, true));
        root.addView(text(getString(R.string.lenos_header_subtitle), 13, MUTED, false));
        root.addView(text("Hardening controls missing from Settings on this image.", 13, MUTED, false));

        statusBody = text("", 13, MUTED, false);
        root.addView(card("Status", statusBody));

        bfuSummary = text("", 13, MUTED, false);
        bfuSpinner = new Spinner(this);
        String[] labels = BFU_CHOICES.values().toArray(new String[0]);
        bfuSpinner.setAdapter(new ArrayAdapter<String>(this,
                android.R.layout.simple_spinner_dropdown_item, labels));
        LinearLayout bfuCol = column();
        bfuCol.addView(bfuSummary);
        bfuCol.addView(text("Reboots after the phone stays locked (Before First Unlock). Lock once after changing so the timer arms.", 13, MUTED, false));
        bfuCol.addView(bfuSpinner);
        root.addView(card("Automatic BFU reboot", bfuCol));

        scrambleSwitch = new Switch(this);
        scrambleSwitch.setText("Scramble PIN layout");
        scrambleSwitch.setTextColor(TEXT);
        LinearLayout pinCol = column();
        pinCol.addView(text("Randomizes the lock-screen PIN pad after a PIN lock is set.", 13, MUTED, false));
        pinCol.addView(scrambleSwitch);
        root.addView(card("PIN scramble", pinCol));

        LinearLayout wifiCol = column();
        wifiCol.addView(text("Off by default for every network (GrapheneOS-faithful): DHCP "
                + "requests carry no hostname, so the local network and its router logs "
                + "never see this phone's name. Override per network in the Wi-Fi network "
                + "details (Advanced).", 13, MUTED, false));
        root.addView(card("Wi-Fi DHCP hostname", wifiCol));

        duressStatus = text("Enter your current screen-lock PIN to check or change duress credentials.", 13, MUTED, false);
        ownerPin = passwordField("Current screen-lock PIN", true);
        duressPin = passwordField("Duress PIN (min 4 digits)", true);
        duressPin2 = passwordField("Confirm duress PIN", true);
        duressPass = passwordField("Duress password (min 4 characters)", false);
        duressPass2 = passwordField("Confirm duress password", false);

        Button check = accentButton("Check duress status");
        Button save = dangerButton("Save duress PIN + password");
        Button delete = outlineButton("Delete duress credentials");
        check.setOnClickListener(new View.OnClickListener() {
            @Override public void onClick(View v) { checkDuress(); }
        });
        save.setOnClickListener(new View.OnClickListener() {
            @Override public void onClick(View v) { confirmSaveDuress(); }
        });
        delete.setOnClickListener(new View.OnClickListener() {
            @Override public void onClick(View v) { confirmDeleteDuress(); }
        });

        LinearLayout duressCol = column();
        duressCol.addView(text("Entering either duress credential anywhere Android asks for your lock deletes the keystore secrets protecting storage, erases stored eSIM profiles and powers the device off. Storage is gone. Do not test on this phone.", 13, DANGER, false));
        duressCol.addView(duressStatus);
        duressCol.addView(ownerPin);
        duressCol.addView(check);
        duressCol.addView(duressPin);
        duressCol.addView(duressPin2);
        duressCol.addView(duressPass);
        duressCol.addView(duressPass2);
        duressCol.addView(save);
        duressCol.addView(delete);
        root.addView(card("Duress PIN and password", duressCol));

        LinearLayout extra = column();
        extra.addView(text("Wi-Fi MAC + DHCP hostname: per network in Settings \u2192 Network & internet \u2192 Internet.", 13, MUTED, false));
        extra.addView(text("Other sensors: Settings \u2192 Apps \u2192 [app] \u2192 Permissions.", 13, MUTED, false));
        extra.addView(text("Per-app network block: app data-usage screen (Lineage POLICY_REJECT_ALL).", 13, MUTED, false));
        extra.addView(text("Do not lock the bootloader from this helper.", 13, DANGER, false));
        root.addView(card("Also on this build", extra));

        setContentView(scroll);
        wireBfu();
        wireScramble();
        refreshStatus();
        refreshBfu();
        refreshScramble();
    }

    private void wireBfu() {
        bfuSpinner.setOnItemSelectedListener(new AdapterView.OnItemSelectedListener() {
            @Override public void onItemSelected(AdapterView<?> p, View v, int pos, long id) {
                int value = bfuValueAt(pos);
                if (value == currentBfu) {
                    return; // programmatic re-sync, not a user change
                }
                if (!writeBfu(value)) {
                    toast("Could not write BFU. Grant BakaSU root to this app.");
                    refreshBfu();
                    return;
                }
                currentBfu = value;
                refreshBfu();
                toast(value == 0 ? "Automatic BFU is off" : "BFU set. Lock the phone once to arm.");
            }
            @Override public void onNothingSelected(AdapterView<?> p) {}
        });
    }

    private void wireScramble() {
        scrambleSwitch.setOnCheckedChangeListener(new CompoundButton.OnCheckedChangeListener() {
            @Override public void onCheckedChanged(CompoundButton buttonView, boolean isChecked) {
                int value = isChecked ? 1 : 0;
                if (value == currentScramble) {
                    return;
                }
                if (!writeScramble(value)) {
                    toast("Could not write PIN scramble");
                    refreshScramble();
                    return;
                }
                currentScramble = value;
                toast(isChecked ? "PIN scramble on" : "PIN scramble off");
            }
        });
    }

    private void refreshStatus() {
        String secure;
        try {
            secure = lock == null ? "lock API deferred" : (lock.isSecure() ? "yes" : "no");
        } catch (Exception e) {
            secure = "error: " + e.getMessage();
        }
        statusBody.setText(
                "profile " + sysProp("ro.lenos.hardening.profile", "?") + "\n"
                        + "auto-BFU backend " + sysProp("ro.lenos.security.auto_bfu", "?") + "\n"
                        + "duress backend " + sysProp("ro.lenos.security.duress", "?") + "\n"
                        + "wifi MAC + DHCP hostname privacy defaults (per-network)\n"
                        + "owner screen lock " + secure);
    }

    private boolean writeBfu(int value) {
        try {
            if (Settings.Global.putInt(getContentResolver(), BFU_SETTING, value)) {
                return true;
            }
        } catch (Throwable ignored) {
            // Not privileged: fall through to root.
        }
        return RootShell.settingsPutGlobal(BFU_SETTING, Integer.toString(value)).ok();
    }

    private void refreshBfu() {
        int value = Settings.Global.getInt(getContentResolver(), BFU_SETTING, BFU_DEFAULT_MS);
        if (!BFU_CHOICES.containsKey(value)) {
            value = BFU_DEFAULT_MS;
        }
        currentBfu = value;
        int index = 0;
        int i = 0;
        for (Integer key : BFU_CHOICES.keySet()) {
            if (key == value) {
                index = i;
                break;
            }
            i++;
        }
        bfuSpinner.setSelection(index);
        bfuSummary.setText(value == 0
                ? "Automatic BFU reboot is off"
                : "Reboot after the device remains locked for " + BFU_CHOICES.get(value));
    }

    private void refreshScramble() {
        int value = readScramble();
        currentScramble = value;
        scrambleSwitch.setChecked(value != 0);
    }

    private int readScramble() {
        // Settings.Secure key, the same one ExtSettings.
        // SCRAMBLE_LOCKSCREEN_PIN_LAYOUT_PRIMARY drives in SystemUI/Settings.
        return Settings.Secure.getInt(getContentResolver(), SCRAMBLE_KEY, 1);
    }

    private boolean writeScramble(int value) {
        try {
            if (Settings.Secure.putInt(getContentResolver(), SCRAMBLE_KEY, value)) {
                return true;
            }
        } catch (Throwable ignored) {
            // Not privileged: fall through to root.
        }
        return RootShell.settingsPutSecure(SCRAMBLE_KEY, Integer.toString(value)).ok();
    }

    private void checkDuress() {
        Object owner = null;
        try {
            requireLock();
            owner = ownerCredential();
            boolean has;
            try {
                has = lock.hasDuress(owner);
            } catch (Exception e) {
                if (!isPrivError(e)) {
                    throw e;
                }
                RootShell.Result r = RootShell.duress(this, "HAS\n" + textOf(ownerPin) + "\n");
                if (!r.ok()) {
                    throw new IllegalStateException(rootFail(r, e));
                }
                has = r.out.contains("HAS=1");
            }
            duressStatus.setText(has
                    ? "Duress credentials are set. You can update or delete them."
                    : "No duress credentials are set.");
            duressStatus.setTextColor(has ? ACCENT : MUTED);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            duressStatus.setText(friendly(e));
            duressStatus.setTextColor(DANGER);
        } finally {
            zero(owner);
        }
    }

    private void confirmSaveDuress() {
        final String pin = textOf(duressPin);
        final String pin2 = textOf(duressPin2);
        final String pass = textOf(duressPass);
        final String pass2 = textOf(duressPass2);
        if (pin.length() < 4 || !pin.equals(pin2)) {
            toast("Duress PIN must match and be at least 4 digits");
            return;
        }
        if (pass.length() < 4 || !pass.equals(pass2)) {
            toast("Duress password must match and be at least 4 characters");
            return;
        }
        if (pin.equals(textOf(ownerPin))) {
            toast("Duress PIN must be different from your real PIN");
            return;
        }
        new AlertDialog.Builder(this)
                .setTitle("Destructive credential warning")
                .setMessage("Entering either duress credential will immediately and irreversibly make storage inaccessible, erase stored eSIM profiles and power off. Do not test on this phone.")
                .setNegativeButton("Cancel", null)
                .setPositiveButton("Proceed", new android.content.DialogInterface.OnClickListener() {
                    @Override public void onClick(android.content.DialogInterface d, int w) {
                        saveDuress(pin, pass);
                    }
                })
                .show();
    }

    private void saveDuress(String pin, String pass) {
        Object owner = null;
        Object dPin = null;
        Object dPass = null;
        try {
            requireLock();
            owner = ownerCredential();
            dPin = lock.createPin(pin);
            dPass = lock.createPassword(pass);
            try {
                lock.setDuress(owner, dPin, dPass);
            } catch (Exception e) {
                if (!isPrivError(e)) {
                    throw e;
                }
                RootShell.Result r = RootShell.duress(this,
                        "SET\n" + textOf(ownerPin) + "\n" + pin + "\n" + pass + "\n");
                if (!r.ok() || !r.out.contains("SET=OK")) {
                    throw new IllegalStateException(rootFail(r, e));
                }
            }
            duressStatus.setText("Duress credentials saved.");
            duressStatus.setTextColor(ACCENT);
            duressPin.setText("");
            duressPin2.setText("");
            duressPass.setText("");
            duressPass2.setText("");
            toast("Duress PIN and password saved");
        } catch (Exception e) {
            duressStatus.setText(friendly(e));
            duressStatus.setTextColor(DANGER);
            toast("Save failed");
        } finally {
            zero(owner);
            zero(dPin);
            zero(dPass);
        }
    }

    private void confirmDeleteDuress() {
        new AlertDialog.Builder(this)
                .setTitle("Delete duress credentials?")
                .setMessage("This only removes the wipe credentials. It does not wipe the phone.")
                .setNegativeButton("Cancel", null)
                .setPositiveButton("Delete", new android.content.DialogInterface.OnClickListener() {
                    @Override public void onClick(android.content.DialogInterface d, int w) {
                        deleteDuress();
                    }
                })
                .show();
    }

    private void deleteDuress() {
        Object owner = null;
        try {
            requireLock();
            owner = ownerCredential();
            try {
                lock.deleteDuress(owner);
            } catch (Exception e) {
                if (!isPrivError(e)) {
                    throw e;
                }
                RootShell.Result r = RootShell.duress(this, "DELETE\n" + textOf(ownerPin) + "\n");
                if (!r.ok() || !r.out.contains("DELETE=OK")) {
                    throw new IllegalStateException(rootFail(r, e));
                }
            }
            duressStatus.setText("Duress credentials deleted.");
            duressStatus.setTextColor(MUTED);
            toast("Duress credentials deleted");
        } catch (Exception e) {
            duressStatus.setText(friendly(e));
            duressStatus.setTextColor(DANGER);
        } finally {
            zero(owner);
        }
    }

    private void requireLock() throws Exception {
        if (lock == null) {
            try {
                lock = new LockBridge(this);
            } catch (Throwable t) {
                throw new IllegalStateException(
                        "Lock APIs blocked. Grant BakaSU Superuser to lenOS security, then retry. "
                                + t.getClass().getSimpleName() + ": " + t.getMessage());
            }
        }
    }

    private void zero(Object cred) {
        if (lock != null) {
            lock.zeroize(cred);
        }
    }

    private Object ownerCredential() throws Exception {
        String pin = textOf(ownerPin);
        if (pin.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Enter your current screen-lock PIN first");
        }
        return lock.createPin(pin);
    }

    private static int bfuValueAt(int pos) {
        int i = 0;
        for (Map.Entry<Integer, String> e : BFU_CHOICES.entrySet()) {
            if (i == pos) {
                return e.getKey();
            }
            i++;
        }
        return BFU_12H_MS;
    }

    private static String friendly(Exception e) {
        String msg = e.getMessage();
        if (msg == null || msg.isEmpty()) {
            msg = e.getClass().getSimpleName();
        }
        if (msg.contains("owner credential")) {
            return "Current PIN is wrong.";
        }
        if (msg.contains("factory reset protection") || msg.contains("FRP")) {
            return "FRP is still active.";
        }
        if (isPrivError(e)) {
            return "Need BakaSU Superuser for \u201clenOS security\u201d, then retry.";
        }
        return msg;
    }

    private static boolean isPrivError(Exception e) {
        String msg = String.valueOf(e.getMessage()) + " " + e.getClass().getName();
        if (msg.contains("owner credential")) {
            return false;
        }
        return msg.contains("ACCESS_KEYGUARD")
                || msg.contains("LockSettingsWrite")
                || msg.contains("Permission Denial")
                || e instanceof SecurityException;
    }

    private static String rootFail(RootShell.Result r, Exception first) {
        if (r.code == 127) {
            return "Root not available. In BakaSU grant Superuser to \u201clenOS security\u201d, then tap again.";
        }
        String detail = r.err.isEmpty() ? r.out : r.err;
        if (detail == null || detail.isEmpty()) {
            detail = first.getMessage();
        }
        return "Root helper failed: " + detail;
    }

    private void toast(String s) {
        Toast.makeText(this, s, Toast.LENGTH_LONG).show();
    }

    private static String sysProp(String key, String fallback) {
        try {
            Class<?> c = Class.forName("android.os.SystemProperties");
            return (String) c.getMethod("get", String.class, String.class).invoke(null, key, fallback);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return fallback;
        }
    }

    private static String textOf(EditText e) {
        return e.getText() == null ? "" : e.getText().toString();
    }

    private static String stack(Throwable t) {
        StringWriter sw = new StringWriter();
        t.printStackTrace(new PrintWriter(sw));
        return sw.toString();
    }

    private LinearLayout card(String heading, View body) {
        LinearLayout card = column();
        card.setPadding(dp(16), dp(16), dp(16), dp(16));
        GradientDrawable bg = new GradientDrawable();
        bg.setColor(CARD);
        bg.setCornerRadius(dp(16));
        bg.setStroke(dp(1), STROKE);
        card.setBackground(bg);
        LinearLayout.LayoutParams lp = new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(
                ViewGroup.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT, ViewGroup.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT);
        lp.topMargin = dp(14);
        card.setLayoutParams(lp);
        card.addView(text(heading, 16, TEXT, true));
        if (body.getParent() == null) {
            card.addView(body);
        }
        return card;
    }

    private LinearLayout column() {
        LinearLayout col = new LinearLayout(this);
        col.setOrientation(LinearLayout.VERTICAL);
        return col;
    }

    private TextView text(String value, int sp, int color, boolean bold) {
        TextView t = new TextView(this);
        t.setText(value);
        t.setTextColor(color);
        t.setTextSize(TypedValue.COMPLEX_UNIT_SP, sp);
        t.setTypeface(Typeface.create("sans-serif", bold ? Typeface.BOLD : Typeface.NORMAL));
        t.setPadding(0, 0, 0, dp(4));
        t.setTextIsSelectable(true);
        return t;
    }

    private EditText passwordField(String hint, boolean numeric) {
        EditText e = new EditText(this);
        e.setHint(hint);
        e.setHintTextColor(MUTED);
        e.setTextColor(TEXT);
        e.setSingleLine(true);
        e.setInputType(numeric
                ? InputType.TYPE_CLASS_NUMBER | InputType.TYPE_NUMBER_VARIATION_PASSWORD
                : InputType.TYPE_CLASS_TEXT | InputType.TYPE_TEXT_VARIATION_PASSWORD);
        e.setPadding(dp(12), dp(12), dp(12), dp(12));
        GradientDrawable bg = new GradientDrawable();
        bg.setColor(Color.parseColor("#0E1116"));
        bg.setCornerRadius(dp(10));
        bg.setStroke(dp(1), STROKE);
        e.setBackground(bg);
        LinearLayout.LayoutParams lp = new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(
                ViewGroup.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT, ViewGroup.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT);
        lp.topMargin = dp(4);
        e.setLayoutParams(lp);
        return e;
    }

    private Button accentButton(String label) {
        return button(label, ACCENT, Color.parseColor("#0B1B33"));
    }

    private Button dangerButton(String label) {
        return button(label, DANGER, Color.parseColor("#2A1210"));
    }

    private Button outlineButton(String label) {
        return button(label, STROKE, Color.TRANSPARENT);
    }

    private Button button(String label, int stroke, int fill) {
        Button b = new Button(this);
        b.setText(label);
        b.setAllCaps(false);
        b.setTextColor(TEXT);
        GradientDrawable bg = new GradientDrawable();
        bg.setColor(fill);
        bg.setCornerRadius(dp(12));
        bg.setStroke(dp(1), stroke);
        b.setBackground(bg);
        LinearLayout.LayoutParams lp = new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(
                ViewGroup.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT, ViewGroup.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT);
        lp.topMargin = dp(4);
        b.setLayoutParams(lp);
        return b;
    }

    private View errorScreen(String msg) {
        TextView t = text(msg, 13, DANGER, false);
        t.setPadding(dp(24), dp(48), dp(24), dp(24));
        t.setBackgroundColor(BG);
        t.setGravity(Gravity.START);
        ScrollView sc = new ScrollView(this);
        sc.setBackgroundColor(BG);
        sc.addView(t);
        return sc;
    }

    private int dp(int v) {
        return Math.round(v * getResources().getDisplayMetrics().density);
    }
}

package org.lenos.security;

import android.content.Context;

import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.io.OutputStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;

/**
 * Best-effort BakaSU / KernelSU / Magisk su. Secrets go on stdin only,
 * never on argv (argv is visible to other processes via /proc).
 */
final class RootShell {
    private static final String[] SU = {
            "su",
            "/debug_ramdisk/su",
            "/system/xbin/su",
            "/system/bin/su",
            "/data/adb/ksu/bin/ksu"
    };

    static final class Result {
        final int code;
        final String out;
        final String err;

        Result(int code, String out, String err) {
            this.code = code;
            this.out = out;
            this.err = err;
        }

        boolean ok() {
            return code == 0;
        }
    }

    static Result run(String shellCommand) {
        return run(shellCommand, null);
    }

    static Result run(String shellCommand, String stdin) {
        Exception last = null;
        for (String su : SU) {
            try {
                Process p = new ProcessBuilder(su, "-c", shellCommand)
                        .redirectErrorStream(false)
                        .start();
                if (stdin != null) {
                    OutputStream os = p.getOutputStream();
                    os.write(stdin.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
                    os.flush();
                    os.close();
                } else {
                    p.getOutputStream().close();
                }
                String out = readAll(p.getInputStream());
                String err = readAll(p.getErrorStream());
                int code = p.waitFor();
                return new Result(code, out, err);
            } catch (Exception e) {
                last = e;
            }
        }
        return new Result(127, "", last == null ? "su not found" : last.getMessage());
    }

    /** Run DuressCli via app_process so the Binder call originates from uid 0. */
    static Result duress(Context ctx, String stdin) {
        String apk = ctx.getPackageCodePath().replace("'", "'\\''");
        String cmd = "CLASSPATH='" + apk + "' app_process /system/bin org.lenos.security.DuressCli";
        return run(cmd, stdin);
    }

    static Result settingsPutGlobal(String key, String value) {
        return run("settings put global " + key + " " + value);
    }

    static Result settingsPutSecure(String key, String value) {
        return run("settings put secure " + key + " " + value);
    }

    private static String readAll(InputStream in) {
        try {
            ByteArrayOutputStream bos = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
            byte[] buf = new byte[4096];
            int n;
            while ((n = in.read(buf)) >= 0) {
                bos.write(buf, 0, n);
            }
            return bos.toString("UTF-8").trim();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return "";
        }
    }
}

# lenOS experimental product fragment.
#
# Inherited from config/lenos.mk only when LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL is 1/true/yes.
# The build helper sets that flag for both patch application and the build, and
# installs experimental/app/ into $SRC/vendor/lenos/app/ only in this mode.
# A default 1.0 build neither includes this fragment nor has the app source.
#
# Everything here is source-complete but not build- or device-validated. See
# experimental/STATUS.md and experimental/docs/verification.md before using it.

PRODUCT_PACKAGES += \
    LenosOpsec

# Makes an experimental image identifiable at runtime. This is not a security
# boundary and must not be treated as one.
PRODUCT_PRODUCT_PROPERTIES += \
    ro.lenos.experimental=1

# HTS-1: hardened thread-stack layout in bionic. The property belongs to the
# experimental series, so it is present only when this fragment is inherited
# (LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1). The stable/default build keeps the stock thread
# mapping. See experimental/docs/verification.md before relying on it.
PRODUCT_PRODUCT_PROPERTIES += \
    ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks=1

# lenOS product configuration.
#
# Inherited from device/nothing/asteroids/lenos_asteroids.mk (see
# patches/device_nothing_asteroids/0001-add-lenos-product.patch).
#
# Branding is ro.lenos.* only. ro.build.*, the build fingerprint and the
# device identity stay stock on purpose: changing them breaks app
# compatibility, attestation and Nothing factory tooling.

# lenOS companion app ("lenOS security"). Everything else in the UI is stock
# LineageOS Settings; this app only hosts controls that Settings does not have.
PRODUCT_PACKAGES += \
    LenosSecurity

# Experimental features are opt-in at build time. The driver only applies the
# patches-experimental/ series and installs experimental/app/ when
# LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1; a normal 1.0 build never inherits this fragment.
ifneq ($(filter 1 true yes,$(LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL)),)
$(call inherit-product, vendor/lenos/config/lenos-experimental.mk)
endif

# Privacy overlays (enabled at boot, no user interaction required):
# * LenosFrameworksOverlay        - non-Google NTP fallback pool (framework-res)
# * LenosNetworkStackOverlay      - Cloudflare connectivity-check probes
# * LenosSettingsProviderOverlay  - hardened first-boot (Settings.Global) defaults
PRODUCT_PACKAGES += \
    LenosFrameworksOverlay \
    LenosNetworkStackOverlay \
    LenosSettingsProviderOverlay

# GrapheneOS parity: pre-installed APEXes stay uncompressed. The AOSP product
# fragment updatable_apex.mk (pulled in by full_base_telephony.mk inside
# lineage_asteroids.mk) sets PRODUCT_COMPRESSED_APEX := true; this file is
# inherited after it, so the assignment below wins. The cost is a few MiB on
# the system partition; the gain is that boot no longer has to decompress APEX
# payloads before mounting them, which removes a decompression/parsing surface
# from early boot.
PRODUCT_COMPRESSED_APEX := false

# Privileged permission allowlist for LenosSecurity. The APK is signed with
# the platform key, so most permissions are already satisfied by the signature;
# the allowlist keeps the app working (and documents the intent) if it is ever
# built without the platform certificate.
PRODUCT_COPY_FILES += \
    vendor/lenos/config/privapp-permissions-org.lenos.security.xml:$(TARGET_COPY_OUT_SYSTEM)/etc/permissions/privapp-permissions-org.lenos.security.xml

# Product properties are loaded last by init, so they override values from
# system/system_ext/vendor/odm (see system/core/init/property_service.cpp).
# Keep this list short and commented; anything user-visible belongs in the
# SettingsProvider defaults or a documented toggle instead.
PRODUCT_PRODUCT_PROPERTIES += \
    ro.lenos.version=1.0.0 \
    ro.lenos.base=lineage-24.0 \
    ro.lenos.dns=dns.quad9.net \
    # Auto-reboot-to-BFU backend: init timer (system/core/0001), armed from
    # the keyguard showing-state in frameworks/base (0003). The timeout lives
    # in Settings.Global."settings_reboot_after_timeout" (18h default via
    # android.ext.settings, frameworks/base/0006). Status string for the
    # lenOS security app.
    ro.lenos.security.auto_bfu=init \
    # Duress credential backend: LockSettingsService (frameworks/base/0005)
    # with the lenOS security app as UI. Destructive by design; entering a
    # duress credential at any prompt destroys the storage keys. Status string
    # for the app.
    ro.lenos.security.duress=framework \
    persist.traced.enable=0 \
    persist.logd.size.radio=64K \
    persist.vendor.verbose_logging_enabled=0 \
    persist.vendor.radio.adb_log_on=0 \
    persist.vendor.radio.ims_log_enabled=0 \
    persist.vendor.sys.modem.logging.enable=0 \
    persist.vendor.radio.snapshot_enabled=0 \
    persist.vendor.radio.snapshot_timer=0

# Building lenOS

lenOS is a patch set, not a full source tree. You supply a LineageOS 24.0 tree,
the normal Android build environment, and your own signing keys.

The series was developed against the `6.6/lineage-24.0` device trees in the
[NullDebris manifest](https://github.com/NullDebris/manifest). It is not a
general-purpose patch set for every LineageOS revision: `--check` will stop if
the surrounding source has drifted.

## 1. Get a compatible tree

Follow the normal LineageOS build setup for your host, using the
`lineage-24.0` branch. Add the device manifest before the first sync:

```bash
repo init -u https://github.com/LineageOS/android.git -b lineage-24.0
mkdir -p .repo/local_manifests
curl -fsSL -o .repo/local_manifests/asteroids.xml \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NullDebris/manifest/main/asteroids-6.6-lineage-24.0.xml
repo sync -c -j"$(nproc --all)"
```

The manifest tracks `kernel/nothing/sm7635-devicetrees` at `6.6/lineage-23.2`
and `ParanoidGlyph`/`GlyphAdapter` at `lineage-23.1`/`15`. Those are the newest
upstream branches available for those projects; they are kernel/device sources
and standalone apps, not Android framework code, so they do not need a 24.0
branch. Leave the manifest pins as-is unless NullDebris publishes newer ones.

This initial sync is expected. Do **not** run `repo sync` again after applying
the patches; reset the tree first if you need to move it.

## 2. Apply the patch series

Clone the patchkit into `vendor/lenos` and apply the default series:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ntrop6/lenos-patches.git vendor/lenos
python3 vendor/lenos/tools/lenos-patch.py --tree . --check
python3 vendor/lenos/tools/lenos-patch.py --tree . --apply
```

`--check` is read-only. `--apply` writes the patches with strict `git apply`;
a patch that does not match is a hard error, not a warning. Do not edit the
tree by hand and do not apply the patches with plain `git apply`.

To undo the series:

```bash
python3 vendor/lenos/tools/lenos-patch.py --tree . --reset
```

`--reset` restores tracked files and deletes files the series created. It will
discard local edits in the patched projects, so commit or save your work first.

## 3. Build

```bash
source build/envsetup.sh
lunch lenos_asteroids-user
mka bacon
```

The build uses the signing and OTA setup configured in your tree. No signing
keys are stored in this repository. If you use custom AVB keys or the
rootless/avbroot packaging flow, use the same procedure you use for any other
LineageOS build.

## Experimental series

The experimental work is a second series applied only after the default one.
It is not part of a normal build. Read
[`experimental.md`](experimental.md) for the full apply/reset contract.

Manual apply:

```bash
python3 vendor/lenos/tools/lenos-patch.py --tree . --experimental --check
python3 vendor/lenos/tools/lenos-patch.py --tree . --experimental --apply
```

The experimental product fragment adds `LenosOpsec`, but its source lives
outside the normal app directory. Copy it in before building:

```bash
cp -a vendor/lenos/experimental/app/LenosOpsec vendor/lenos/app/
LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1 mka bacon
```

To switch back, remove the copied app and reset the experimental series before
resetting the default series:

```bash
rm -rf vendor/lenos/app/LenosOpsec
python3 vendor/lenos/tools/lenos-patch.py --tree . --experimental --reset
python3 vendor/lenos/tools/lenos-patch.py --tree . --reset
```

If the patchkit is not inside the build tree, copy `config/`, `app/`, `rro/`,
and `release/` into `$SRC/vendor/lenos/` before building. For an experimental
build also copy `experimental/app/LenosOpsec` into
`$SRC/vendor/lenos/app/`.

## Optional helper

`lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh` is a wrapper used for one local build/signing setup. It
is not needed to build lenOS and it has extra dependencies (the LineageOS
signing wizard, avbroot 3.33.0+ for packaging, and a key directory). `package`
verifies the input OTA against your `ota.crt`/`avb_pkmd.bin`, and both the
rootless and root paths verify the final `init_boot` ramdisk and OTA/AVB chain.
If you use it, keep the patchkit outside the build tree:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ntrop6/lenos-patches.git ~/lenos-patches
LENOS_SOURCE=$HOME/lineage ~/lenos-patches/lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh doctor
LENOS_SOURCE=$HOME/lineage ~/lenos-patches/lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh apply
LENOS_SOURCE=$HOME/lineage ~/lenos-patches/lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh build
```

The wrapper replaces `$LENOS_SOURCE/vendor/lenos` with its build inputs during
`apply`, so do not run it from a checkout that lives inside the build tree.
Use the manual path above in that case.

## Root (optional)

The default output is rootless. An opt-in root OTA is produced after the normal
rootless build, from the exact signed base OTA:

```bash
LENOS_SOURCE=$HOME/lineage LENOS_ROOT=bakasu \
  ~/lenos-patches/lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh root-prepare
LENOS_SOURCE=$HOME/lineage LENOS_ROOT=bakasu \
  ~/lenos-patches/lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh package
```

Use `LENOS_ROOT=kernelsu` for the fallback. `root-prepare` needs avbroot 3.33.0
or newer, network access for the pinned assets, and the `asteroids` device tree.
It verifies the base OTA against your configured OTA/AVB keys, does not modify
the source tree, and does not include a root manager in the system image.
Packaging re-signs `init_boot` and the OS AVB partitions, then verifies the final
OTA and its init_boot ramdisk.

Read [`root.md`](root.md) before using it. Root has not been boot-tested, and
locking is still not supported.

## Tests

From the patchkit checkout, the tests expect a pristine tree and do not build
Android:

```bash
LENOS_WORKSPACE=/path/to/lineage bash tests/run-tests.sh
```

`LENOS_PYTHON` can point at a Python with tree-sitter installed; Java syntax
checks are skipped when tree-sitter is unavailable, never silently passed as a
different check.

## After a build

Read-only helpers:

```bash
OUT=/path/to/out/target/product/asteroids tools/verify-build.sh
ANDROID_SERIAL=... tools/verify-device.sh
```

The device checklist, including the items that cannot be checked without a
cable or a reboot, is in
[`experimental/docs/verification.md`](../experimental/docs/verification.md).
Flashing and locking rules are in
[`flash-and-lock.md`](flash-and-lock.md).

# Experimental builds (opt-in)

Experimental work lives in this repository but is **not** part of the default
1.0 build. It is selected at build time with `LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1`.

If you use the optional helper, the two modes are:

```bash
# default 1.0
./lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh apply
./lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh build

# experimental image
LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1 ./lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh apply
LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1 ./lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh build
```

For the manual path, see [Apply-order contract](#apply-order-contract) below.
The driver normalizes the flag to `0` or `1` and exports it to the build.
`config/lenos.mk` inherits `config/lenos-experimental.mk` only when the value
is `1`, `true` or `yes`. If you apply patches manually and then run `mka`, pass
the same variable yourself:

```bash
LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1 mka bacon
```

Without it, `LenosOpsec` is not in `PRODUCT_PACKAGES` and the experimental app
source is not installed into `$WS/vendor/lenos/app/`. For a manual build, copy
it there yourself after applying the series:

```bash
cp -a experimental/app/LenosOpsec "$WS/vendor/lenos/app/"
```

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `patches-experimental/<alias>/series` | Upstream-project patches applied **after** `patches/` |
| `experimental/app/LenosOpsec/` | OPSEC app source, installed only for an experimental build |
| `config/lenos-experimental.mk` | Experimental product fragment (`LenosOpsec`, `ro.lenos.experimental=1`, `ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks=1`) |
| `experimental/docs/` | OPSEC threat model, provenance, security review, device checklist |
| `experimental/tests/` | Source-level tests for the experimental series and app |
| `tools/verify-build.sh` | Read-only post-build artifact check |
| `tools/verify-device.sh` | Read-only adb property/setting/package check |

There is no `patches-experimental/vendor_lenos/` patch. The former
`vendor_lenos/0001-opsec-tools.patch` is now the gated source tree above, so
the patchkit never edits its own checkout.

## Apply-order contract

The experimental series is a **second series on top of the stable tree**, not
an alternative fork:

```bash
PY=python3
WS=/path/to/lineage

$PY tools/lenos-patch.py --tree "$WS" --check
$PY tools/lenos-patch.py --tree "$WS" --apply

$PY tools/lenos-patch.py --tree "$WS" --experimental --check
$PY tools/lenos-patch.py --tree "$WS" --experimental --apply

$PY tools/lenos-patch.py --tree "$WS" --require-applied
$PY tools/lenos-patch.py --tree "$WS" --experimental --require-applied
```

`--experimental --check` must be run after the stable series is applied. Each
experimental patch still has to apply with strict `git apply`, and the test
suite rebuilds the stable base in a sandbox before applying every experimental
patch independently and in series order.

`--require-applied` reverse-replays the whole series in reverse order in a
throwaway copy of every touched file. This is the authoritative check: a single
reverse check can report an earlier patch as `missing` when a later patch in
the same file changes its context. `--status` remains a per-patch display;
`--require-applied` is what the driver uses before it builds. Validate the
stable series **before** applying the experimental overlays.

## Reset / switching back

The driver detects an applied experimental series before resetting stable
projects, runs `--experimental --reset` first, then resets the stable series.
That removes experimental source files (including renames) before returning to
a stable build. To do it manually:

```bash
$PY tools/lenos-patch.py --tree "$WS" --experimental --reset
$PY tools/lenos-patch.py --tree "$WS" --reset
```

Never leave a partially applied series in the tree.

## Safety

Experimental means **source-complete, not validated**:

* no full `asteroids` build has been run for this combined series;
* no image has been flashed, wiped, relocked or booted;
* untested items include the USB HAL `enableUsbData` path, fs-verity updates,
  Seedvault restore migration, ENF-1 ptrace behavior, Setup Wizard verified-boot
  states, HTS-1 thread-stack behavior/compatibility, and every OPSEC UI flow.

The no-flash/no-wipe/no-relock rules in
[`flash-and-lock.md`](flash-and-lock.md) still apply. An experimental build
must not be flashed without explicit approval and a recovery plan.

## Hardened thread stacks (HTS-1, experimental only)

`bionic/0001-hardened-thread-stacks.patch` is a source port of the GrapheneOS
pthread stack-layout changes. It is part of the experimental series: a normal
`LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1` build applies the patch and
`config/lenos-experimental.mk` adds `ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks=1`. The
stable/default build has no property and keeps the pinned AOSP mapping.

Bionic reads the property for each new `pthread_create` and accepts only the
exact value `1`. When the property is absent, the pinned AOSP mapping is used
unchanged. `verify-build.sh` reports the property and `verify-device.sh` prints
it on a booted device.

When enabled, a new thread mapping is laid out as:

```
[ stack guard ][ stack ][ random PROT_NONE gap ][ pthread_internal_t ][ static TLS ][ libgen ][ guard ]
```

The gap is at least one page and up to 50% of the stack on 64-bit (10% on
32-bit); the stack top is randomized within the old `pthread_internal_t` slot.
The main thread is intentionally unchanged because
`__libc_init_main_thread.cpp` calls the old allocator directly.

This is not `hardened_malloc`, MTE/TBI, BTI/PAC, exec spawning, JIT policy or a
sandbox. It only makes a stack overflow less likely to overwrite
`pthread_internal_t` and TLS. It has not been built or booted, and the extra
virtual address space and app/ART compatibility are unmeasured. See
[`../experimental/docs/verification.md`](../experimental/docs/verification.md)
for the required boot and thread-stress checks, and
[`../experimental/STATUS.md`](../experimental/STATUS.md) for the limits.

## Verification

```bash
# source-level tests (main suite, no build)
LENOS_WORKSPACE="$WS" LENOS_PYTHON=$PY bash tests/run-tests.sh

# experimental feature tests (stable base is built inside each sandbox)
cd experimental/tests
LENOS_WORKSPACE="$WS" LENOS_PYTHON=$PY ./run-tests.sh

# after a real build, read-only artifact check
OUT=/path/to/out/target/product/asteroids tools/verify-build.sh

# after an approved flash, read-only device check
ANDROID_SERIAL=... tools/verify-device.sh
```

The device checklist and honest limitations remain in
[`experimental/docs/verification.md`](../experimental/docs/verification.md),
[`experimental/STATUS.md`](../experimental/STATUS.md) and
[`experimental/docs/security-review.md`](../experimental/docs/security-review.md).

# Features

A working list of what the default series changes, with the limits that matter.
Base: LineageOS 24.0 (`asteroids` = Nothing Phone (3a) / (3a) Pro).

All features below are **source-complete**: patches, resources and tests are in
this repository. None of it has been verified on a running device yet. Until a
build has been checked on hardware, treat every feature as bring-up.

## First-boot defaults (Settings.Global)

Seeded once by `frameworks/base/0002-lenos-first-boot-defaults.patch` from
resources that `rro/LenosSettingsProviderOverlay` hardens (stock values stay
AOSP-compatible in the upstream source). Every value stays a normal user
setting afterwards; lenOS never rewrites a user change. Wi-Fi privacy
defaults are not seeded here — they are GrapheneOS-faithful per-network
defaults in `packages_modules_Wifi/0001` (see Network).

| Setting | Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `private_dns_mode` | `hostname` | strict DNS-over-TLS |
| `private_dns_specifier` | `dns.quad9.net` | Quad9 DoT |
| `NTP_SERVER` | `pool.ntp.org` | no Google time service (framework fallback lives in `rro/LenosFrameworksOverlay`) |
| `captive_portal_mode` | `1` | prompt — never silently logged-in to portals |

Other first-boot hardening from the same overlay: Bluetooth off, no Wi-Fi
wakeup scanning, no "open networks available" notifications, location off,
USB mass storage off, no lock-screen QR scanner shortcut.

One Secure default is seeded through the stock resource instead
(`frameworks/base/0012`, GrapheneOS-faithful): the
`def_lock_screen_allow_private_notifications` default flips to `false`, so
new installs and new users start with `Settings.Secure
lock_screen_allow_private_notifications=0` — lock-screen notifications hide
their content until the user explicitly allows it.

## Identity / correlation

| Feature | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SSAID (Android ID) rotates on reinstall | `frameworks/base/0001` | same app reinstall gets a new ID; setting `Settings.Secure`/user-visible to disable; units tested |
| Generic device name by default | `device_nothing_asteroids/0006` | "Android" instead of "Nothing Phone (3a)" — the device name is the Bluetooth adapter / Wi-Fi Direct name neighbours see; user can rename |
| Generic tether SSID | `device_nothing_asteroids/0002` | `AndroidAP`, no model name |
| Build fingerprint / product identity | *untouched by design* | keeps app compatibility, attestation, Nothing factory tooling |

## Users and profiles

| Feature | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Up to 32 users/profiles | `device_nothing_asteroids/0007` | GrapheneOS parity: `config_multiuserMaximumUsers` raised 4 → 32 in the vendor overlay (the framework raw default is 1; the overlay is what ships). Each profile is its own encryption domain, so more profiles support stronger per-identity separation; the limit is a ceiling, not a default |
| Per-user app installation policy | `packages_apps_Settings/0003` (GrapheneOS port) | the owner can set, per user, whether that user may install and update apps: **enabled**, **first-party sources only** (unknown sources blocked), or **disabled** — GrapheneOS's `UserAppsInstallSettings` screen behind a new "App installs and updates" row in user details. It uses the standard `DISALLOW_INSTALL_APPS` / `DISALLOW_INSTALL_UNKNOWN_SOURCES` restrictions, which A17's framework already enforces in `PackageInstallerService`/`InstallPackageHelper`; the guest's choice is written to the guest-default bundle. No framework change; the helper's private-space inheritance half (a separate GrapheneOS feature) is not ported |

## Network

| Feature | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Network (INTERNET) permission | `frameworks_base/0025` + `packages_modules_Connectivity/0002` + `packages_modules_Permission/0002` (GrapheneOS port) | `android.permission.INTERNET` becomes a real runtime permission (GrapheneOS "special runtime permissions"), presented as the "Network" group in app info with an on/off toggle and granted automatically on install — an app *update* never re-grants a revoked one. Revoking gives the app no network: sockets are blocked at the kernel level (netd per-UID BPF map, AOSP machinery already shipped and unconditional on Android 17) *and* the app is put into "internet compat" mode — the OS pretends there is no network (32 `ConnectivityManager` APIs answer none/empty, NSD gets a stubbed connector, `DownloadManager` returns nothing) while the app's own INTERNET self-checks are spoofed as granted, so legacy apps degrade to "offline" instead of crashing. System apps never get compat mode (GrapheneOS behavior: real enforcement only). Auto-revoke/hibernation never touches this permission |
| Wi-Fi MAC randomization (per connection) | `packages_modules_Wifi/0001` (GrapheneOS port) | new networks default to `RANDOMIZATION_ALWAYS` (per-connection, non-persistent MACs); a per-network strategy the user picks explicitly still wins |
| Strict Private DNS (DoT, Quad9) | first-boot default | breaks networks that block DoT or need captive-portal DNS; user-changeable |
| NTP without Google | first-boot default + frameworks RRO | `pool.ntp.org` is a central pool; SNTP is unauthenticated either way |
| Connectivity checks without Google | `rro/LenosNetworkStackOverlay` | `cp.cloudflare.com/generate_204`; the check still uses a third party (Cloudflare), it is just not Google (see limits) |
| DHCP hostname blocked by default | `packages_modules_Wifi/0001` (GrapheneOS port) | new networks never send the hostname (XML tag renamed `SendDhcpHostname` → `SendDhcpHostname2`, so values written by stock Android are ignored after upgrade); per-network opt-in in the Wi-Fi network details — no global override |
| DHCP lease not reused under per-connection MAC randomization | `packages_modules_NetworkStack/0001` (GrapheneOS port) | when a network uses per-connection randomized MACs (the default), the DHCP client starts from DISCOVER instead of renewing the lease it cached for that network, so the DHCP server cannot link two connections as the same device (GrapheneOS `62d70edb46`, still shipped on their branch 17). The check asks Wi-Fi for the connected network's randomization mode and conservatively avoids reuse if that lookup fails; the other randomization modes keep the upstream fast-renewal path |
| VPN lockdown DNS leak fixed | `system_netd/0001` (GrapheneOS port) | the system resolver no longer marks every query as VPN-protected; with all VPNs down under "Block connections without VPN", DNS falls into the blocked path instead of the default network's resolvers (GrapheneOS `82da9204`) |
| VPN multicast firewall | `system_netd/0001` (GrapheneOS port) | drops multicast, IGMP and MLD in/out/through `tun+` interfaces, closing the cross-profile VPN side channel; inbound router advertisements stay allowed (GrapheneOS `dcef5ccb` + `d57ea8dc`) |
| NSD blocked under VPN lockdown | `packages_modules_Connectivity/0001` + `frameworks_base/0017` (GrapheneOS port) | regular apps get no NSD connector while an always-on VPN with lockdown is active, so mDNS discovery can't bypass the tunnel; system apps keep access (`android.ext.ConnectivityUtil`) |
| Always-on VPN survives temporary app loss | `frameworks_base/0018` (GrapheneOS port) | an unsupported (disabled/safe-mode) always-on VPN package no longer clears the setting, so the lockdown fail-safe stays configured and the VPN restarts when the package returns |
| Insecure enterprise Wi-Fi configs blocked | `device_nothing_asteroids/0002` | Settings/SetupWizard cannot configure "no certificate validation" enterprise networks |
| Distrusted root CAs removed | `system_ca-certificates/0001` | Chunghwa Telecom (HiPKI Root CA - G1, ePKI Root CA) and NetLock Arany (Class Gold) roots are deleted from the system trust store, matching GrapheneOS commit `14ad6bb` and Google's 2025 root-store distrust; user-installed CAs and app-pinned trust are unaffected (see limits) |
| Wireless alerts optional | `packages_apps_CellBroadcastReceiver/0001` (GrapheneOS port) | presidential alerts and (in Brazil) extreme alerts become user-toggleable: the presidential preference is visible, runs the config service and is read by the alert path (GrapheneOS commits "allow toggling presidential alerts" + "always allow disabling extreme alerts"). Every alert type stays enabled by default — nothing is silently forced on or off |
| Default radio mode without 2G | `device_nothing_asteroids/0004` | `ro.telephony.default_network=28,28` (NR+LTE+WCDMA); no GSM/2G fallback, user can change |
| LTE-only / 5G-only network mode | `packages_apps_Settings/0001` (GrapheneOS port) | the preferred-network-type list gains "LTE only" (always) and "5G or LTE only" / "5G only" (when the carrier and baseband expose NR; "5G only" also requires NR standalone). Picking one strips 2G/3G (or LTE) from the modem's allowed RATs, shrinking the baseband attack surface. Ports GrapheneOS `5310142ccc` + `8d37b32db6`; the carrier-hidden-settings guard is kept (see deviations) |
| SUPL / PSDS network assistance off | `frameworks_base/0021` + `packages_apps_Settings/0001` (GrapheneOS port) | SUPL (A-GNSS) and PSDS (predicted satellite data) default to **off**, so the device does not send its IP address and cell-derived location to an assistance server. Settings → Location → Network assistance offers "Off"/"Standard server" for each. The old device-level `gps.supl_host` blanking (`device/0003`) was removed so "Standard server" actually works; GrapheneOS's own proxies are not offered (no proxy infrastructure) |
| Modem/radio logging and snapshot props off | `config/lenos.mk` | `persist.vendor.radio.*` logging off, small radio log buffer, `persist.traced.enable=0` |

| Feature | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Auto reboot to before-first-unlock (BFU) | `system_core/0001` + `frameworks_base/0003` + `frameworks_base/0006` | GrapheneOS port: init owns a `CLOCK_BOOTTIME_ALARM` timer driven through the `sys.auto_reboot_ctl` property; system_server forwards keyguard showing-state changes (timeout while locked, `on_device_unlocked` on unlock). Requests before the first unlock are ignored, a running timer is not restarted by relocking, and expiry performs a normal reboot, so the FBE keys stay out of memory until the next unlock. `Settings.Global.settings_reboot_after_timeout` (GrapheneOS key, 18h default via `android.ext.settings`, 0 = off, 10min–3 days) with UI in the lenOS app |
| Quick settings require unlock | `frameworks_base/0004` | GrapheneOS port: every tile action (click, secondary click, long click) goes through `QSTileImpl#handleAction`. While a secure keyguard is up, non-allow-listed tiles do nothing until the user authenticates — the keyguard bouncer is shown and the action runs only after a successful unlock. A locked device cannot toggle radios/connectivity (e.g. airplane mode to break remote tracking). Allow-list as in GrapheneOS: flashlight (both variants), QR scanner, color inversion/correction, Night Light, reduce bright colors, dark theme, rotation lock, battery saver, device controls |
| PIN keypad scrambling | `frameworks_base/0008` + `packages_apps_Settings/0001` (+ default in `0006`) | GrapheneOS port: the keypad is shuffled with `SecureRandom` on every setup and hardware keys route through the digit→view map; the keyguard reads `ExtSettings.SCRAMBLE_LOCKSCREEN_PIN_LAYOUT_PRIMARY`, SIM PIN/PUK views read the inheriting `SCRAMBLE_SIM_PIN_LAYOUT`. lenOS deviation: default **on** (GrapheneOS ships it off; commented in `frameworks_base/0006`). UI: lock-screen picker switch + SIM-lock switch; the lenOS app toggles the same `Settings.Secure` key |
| Duress PIN/password | `frameworks_base/0005` + `0007`, `frameworks_opt_telephony/0001` + app UI | entering either duress credential at any credential prompt (lock screen, Settings confirm, shell) destroys the KeyMint storage keys + Secretkeeper secrets — the user data becomes cryptographically inaccessible — erases every eSIM profile and powers off. The eUICC reset runs on a side thread with a three second budget, requires system uid and skips the carrier eSIM-removal notification. Only failed verifications are checked and only typed PIN/password credentials, so the real lock credential can never trigger it. Setting/checking/deleting requires the owner credential; the stored form is a scrypt-stretched hash, never the credential |
| Credential limits (GrapheneOS values) | `frameworks_base/0009` | the fingerprint sensor locks out permanently after 5 failed attempts (AOSP 20; the 30 s timed lockout is unchanged) and the maximum supported password length is 128 characters (AOSP 64) |
| Lock-screen notification content hidden | `frameworks_base/0012` | GrapheneOS default: content stays hidden on the lock screen until the user allows private notifications (see first-boot defaults) |
| FBE filename padding | `system_extras/0001` (GrapheneOS port) | every encryption policy created by this build pads filenames to 32 bytes instead of AOSP's 16 (GrapheneOS commit "pad filenames to 32 bytes instead of 16 or 4 bytes"), hiding filename lengths better. SystemUI runs it in `handleShowInner`; system_server runs it on the transition-gated `setLockScreenShown` binder thread right after the lock transition and outside the global lock |

The action stays available from the power menu, where the lock-screen restrictions apply. GrapheneOS's A17 DevicePolicyManager logout split (`isPolicyManagerLogoutEnabled`) is an A17-only refactor and is not ported |

Defaults are `core/res/res/values/config_ext.xml` resources and `Settings.Global`/`Settings.Secure` keys with GrapheneOS-identical literals, so later ports can drop in without redefining storage. Entries whose enforcement code is not ported yet are inert (no UI is surfaced for them); PIN scramble, the clipboard defaults, the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth auto-off timers and the sensors auto-grant are enforced — see the lock, clipboard and framework sections |

Revoking it makes `SensorService` deny app UIDs: apps get no events at all (continuously reporting sensors report nothing), system processes (e.g. the closed-source `gpsd` daemon) and sensors with their own permission (body sensors, activity recognition) are unaffected. The first blocked access posts a rate-limited "… tried to access sensors" notification that taps through to the grant dialog; "Don't show again" marks the app as user-set and silences it. The permission shows up in app info as its own "Sensors" group |

GrapheneOS's `SystemServerExt` is trimmed to the auto-off wiring; GrapheneOS shows these on its Exploit protection screen with a radio-button sub-screen — lenOS uses plain list rows (documented substitution).
