====================================================================================================
package org.lenos.opsec;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.content.ClipData;
import android.content.ClipboardManager;
import android.content.Intent;
import android.os.Bundle;
import android.widget.Button;
import android.widget.EditText;
import android.widget.TextView;
import android.widget.Toast;

/** Share target that strips known tracking parameters from links in shared text. */
public class ScrubTextActivity extends Activity {
    private EditText mText;
    private TextView mStatus;
    private Button mRemove;
    private Button mShare;
    private Button mCopy;

    @Override
    protected void onCreate(Bundle savedInstanceState) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState);
        setContentView(R.layout.activity_scrub_text);
        mText = findViewById(R.id.text);
        mStatus = findViewById(R.id.status);
        mRemove = findViewById(R.id.remove);
        mShare = findViewById(R.id.share);
        mCopy = findViewById(R.id.copy);

        final Intent intent = getIntent();
        CharSequence shared = intent == null ? null : intent.getCharSequenceExtra(Intent.EXTRA_TEXT);
        if (shared == null && intent != null) {
            shared = intent.getStringExtra(Intent.EXTRA_TEXT);
        }
        final String text = shared == null ? "" : shared.toString();

        findViewById(R.id.cancel).setOnClickListener(v -> finish());
        mRemove.setOnClickListener(v -> applyScrub(false));
        mShare.setOnClickListener(v -> applyScrub(true));
        mCopy.setOnClickListener(v -> copyCleaned());

        if (text.isEmpty()) {
            mStatus.setText(R.string.scrub_text_nothing);
            setButtonsEnabled(false);
        } else {
            mText.setText(text);
            mText.setSelection(0);
            setButtonsEnabled(true);
        }
    }

    private void applyScrub(boolean share) {
        final LinkScrubber.Result result = LinkScrubber.scrub(mText.getText().toString());
        mText.setText(result.text);
        mText.setSelection(0);
        if (result.removed == 0) {
            mStatus.setText(R.string.scrub_text_clean);
        } else {
            mStatus.setText(getString(R.string.scrub_text_removed, result.removed));
        }
        if (share) {
            share(result.text);
        }
    }

    private void copyCleaned() {
        final LinkScrubber.Result result = LinkScrubber.scrub(mText.getText().toString());
        mText.setText(result.text);
        final ClipboardManager clipboard = getSystemService(ClipboardManager.class);
        if (clipboard != null) {
            clipboard.setPrimaryClip(ClipData.newPlainText(
                    getString(R.string.scrub_text_clip_label), result.text));
            Toast.makeText(this, R.string.scrub_text_copied, Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show();
        }
    }

    private void share(String text) {
        final Intent share = new Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND);
        share.setType("text/plain");
        share.putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_TEXT, text);
        startActivity(Intent.createChooser(share, getString(R.string.scrub_text_title)));
    }

    private void setButtonsEnabled(boolean enabled) {
        mRemove.setEnabled(enabled);
        mShare.setEnabled(enabled);
        mCopy.setEnabled(enabled);
    }
}

====================================================================================================
# lenOS OPSEC additions

These are lenOS-original controls, not GrapheneOS ports. GrapheneOS is a security-hardened
Android; its defaults assume an adversary with physical access, but it does not ship a metadata
sanitizer, a one-tap radio kill switch, or a screen-off clipboard wipe. lenOS adds these as
separate, opt-in tools so they can be evaluated without changing the 1.0 series.

The design rule is the same as the rest of lenOS: local-only, fail closed, no new trust anchors,
and no silent weakening of verified boot, encryption, SELinux or emergency calling.

## OPS-1 — metadata-scrubbing share target

**Problem.** Sharing a photo or screenshot can leak GPS coordinates, capture time, device model,
software version, thumbnail images, XMP history and original file names. Android's share sheet
hands the receiving app the original bytes unless the sending app sanitizes first.

**Implementation.** `LenosOpsec` registers a share target for `image/*` and `image/*` with
`ACTION_SEND` / `ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE`. It decodes the image with `ImageDecoder`, re-encodes the
pixels with `Bitmap.compress` into a new cache file with a random UUID name, and shares only that
file through a non-exported `FileProvider` with a one-shot read grant. Re-encoding drops EXIF,
GPS, XMP, ICC and file-name metadata; the output name is unrelated to the source. A copy can also
be saved to `Pictures/lenOS` through MediaStore.

**Limits.**

* Re-encoding is not a cryptographic sanitizer. The source app, MediaStore thumbnails, caches and
  the original file may still contain the metadata. The user must delete the source separately.
* JPEG/WebP quality is recompressed (quality 95). A 4096 px longest-edge cap prevents pathological
  memory use; larger images are downsampled.
* Animated GIF is rejected. HEIF/AVIF is decoded and written as JPEG. PDF and video metadata are
  not handled by this tool.
* The app has no `INTERNET` permission and no network code. It cannot phone home, and it does not
  use a cloud OCR/classification service.

**Verification.** Share a geotagged JPEG; run `exiftool` on the received file and confirm there is
no GPS/EXIF/XMP, that the file name is randomized, and that the image still opens. Repeat with a
multi-select share and with the “save sanitized copy” path.

## OPS-2 — one-tap Offline tile

**Problem.** A user who needs to cut connectivity quickly has to open Settings and toggle airplane
mode, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth separately. Each extra step is a window in which a radio can remain
associated with a network.

**Implementation.** `OfflineTileService` is a Quick Settings `TileService` in `LenosOpsec`. On tap
it turns off Wi-Fi and Bluetooth first, then calls `ConnectivityManager.setAirplaneMode(true)`.
The tile is active when airplane mode is on; tapping again turns airplane mode off and leaves
Wi-Fi/Bluetooth off for the user to re-enable deliberately. If the platform call is denied it
falls back to the `AIRPLANE_MODE_ON` setting plus the protected broadcast, and never crashes the
tile.

**Limits.**

* Airplane mode is an Android/telephony policy, not a hardware power cut. It cannot prove the
  baseband, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth firmware has stopped transmitting. A faraday bag is the only
  physical guarantee.
* NFC is not toggled. Some devices keep NFC available in airplane mode.
* The tile needs the platform certificate for `NETWORK_SETTINGS`, `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` and
  `BLUETOOTH_PRIVILEGED`. It is built into the experimental product only.
* The tile does not erase Wi-Fi history, saved networks, eSIMs or accounts. Use the duress/auto-BFU
  controls for destruction.

**Verification.** On a test device, enable Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, tap the tile, and confirm all
three are off and the tile shows active. Tap again and confirm only airplane mode is off. Repeat
while the screen is locked and while a call is active; observe telephony behavior rather than
assuming.

## OPS-3 — clear clipboard on screen off

**Problem.** Android keeps the primary clip after the screen turns off. A locked device prevents
apps from reading it while locked, but the content survives until the app reads it or AOSP's
one-hour auto-clear timer fires. A user who copies a password, recovery phrase or address and then
puts the phone down leaves that content resident.

**Implementation.** A new `Settings.Secure.CLIPBOARD_CLEAR_ON_SCREEN_OFF` key (per user, default 0)
is read by `ClipboardService` when the protected `ACTION_SCREEN_OFF` broadcast arrives. For every
user who opted in, the service clears each clipboard for that user through the existing internal
clear path, which revokes URI grants and notifies listeners. The switch lives in
**Settings → Security & privacy → More security & privacy → Clipboard privacy**.

**Limits.**

* This is off by default. It is a deliberate user choice, not a forced data-loss policy.
* It clears the system clipboard, not copies kept by apps (clipboard managers, password managers,
  some keyboards) or autofill/IME histories.
* A lock without screen-off (for example, an app calling `lockNow()` while the display stays on)
  does not trigger the wipe. The feature is bound to screen-off because that is the reliable
  system broadcast.
* The AOSP one-hour auto-clear remains in place. A user setting a shorter timer is not part of this
  batch; the screen-off wipe is the OPSEC control.

**Verification.** Enable the switch; copy text, an image URI and a text URI; turn the screen off
and on; confirm `getPrimaryClip` is empty and URI grants are revoked for a test app. Confirm the
setting is per-user and survives a reboot.

## OPS-4 / Secure Paste stage 2 — per-app clipboard read control

**Problem.** The 1.0 Secure Paste control is a single global default. A user who wants to keep
paste working for a trusted password manager or notes app must allow clipboard reads for every
third-party app, or turn the global control off entirely. Android already has a per-app AppOp for
this (`android:read_clipboard`, `OP_READ_CLIPBOARD`), but no Settings surface for it.

**Implementation.** `ClipboardAppAccessSettings` is a Settings-only feature. It enumerates
user-installed apps, shows a switch per package, and writes `MODE_ALLOWED` / `MODE_IGNORED` through
`AppOpsManager.setMode`. `ClipboardService` already checks this AppOp after its focus and
system-service exemptions, so no framework patch, new permission or new AppOp is added. The screen
excludes system apps, updated system apps and disabled packages, and warns when an app shares a UID
with other packages. It is independent of the global Secure Paste switch: the global block wins,
and a per-app allow cannot override it.

**Limits.** Only user-installed apps are offered; blocking system apps or enabled keyboards is not a
supported path because it can break paste. Shared-UID packages share the mode. The screen uses a
simple preference list (no search provider) and is not a cryptographic capability boundary: an app
with a root compromise or a system service can still read what the system exposes. It does not
stop an app from writing to the clipboard.

## OPS-5 — tracking-parameter scrubber for shared text

**Problem.** Sharing a link often shares the sender's campaign source, ad click ID, referrer and
other tracking parameters. The receiving app can correlate the share with an advertising profile
even when the URL itself looks ordinary.

**Implementation.** `ScrubTextActivity` registers a `text/plain` share target in `LenosOpsec`. It
extracts `http`/`https` URLs with a local regex, removes known tracking parameters while preserving
the path, non-tracking query parameters and fragment, and lets the user inspect the result before
sharing or copying it. The parameter list is conservative: `utm_*`, `pk_*`, `mtm_*`, `hsa_*`,
`vero_*`, `oly_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, `dclid`, `msclkid`, `yclid`, `twclid`, `igshid`, `mc_cid`,
`mc_eid`, `_ga`, `_gl`, `gclsrc`, `srsltid`, `gad_source`, `wbraid`, `gbraid`, `mkt_tok`,
`elqTrackId`, `elqTrack`, `sc_cid`, `si`, and referrer fields. Links are never opened, resolved or
sent to a service.

**Limits.** This is not a URL safety scanner. It does not detect phishing, shortened-link targets,
tracking encoded in path segments or fragments, or unique identifiers in the remaining functional
parameters. It preserves parameters such as `source` and search queries because they may be needed
for the link to work. A site can still fingerprint the browser after the link is opened. The user
must review the cleaned text before sharing.

**Verification.** Share a URL containing `utm_source`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, a functional `id` and a
fragment; confirm only the tracking parameters are removed and the function/fragment survive.
Repeat with multiple URLs and plain text without links. Confirm the app has no network permission
and that “Copy cleaned text” produces the same string.

## Future OPSEC backlog (not implemented)

| Idea | Why it is not in this batch |
|---|---|
| Tor-only / Orbot routing | Requires an external Tor daemon/VpnService and a product decision about supported apps; not a source-only framework patch |
| Screenshot redaction / secure-screen automation | Needs a per-app policy and window-manager coordination; high risk of breaking banking/DRM apps |
| File timestamp and filesystem metadata scrubbing | Needs a privileged file manager and careful handling of media sync; not a share-sheet-sized feature |
| Panic destruction beyond duress/auto-BFU | Already covered by the 1.0 duress credential and auto-BFU timer; a new panic path needs a hardware/UX decision and is dangerous to add without device testing |
| Browser choice and update channel | Product decision; the experimental series deliberately ships no browser |

## Threat model summary

These controls are aimed at:

* a device that is about to be handed to another person or left unattended;
* metadata leakage when sharing media;
* radio persistence after the user believes connectivity is off;
* clipboard remnants after the user copies a secret.

They do **not** defend against a compromised OS, a malicious app with root, a hardware implant, or
an adversary who can image the storage before the wipe. They are not a substitute for verified
boot, full-disk encryption, the duress credential, or the auto-BFU timer.

# Provenance and deviations

The patches were produced by reading the GrapheneOS trees and re-applying the logic to the pinned
LineageOS 24.0 checkouts. They are not cherry-picks with hidden context: each patch is a complete
diff against the commit below. Original lenOS work is marked as such.

## Pinned targets

| Project | Revision | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `bionic` | `ff3bb041547924ac1a7504e4b3bd3ea18169ca2f` (`lineage-24.0`) | HTS-1 hardened thread stacks |
| `frameworks/base` | `7c7188f8585e20c035eb43fed72df5e717614b38` (`lineage-24.0`) | #20/#21, #22, #23 partial, #25, OPS-3 |
| `packages/apps/Settings` | `2f16bfe2c784623a324350cd19dae7f6066e2cfb` (`lineage-24.0`) | #17, #22, #23 partial, OPS-3, OPS-4 |
| `packages/apps/SetupWizard` | `9c75b8a75bb3e48d4ec96375fba00b1e409c8763` (`lineage-24.0`) | #28 |
| `packages/apps/Seedvault` | `cd6ab3fa1631d8c230b16a66239faca1e370b27e` (`lineage-24.0`) | #27 |
| `vendor/lenos` (main patchkit) | this repository, `lenos-1.0` | OPS-1 / OPS-2 source and opt-in product integration |

## GrapheneOS references

The local reference tree is `graphene-repos/fwb-full` at `ef402132a` (branch `17`). The Seedvault
reference is `GrapheneOS/platform_packages_apps_Seedvault` at `7cfffed` (branch `17`). The bionic
reference is the GrapheneOS bionic branch `17` at `e93ce48518dc0fba69878cb4ace37a3525862cbe`; the
hardened-thread-stack changes come from commits `4aefb578a7a0` (guard pages between static TLS and
stack), `369305a6632d` (move `pthread_internal_t` behind a guard page), `ff25c271653a` (secondary
stack randomization) and `b777629641e8` (missing overflow-check fixup). The relevant upstream files
are:

| lenOS patch | GrapheneOS source |
|---|---|
| `bionic/0001-hardened-thread-stacks.patch` | `libc/bionic/pthread_create.cpp` from the four GrapheneOS bionic commits listed above; no header change is needed |
| `frameworks_base/0001-system-app-update-verity.patch` | `services/core/java/com/android/server/pm/PackageVerityExt.java`; hooks in `services/core/java/com/android/server/pm/InstallPackageHelper.java` (`scanPackageForInitLI`, `preparePackageLI`) |
| `frameworks_base/0002-screenshot-sound-settings.patch` | `packages/SystemUI/src/com/android/systemui/screenshot/ScreenshotSoundController.kt` and `ScreenshotSoundPolicy.kt`; the existing `multivalentTests` for both classes |
| `frameworks_base/0003-usb-port-security.patch` | `core/java/android/hardware/usb/UsbPortSecurity.java`, `core/java/android/ext/settings/UsbPortSecurity.java`, `services/core/java/com/android/server/policy/keyguard/UsbPortSecurityHooks.java`, `core/java/android/hardware/usb/UsbManager.java`; AOSP `UsbService.enableUsbDataInternal` / `UsbPortManager.enableUsbData` |
| `packages_apps_Settings/0002-usb-port-security.patch` | GrapheneOS Settings `UsbPortSecurityPrefController.java` and `exploit_protection_settings.xml` (adapted to a standalone lenOS preference fragment) |
| `packages_apps_Seedvault/0001-grapheneos-app-id-prefix.patch` | Seedvault commit `db21e16` (internal `app.grapheneos` package prefix), binary chunker commit `61d1b60` / `libs/seedvault-chunker-0.1.jar` |
| `packages_apps_Settings/0004-clipboard-app-access.patch` | AOSP `AppOpsManager.OP_READ_CLIPBOARD` policy; the GrapheneOS per-app `GosPackageState` switch is not ported. This is the AppOps route anticipated by the stage-2 note in §8 of the main porting guide. |

## Original lenOS work

| Patch | Why it is original |
|---|---|
| `packages_apps_Settings/0001-crash-log-viewer.patch` | GrapheneOS's crash-reporting stack is a 17-file system-server service with a different UI and upload flow. This is a smaller, local-only DropBox reader with explicit sharing. |
| `packages_apps_SetupWizard/0001-bootloader-unlocked-warning.patch` | GrapheneOS's SetupWizard fork has no bootloader/unlocked warning; the feature was specified for lenOS and implemented against the LineageOS 24.0 Kotlin wizard. |
| `experimental/app/LenosOpsec` (source tree, installed only with `LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1`) | Original lenOS OPSEC tools: a metadata-scrubbing image share target, an Offline Quick Settings tile, and a tracking-parameter scrubber for shared text. |
| `frameworks_base/0004-clipboard-clear-on-screen-off.patch` + `packages_apps_Settings/0003-clipboard-privacy.patch` | Original lenOS OPSEC control. AOSP has a DeviceConfig auto-clear timer, not a screen-off wipe and not a user-facing setting. |
| `packages_apps_Settings/0004-clipboard-app-access.patch` | Original lenOS Settings UI over AOSP's existing `OP_READ_CLIPBOARD` AppOp. It does not port GrapheneOS's `GosPackageState` per-app state or its denial notification/toolbar path. |
| `frameworks_base/0005-native-debugging-block.patch` + `packages_apps_Settings/0005-native-debugging-block.patch` | Original lenOS global approximation of GrapheneOS's native-debugging control. It uses `prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)` for newly bound user app processes; the GOS per-app `GosPackageState`, SELinux package domains, denial notification and per-app UI are not ported. |

## Deliberate deviations

### HTS-1 — hardened thread stacks

* GrapheneOS enables the alternate layout unconditionally. lenOS keeps the four
  changes in one patch but selects them at runtime with
  `ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks`; only the exact value `1` enables the
  hardened path. The property is part of the experimental series
  (`LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1`), so the stable/default build adds no property and
  keeps the stock mapping.
* The port is limited to `libc/bionic/pthread_create.cpp`; no
  `pthread_internal.h`, linker, ART or allocator change is included. The main
  thread stays on the old path because `__libc_init_main_thread.cpp` calls the
  old allocator directly.
* The hardened path keeps the GrapheneOS layout: a page-aligned stack, a random
  `PROT_NONE` gap of at least one page (up to 50% of the stack on LP64 and 10%
  on LP32), a dedicated page for `pthread_internal_t`, and a stack top
  randomized within the old `pthread_internal_t` slot and aligned to 16 bytes.
* **lenOS deviation:** the zero-size mapping used for a caller-supplied stack
  skips the stack `mprotect` and the stack-top randomization. GrapheneOS's
  single `mprotect` range is not zero-length there, but splitting the regions
  in this port would otherwise call `mprotect(..., 0, ...)`. The metadata
  region is still protected and the gap remains `PROT_NONE`.
* **lenOS deviation:** all size additions on the hardened path use
  `__builtin_add_overflow`; the GrapheneOS code relies on the surrounding
  size checks. This is fail-closed: an overflow returns the empty mapping and
  `pthread_create` fails with `EAGAIN`.
* The existing AOSP `__allocate_thread_mapping` function is left unchanged and
  remains the only path when the property is absent or false.

### #20/#21 — system-app update verification

* The GrapheneOS class is ported in full for the normal package path, including static shared
  library handling. The AndroidPackageUtils original-package exception used by GrapheneOS for its
  browser and PDF viewer is **not** ported; lenOS does not ship those packages, and adding an
  allowlist without a concrete renamed system app would weaken the check.
* The boot-time signature check uses the same `INSTALLED_DATA` / `ROLLBACK` capability decision as
  GrapheneOS. LineageOS's additional signing-lineage helpers do not change that decision.
* The debug-only properties (`persist.disable_boot_time_fsverity_check`,
  `persist.disable_same_versionCode_sys_pkg_update_check`,
  `persist.disable_install_time_fsverity_check`) are retained so a debuggable build can recover
  from a bad test APK. They are never read on user builds.
* `PackageVerityExt` is not wired into `AndroidPackageUtils.getRealPackageOrNull`; this only
  matters for renamed system packages, which are not present in this product.

### #25 — screenshot sound

* The GrapheneOS diff is applied to the same two SystemUI classes and their existing
  `multivalentTests`. The `screenshotRemoveNonforcedSound` aconfig flag remains in place (it is a
  separate GrapheneOS feature that removes the non-forced sound on devices where it should not
  exist); only the `screenshotForceShutterSound` gate around registration and playback is removed.
* The forced-shutter path is unchanged: `MediaActionSound.mustPlayShutterSound()` still forces the
  sound when the camera is open, even if sound effects are disabled.
* **lenOS deviation:** GrapheneOS branch 17 checks `SOUND_EFFECTS_ENABLED` before evaluating the
  forced path, which can silence a legally required shutter sound when touch sounds are off. lenOS
  evaluates `shouldForceShutterSound()` first and gates only the non-forced player. The test
  `screenshotSoundForced_ignoresSoundEffectsSetting` pins that behavior.
* The GrapheneOS implementation moved `registerAvailabilityCallback` into an application-scoped
  coroutine and made `shouldForceShutterSound()` suspend. That is a required consequence of
  removing the aconfig guard: the callback must exist on every build, not only on builds where the
  flag was compiled in.

### #22 — USB-C data-line control

* GrapheneOS enforces the policy through vendor sysprops (`sys.port_security_mode`,
  `security.deny_new_usb2`) and its keyguard hooks. Those props are not portable to `asteroids`
  without the matching vendor HAL/kernel support, so this port uses the standard Android 17
  per-port `UsbPortManager.enableUsbData` HAL operation.
* Consequence: the AOSP operation disables the data lines only. Modes `ALL_PORTS_DISABLED` (0) and
  `CHARGING_ONLY` (1) are therefore equivalent on this build; a true VBUS-off mode needs a vendor
  HAL and is not claimed. The persistent key remains GrapheneOS's `persist.security.usb_mode` so a
  future HAL can consume it.
* The mode is applied on boot, on keyguard lock/unlock, and on first user unlock. AFU
  (`MODE_CHARGING_ONLY_WHEN_LOCKED_AFU`) uses an in-memory first-unlock flag, reset by every boot.
* User builds default to `MODE_CHARGING_ONLY_WHEN_LOCKED`; debuggable builds default to
  `MODE_ALL_PORTS_ENABLED` to keep adb available during bring-up. The Settings UI requires the
  device to be unlocked and asks for confirmation before allowing USB data while locked.
* The service has a deny gate for ordinary enable requests while the port-security policy is
  blocking; the controller bypasses it through `UsbPortManager` directly. This is intentionally
  asymmetric: security policy wins over app/HAL requests, while disable requests are always
  allowed.
* No `sys.port_security_mode`/`security.deny_new_usb2` writes are added. If the `asteroids` USB HAL
  does not implement `enableUsbData`, the policy is a no-op; the Settings screen detects “no USB
  ports” but cannot detect a HAL that reports ports and silently rejects the operation, hence the
  experimental status and physical verification step.

### #17 — crash/ANR log viewer

* Not a GrapheneOS port. It reads the existing DropBox crash/ANR/watchdog tags, bounds the number
  of records, and shares only on an explicit user action. There is no upload, no network
  permission, and no background reporting service.
* Settings needs `READ_LOGS`; the Settings UID is the system UID. The viewer is an About-phone
  entry, not a replacement for `logcat` or a full crash reporter.

### #27 — Seedvault app-id prefix

* LineageOS 24.0 already ships the Android 17 Seedvault upstream. This port applies the
  internal-prefix commit (`db21e16`) plus the GrapheneOS prebuilt chunker
  (`sha256 121735802e8e8c5e558379c9f3cfd5230e1baa60f73cd3905e935d40208148bb`).
* The public application id remains `com.stevesoltys.seedvault`, and the legacy
  `org.calyxos.seedvault.BASE_SPLIT` constant is retained for allowlist/backup compatibility.
  Only the internal `app.grapheneos` package prefix and permission names are renamed.
* Existing LineageOS Seedvault backups use the old internal names and may not restore. A migration
  test is required before this can be promoted.

### #28 — bootloader warning

* Original lenOS feature. GrapheneOS has no equivalent Setup Wizard code, and the LineageOS
  wizard is a different app. The warning is inserted on the welcome page, uses the hidden
  `ro.boot.verifiedbootstate` property, and is conditional on a non-green state. It does not block
  setup, does not ask the user to re-lock, and points out that re-locking an unsigned build can
  brick it.

### ENF-1 / #23 partial — native-debugging block

* Original lenOS implementation. GrapheneOS enforces `BLOCK_NATIVE_DEBUGGING` per package through
  `GosPackageState` and SELinux package domains, with per-app toggles and a denial notification.
  lenOS instead adds one global secure setting, one `prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)` native helper and
  an ActivityThread hook. It exempts system, debuggable and profileable apps, and it does not
  block root or any caller with `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`.
* It is intentionally not described as a full #23 port. Running processes are not changed, and
  there is no per-app state, denial UI or SELinux integration. It is an experimental primitive that
  must be boot-tested and reviewed before it could be promoted.

### OPS-1 — metadata scrubber

* Original lenOS work. Re-encoding is chosen over metadata parsing because it removes unknown
  metadata fields as well as EXIF/XMP/GPS, at the cost of recompression. The output is a new random
  file; the source is never modified. Animated GIF is rejected rather than silently flattened.
* The app has no `INTERNET` permission and no network code. It is platform-signed only because
  the same package also contains the privileged Offline tile; the scrubber itself uses no
  privileged API.

### OPS-2 — Offline tile

* Original lenOS work. Airplane mode is the authoritative switch; Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are turned
  off first. It does not toggle NFC and does not claim to power down the baseband. The
  platform-signed service uses `NETWORK_SETTINGS`, `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` and
  `BLUETOOTH_PRIVILEGED`; the fallback path writes the airplane setting and sends the protected
  broadcast rather than crashing.

### OPS-3 — screen-off clipboard wipe

* Original lenOS work. AOSP's existing auto-clear is a DeviceConfig timer (default one hour) that
  runs after a clip is read; this patch adds a per-user `Settings.Secure` opt-in and clears the
  clipboard when `ACTION_SCREEN_OFF` is received.
* The wipe uses the existing internal clear path, so URI grants are revoked and listeners are
  notified. It does not clear app-owned histories, IMEs or autofill storage, and it is off by
  default because deleting clipboard content without warning is a data-loss risk.

### OPS-4 — per-app clipboard access

* Original lenOS UI. GrapheneOS implements per-app clipboard access with `GosPackageState` and a
  denial notification/toolbar path; lenOS uses the existing AOSP `OP_READ_CLIPBOARD` AppOp instead.
  That is the stage-2 route anticipated in the main §8 audit. It deliberately does not port the
  `GosPackageState` core, the per-app state storage or the SystemUI toolbar.
* Only user-installed apps are listed. System apps, enabled keyboards and disabled packages are
  excluded to avoid breaking keyboard paste; shared-UID apps are shown with a warning because the
  AppOp applies to the package, not an isolated process. The global Secure Paste setting remains
  authoritative.

### OPS-5 — tracking-parameter scrubber

* Original lenOS work. The URL matcher and parameter list are local and intentionally conservative;
  the app never resolves a shortener, fetches a page or checks a blocklist. It preserves functional
  query parameters and fragments, so it is not a complete URL anonymizer. No GrapheneOS code is used.

## License

New files carry the Apache-2.0 header and credit GrapheneOS where the implementation derives from
it and the lenOS contributors. Modified AOSP files keep their original headers. See
[`../../LICENSE`](../../LICENSE).

====================================================================================================
# Security review (source-level)

This review covers the experimental patch set, not the main lenOS 1.0 series. Nothing here has
been built or booted. It records the threat model, the deliberate non-goals, and the issues found
while reviewing the patches at source level. A passing test is not a runtime security proof.

## Method

* Read every added framework, Settings, SetupWizard, bionic and `LenosOpsec` source file.
* Checked exported manifest components, signature/platform permissions and every call that writes a
  setting, system property or AppOp.
* Checked that the OPSEC app has no `INTERNET` permission and no socket/HTTP code.
* Checked that no patch flashes, wipes, relocks or changes verified boot.
* Ran the independent `git apply --check` series and an additional in-order Settings-series apply.
* Reviewed `--reset` behavior so test artifacts cannot survive into a later build.

## Findings

| Area | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Settings patch series | Five patches inserted at the same end-of-file anchors. Each passed alone, but 0002 failed after 0001. | **Fixed.** Distinct anchors, in-order sandbox test added. |
| Reset driver | Rename destinations (the Seedvault `app.grapheneos` tree) survived `--reset`. | **Fixed.** Rename/copy destinations and empty parents are removed; regression test added. |
| ENF-1 / #23 | This is a global opt-in dumpable-bit clear, not per-app native-debugging policy. Root/`CAP_SYS_PTRACE` and existing processes are exempt. If app seccomp rejects `prctl`, the helper logs and does nothing. An app that deliberately calls
`prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 1)` can undo its own bit; this is a hardening primitive, not a sandbox. | Deliberate limitation; documented and marked unbuilt. |
| #22 USB | The controller asks each port HAL to enable/disable data but does not turn a HAL failure into a UI error. A present port whose HAL ignores `enableUsbData` can therefore leave data enabled despite the selected mode. | Build/device validator required; documented limitation. |
| #17 crash logs | `READ_LOGS` is signature-level; entries stay local and sharing is explicit. The viewer does not upload. | Acceptable for a platform Settings app; runtime test pending. |
| #27 Seedvault | Internal prefix migration can make old backups unreadable by the new app id. | Documented; restore-migration test required. |
| #28 SetupWizard | Shows a warning when verified boot is not green; does not block setup, unlock, or relock. | Acceptable; first-boot states still need testing. |
| OPS-1 / OPS-5 | Both are exported share targets. They process only after a user action, cap image count at 20, re-encode images, and never resolve/open links. | Intentional export; no network. |
| OPS-2 Offline tile | Requires `NETWORK_SETTINGS`, `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` and `BLUETOOTH_PRIVILEGED`; the tile service is protected by `BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE`. The app is platform-signed. | High privilege is necessary for a radio kill switch; no extra permission beyond that. |
| OPS-3 / OPS-4 | Settings writes the secure clipboard setting and the existing `OP_READ_CLIPBOARD` AppOp. OPS-4 cannot override the global Secure Paste policy. | Acceptable; no new AppOp or permission. |
| HTS-1 thread stacks | The bionic mapping is selected only by the exact read-only property `ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks=1`, added by the experimental product fragment (`LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1`). `__allocate_thread_mapping` remains unchanged for the absent/false case. The random gap stays `PROT_NONE`; `pthread_internal_t` is in its own page. The main thread and existing threads keep their old layout. | Stable/default build keeps the stock mapping; source-level tests pass. Full bionic build, boot, thread stress and app compatibility required. |
| HTS-1 and MTE stack | Bionic's existing `__pthread_internal_remap_stack_with_mte` remaps the whole `mmap_base_unguarded` range for existing threads. If stack MTE is activated after hardened threads exist, that remap may make the random gap writable for those threads. HTS-1 does not enable MTE, and the target build does not claim MTE support. | Documented limitation; do not combine with stack MTE without a follow-up bionic change and validation. |
| #32 kernel | Additive config fragment only; no vendor/GKI option is disabled. It is not a runtime validation. | Needs boot, `/proc/config.gz`, `dmesg_restrict` and performance checks. |

## Deliberate non-goals

* ENF-1 does not claim to stop root, kernel, `debuggerd`, or a process with `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`.
* The USB policy does not claim to cut VBUS or protect against a malicious charger; it only asks
  the port HAL to disable data.
* The share targets do not sanitize arbitrary file formats; unsupported images fail rather than
  silently pass through.
* The Settings log viewer does not guarantee deletion of logs held by other system components.
* HTS-1 is a stack-layout change, not a memory-safety proof or a sandbox. It does not stop
  arbitrary memory corruption, replace `hardened_malloc`, enable MTE/TBI or change BTI/PAC,
  seccomp, ART or JIT policy. Its memory/performance cost and app compatibility are unmeasured.
* No signing key, recovery image, bootloader state or verified-boot chain is modified by these
  patches.

## Required before promotion

1. Build every project with the experimental series applied in order.
2. Boot `asteroids`, check SELinux denial logs and the hidden-API build check.
3. Run the checks in `verification.md`, including a same-UID ptrace attempt, USB data behavior
   while locked, a Seedvault restore, a Setup Wizard first boot with green and non-green
   verified-boot properties, and HTS-1 thread-creation/app-compatibility/memory checks against a
   control build. Do not promote HTS-1 on source-level tests alone.
4. Promote only the features that pass. ENF-1 remains experimental until the per-app policy or an
   explicit product decision replaces it.

# Verification checklist (after the first build)

Nothing in this repository has been built or booted. Run these checks only in a build window that
follows [`../../docs/flash-and-lock.md`](../../docs/flash-and-lock.md); flashing needs explicit
approval.

## Build-time

1. From the main `vendor/lenos` checkout, apply the **stable series first** and the
   experimental series second, with the opt-in flag:

   ```bash
   LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1 ./lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh apply
   ```

   This applies `patches/` then `patches-experimental/`, installs
   `experimental/app/LenosOpsec` into the build tree, adds the HTS-1 property,
   and exports the flag. For a manual `mka` invocation, pass
   `LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1` yourself.
2. Build the full `asteroids` product. `config/lenos-experimental.mk` adds `LenosOpsec` to
   `PRODUCT_PACKAGES` only under that flag; confirm it is in the build graph:
   ```bash
   adb shell pm path org.lenos.opsec
   adb shell cmd package resolve-activity --brief \
       -a android.intent.action.SEND -t image/jpeg
   ```
3. Confirm `PackageVerityExt`, `UsbPortSecurity`, `UsbPortSecurityController`,
   `ClipboardPrivacySettings`, `NativeDebuggingBlock` and `LenosOpsec` are compiled (inspect the
   build log for the paths).
4. Confirm no `neverallow` or hidden-API failure was introduced. The brand-new framework APIs are
   `@hide`; Settings and `LenosOpsec` are platform apps. The USB, clipboard and native-debugging
   patches must not require sepolicy changes.
5. Check the experimental product does not include a browser or network code from `LenosOpsec`:
   `adb shell dumpsys package org.lenos.opsec | grep -i internet` must be empty.
6. Run the read-only helpers before manual testing:
   ```bash
   OUT="out/target/product/asteroids" tools/verify-build.sh
   ANDROID_SERIAL=... tools/verify-device.sh
   ```
   `verify-build.sh` only checks artifacts; `verify-device.sh` only reads properties/settings and
   never writes, flashes, reboots or force-stops.

## #20/#21 — system-app update verification

These checks are intentionally destructive to a **test** system-app update, not to a production
device. Use a disposable userdata image or a test device.

1. Boot and filter logcat:
   ```bash
   adb logcat -b all -s PackageVerityExt
   ```
   A normal boot with no `/data` system-app updates should be quiet. If a system app has an
   update, expect `Performing verification of system package update <package>`.
2. Install a test update for a debuggable system app signed with the platform key. It should
   install if its `versionCode` is greater and every split has fs-verity.
3. Try the same `versionCode` as the system image package. The install must fail; the log should
   contain `Not allowed to update system package to the same versionCode`.
4. Try an update without fs-verity (remove the `.idsig`, or use an APK that does not get fs-verity
   set up). The install must fail with the fs-verity message. A debug build can bypass with
   `adb shell setprop persist.disable_install_time_fsverity_check true`; a user build must not.
5. Reboot with a lower-version `/data` update already installed. The boot-time scan must reject it
   and the system image version must be active again. Confirm with:
   ```bash
   adb shell dumpsys package <package> | grep -E 'versionCode|codePath'
   ```
6. Reboot with a valid update. It must survive the reboot and remain the active code path.
7. Verify a mismatched signing certificate is rejected with `INSTALL_FAILED_BAD_SIGNATURE`.

## #25 — screenshot sound

1. With **Settings → Sound & vibration → Touch sounds** (the `SOUND_EFFECTS_ENABLED` setting) on,
   take a screenshot: the normal screenshot sound must play.
2. Turn it off, take a screenshot: no sound.
3. On a device/region where `MediaActionSound.mustPlayShutterSound()` is true, open the camera and
   take a screenshot with sound effects off: the forced shutter sound must still play.
4. Repeat with the camera closed: no forced sound.
5. Check that screenshot capture latency and SystemUI crashes are unchanged in logcat.

## #22 — USB-C data-line control

This is the highest-risk item in the batch because it depends on a vendor HAL. Test with a
**non-production** device and a USB cable/host that cannot damage the port.

1. Before applying the patch, confirm the device's USB port list:
   ```bash
   adb shell dumpsys usb
   ```
   If Android reports no ports, Settings will show “unsupported” and the feature cannot work.
2. Confirm the HAL implements `enableUsbData`:
   ```bash
   adb shell dumpsys usb | grep -i -E 'enableUsbData|data signal|port'
   adb logcat -b all -s UsbPortSecurity UsbPortManager
   ```
   A successful policy change should log `applying USB port security mode ...` with the port
   count. If the HAL returns an error, the log must show it and data must remain in its prior
   state; do not treat an error as a successful block.
3. Lock the device with a USB data device attached (a USB stick, not just a charger). The data
   device must disappear; charging must continue. Unlock and confirm it re-enumerates.
4. Check `adb shell getprop persist.security.usb_mode` returns the mode written by Settings.
   `MODE_CHARGING_ONLY_WHEN_LOCKED` should be `2`, AFU `3`, enabled `4`.
5. Reboot locked, attach a USB device, and confirm AFU mode does not expose data before first
   unlock. Unlock and confirm data returns.
6. Try an ordinary app/USB enable request while the policy is blocking; it must fail with the
   documented internal error rather than overriding the policy.
7. On a debug build, confirm the default is `4` (USB data enabled) so adb remains available.
   On a user build, confirm the default is `2`; document the escape hatch before testing.
8. Test the Settings confirmation dialog, the unsupported state, and changing the mode while the
   device is locked (must be rejected).

## #17 — crash/ANR log viewer

1. Open **Settings → About phone → Crash logs** (wording may differ), trigger a deliberate test
   crash in a disposable app, then confirm the entry appears after DropBox records it.
2. Confirm only crash/ANR/Java/watchdog tags are shown, entries are bounded, and no network
   permission or upload path exists.
3. Use the explicit share action and confirm it opens a chooser; cancel it and verify no file is
   written outside the app's cache.
4. Confirm the viewer does not expose other users' DropBox entries and that a locked device cannot
   open the Settings activity.

## #27 — Seedvault app-id prefix

1. Build Seedvault; confirm `com.stevesoltys.seedvault` is still the package id and the app
   launches.
2. Create a new backup with the GrapheneOS chunker; restore it on a clean test device.
3. Restore an **old** LineageOS Seedvault backup and record whether it succeeds. If it does not,
   the migration path must be written before promotion.
4. Check the internal package prefix with:
   ```bash
   adb shell dumpsys package com.stevesoltys.seedvault | grep -i app.grapheneos
   ```
5. Confirm `BASE_SPLIT` and the allowlist still resolve; do not remove the legacy constant.

## #28 — Setup Wizard bootloader warning

1. On a test build with `ro.boot.verifiedbootstate=green`, run Setup Wizard and confirm the
   warning is absent.
2. On an unlocked/unsigned test build (`orange`/`yellow`/`red`), confirm the warning appears on
   the welcome page, does not block Next, and the text does not tell the user to re-lock an
   unsigned build.
3. Confirm the property read is safe when the property is missing; the warning must not crash
   Setup Wizard.
4. Check the warning survives rotation and is not duplicated on back/forward navigation.

## OPS-1 — metadata scrubber

1. Share a geotagged JPEG to “lenOS OPSEC” from Gallery/Files; choose “Remove metadata and share”.
2. Receive it in a test app and parse it with an external tool:
   ```bash
   exiftool received.jpg | grep -i -E 'gps|exif|xmp|software|date'
   ```
   The output must have no GPS/EXIF/XMP fields and a randomized file name.
3. Repeat with PNG, WebP, HEIF and a multi-select share. Confirm animated GIF is rejected cleanly.
4. Confirm the app requests no network access and that airplane mode does not break the flow.
5. Test “Save sanitized copy” and confirm `Pictures/lenOS` contains a file with no source name.

## OPS-2 — Offline tile

1. Add the “Offline” tile from the Quick Settings edit screen; confirm it appears and the icon
   state reflects airplane mode.
2. With Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on, tap the tile. All three must turn off; the tile must be active.
3. Tap again; airplane mode must turn off, and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth must stay off until explicitly
   re-enabled.
4. Repeat while a call is active and while the screen is locked; record telephony behavior and any
   permission denial in logcat.
5. Confirm no crash when the platform call is denied (revoke `NETWORK_SETTINGS` on a test build or
   use the fallback path) and that the tile still updates.

## OPS-3 — screen-off clipboard wipe

1. Enable **Settings → Security & privacy → More security & privacy → Clipboard privacy**.
2. Copy text, an image URI and a text URI; turn the screen off, wait for the lock screen, then turn
   it on. A test app must get an empty primary clip; URI grants must be revoked.
3. Repeat with the setting disabled; the clip must survive (until AOSP's own auto-clear timer).
4. Confirm the setting is per-user: a second user with the setting off must keep their clipboard.
5. Reboot and confirm the setting persists and the screen-off receiver still fires.
6. Confirm clearing does not crash when the clipboard contains a URI grant or a virtual-device
   clipboard.

## OPS-4 — per-app clipboard access

1. Open **Settings → Security & privacy → More security & privacy → Clipboard access by app** and
   confirm only user-installed packages appear, with labels, package names and switches.
2. Use a test app that reads the clipboard while focused. Allow it, copy text in another app, and
   confirm the test app can read it.
3. Turn the test app off. Copy again and confirm the read returns null/empty while the app is
   focused. Confirm the global Secure Paste setting still wins if it is also blocking reads.
4. Confirm system apps and enabled keyboards are absent, and that a shared-UID package shows the warning.
5. Toggle an app, reboot, and confirm the AppOp persists:
   ```bash
   adb shell cmd appops get <package> android:read_clipboard
   ```
6. Confirm the screen does not crash when the package list is empty or when an app is uninstalled
   while the list is loading.

## OPS-5 — tracking-parameter scrubber

1. Share text containing a URL with `utm_source`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, a functional `id` parameter
   and a fragment to “lenOS OPSEC”; choose “Remove tracking parameters”.
2. Confirm only the known tracking fields are gone, the `id` parameter and fragment remain, and
   the app does not open the link.
3. Share multiple URLs and plain text with no links; confirm only the URLs are changed.
4. Use “Copy cleaned text” and compare it with the preview. Confirm the app has no network code and
   that a malformed URL is left untouched rather than crashing.
5. Check a shortened link: the scrubber must not resolve it and the UI must not imply it is safe.

## HTS-1 — hardened thread stacks

HTS-1 is part of the experimental series (`LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1`). The stable
default build keeps the stock mapping. Do not use HTS-1 on a daily driver until
the boot and compatibility checks pass.

1. Build two images for comparison. The HTS-1 image is a normal experimental
   build. For the control, temporarily remove the
   `ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks=1` line from
   `$SRC/vendor/lenos/config/lenos-experimental.mk` in a separate tree, rebuild,
   and restore the line afterwards. Confirm the HTS-1 image has the property set
   to exactly `1` and the control build does not have it:
   ```bash
   adb shell getprop ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks
   OUT=out/target/product/asteroids LENOS_EXPECT_HARDENED_STACKS=1 \
       tools/verify-build.sh
   ```
   `verify-build.sh` prints the property; the control build should print
   `<unset>`. Do not try to change it with `setprop`; it is a read-only build
   property.

2. Confirm the alternate mapping is actually used for a new thread. Pick a
   debuggable test app, start several worker threads, and inspect its VMAs:
   ```bash
   PID="$(adb shell pidof <test.package>)"
   adb shell cat "/proc/$PID/maps" | grep 'stack_and_tls'
   ```
   With the property set, the mapping should contain a writable stack region,
   a `---p` (PROT_NONE) gap, and a separate writable page for
   `pthread_internal_t`/TLS. With the property absent, use the same command on
   the control build and record the stock layout. If SELinux denies
   `/proc/<pid>/maps`, use a debuggable test app and `run-as`, or a native
   test binary in `/data/local/tmp`; do not weaken SELinux to run the check.

3. Stress thread creation and teardown: create and join at least 10,000
   short-lived threads in a native test app, plus repeated app launches,
   ART/zygote activity, WebView page loads, camera open/close, and Binder-heavy
   flows. Watch for:
   ```bash
   adb logcat -b crash -b main -s libc DEBUG tombstoned
   adb shell dmesg | grep -i -E 'oom|segfault|stack'
   ```
   A `pthread_create` failure with `EAGAIN` is fail-closed behavior, not a
   reason to disable the guard; investigate the mapping arithmetic instead.

4. Compare memory and launch time between the control and HTS-1 builds. The
   random gap is virtual address space, so expect `VmSize` to rise (up to 50%
   of thread stack size on 64-bit, 10% on 32-bit) without a matching RSS rise.
   Record `MemAvailable`, `VmSize`, `VmRSS`, cold app-launch time, and any
   increase in page-fault rate. Reject the feature if RSS or latency regresses
   materially.

5. Reboot, lock/unlock, make an emergency call, use the camera, and run a
   full app-compatibility pass. HTS-1 does not touch AVB, encryption, SELinux,
   recovery or the kernel, but the boot must still be treated as a test build
   until this pass is complete.

6. Only then consider a longer soak. Keep the control build available so a
   regression can be bisected to the property rather than to the rest of the
   experimental series.

Known limitation: the main thread and threads created before the property is
read keep their existing layout. This feature does not add `hardened_malloc`,
MTE/TBI, BTI/PAC, exec spawning, JIT restrictions or seccomp changes.

## ENF-1 / #23 partial — native-debugging block

This verifies the experimental global primitive, **not** GrapheneOS's per-app feature.

1. Build and boot with the framework and Settings patches. Confirm **Block native debugging** is
   off by default:
   ```bash
   adb shell settings get secure block_native_debugging
   ```
   The expected result is `null` or `0`.
2. Enable it in **Settings → Security & privacy → More security & privacy → Block native
   debugging**. Start a fresh non-system, non-debuggable app process and confirm its dumpable bit is
   clear:
   ```bash
   adb shell pidof <package>
   adb shell cat /proc/<pid>/status | grep -i dumpable
   ```
   Also verify from a same-UID non-root context that `ptrace`/`/proc/<pid>/mem` is denied. Do not
   use this check on a production device without a recovery plan.
3. Confirm the exemptions: a debuggable build, a profileable app and a system app must retain
   normal debugging/profiling behavior. Confirm a newly started app after disabling the setting is
   back to normal.
4. Confirm root or a process with `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` (for example the crash dumper) can still collect
   a tombstone; ENF-1 is not a root-of-trust boundary.
5. Reboot and force-stop an app after toggling; verify the setting persists and that running
   processes are not silently retrofitted. This is the documented global approximation, not the
   per-app `GosPackageState` policy.

## Rollback

If the build fails or the device misbehaves, use `lenos-patch.py --reset` on the source tree and
rebuild. Do not attempt to recover a device by weakening verified boot or locking state. Follow

"""Test harness for the experimental series in this repository.

The experimental patches are *not* standalone against a pristine AOSP tree.
They are applied after the stable lenOS 1.0 series. ``LenosPatchTest`` builds
a sandbox containing the pinned files touched by both series, applies the
stable patches for the project, then applies the requested experimental
patch(es). This is the same strict ``git apply`` path the driver uses, without
touching the workspace checkout.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

MAIN = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
VENDOR = MAIN
PATCH_ROOT = MAIN / "patches-experimental"
STABLE_PATCH_ROOT = MAIN / "patches"
WORKSPACE = Path(os.environ.get(
    "LENOS_WORKSPACE",
    str(Path.home() / "lineage")))

sys.path.insert(0, str(MAIN / "tools"))
from lenos_projects import alias_for, project_for  # noqa: E402

try:
    import tree_sitter
    import tree_sitter_java
    _JAVA_PARSER = tree_sitter.Parser(tree_sitter.Language(tree_sitter_java.language()))
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - optional dependency
    _JAVA_PARSER = None


def java_syntax_errors(path: Path) -> int:
    if _JAVA_PARSER is None:
        raise unittest.SkipTest("tree-sitter-java not installed")
    tree = _JAVA_PARSER.parse(path.read_bytes())

    def walk(node):
        n = 1 if (node.type == "ERROR" or node.is_missing) else 0
        for child in node.children:
            n += walk(child)
        return n

    return walk(tree.root_node)


def patch_paths(patch: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Every file path the patch touches, including rename/copy and binary ends."""
    out: list[str] = []

    def add(p: str) -> None:
        p = p.split("\t")[0].strip()
        if p.startswith("a/") or p.startswith("b/"):
            p = p[2:]
        if p not in ("", "/dev/null") and p not in out:
            out.append(p)

    for line in patch.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 4:
                add(parts[2])
                add(parts[3])
        elif line.startswith("--- ") or line.startswith("+++ "):
            add(line[4:])
        elif line.startswith(("rename from ", "rename to ",
                              "copy from ", "copy to ")):
            add(line.split(" ", 2)[2])
    return out


def patch_created_paths(patch: Path) -> set[str]:
    """Files the patch creates or renames to."""
    created: set[str] = set()
    old_is_null = False
    for line in patch.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("--- "):
            old_is_null = line[4:].split("\t")[0].strip() == "/dev/null"
        elif line.startswith("+++ "):
            p = line[4:].split("\t")[0].strip()
            if old_is_null and p not in ("", "/dev/null"):
                created.add(p[2:] if p.startswith("b/") else p)
            old_is_null = False
        elif line.startswith(("rename to ", "copy to ")):
            p = line.split(" to ", 1)[1].strip()
            if p not in ("", "/dev/null"):
                created.add(p[2:] if p.startswith("b/") else p)
    return created


def series_for(project: str, root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    pdir = root / alias_for(project)
    sfile = pdir / "series"
    if not sfile.is_file():
        return []
    out = []
    for line in sfile.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        patch = pdir / line
        if not patch.is_file():
            raise AssertionError(f"series lists missing patch: {patch}")
        out.append(patch)
    return out


def build_sandbox(project: str, extra_patches: list[Path],
                  extra_files: list[str] | None = None,
                  apply_extra: bool = True) -> Path:
    """Copy the needed pinned files, apply stable then experimental patches."""
    sandbox = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="lenos-exp-test-"))
    project_dir = WORKSPACE / project
    if not project_dir.is_dir():
        raise unittest.SkipTest(f"workspace project missing: {project_dir}")

    stable_patches = series_for(project, STABLE_PATCH_ROOT)
    patches = stable_patches + list(extra_patches)
    files: list[str] = list(extra_files or [])
    created: set[str] = set()
    for patch in patches:
        files += patch_paths(patch)
        created |= patch_created_paths(patch)

    for rel in files:
        src = project_dir / rel
        if not src.is_file():
            if rel in created:
                continue  # git apply creates it in the sandbox
            raise AssertionError(f"pinned file missing in workspace tree: {project}/{rel}")
        dst = sandbox / rel
        dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(src, dst)

    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = "/dev/null"
    env["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"] = "/dev/null"
    to_apply = stable_patches + (list(extra_patches) if apply_extra else [])
    for patch in to_apply:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", str(patch)],
            cwd=sandbox, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            shutil.rmtree(sandbox, ignore_errors=True)
            raise AssertionError(f"patch failed to apply: {patch}\n{proc.stderr}")
    return sandbox


class LenosPatchTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Apply the stable base plus one or more experimental patches."""

    PROJECT: str = ""
    PATCHES: list[str] = []
    EXTRA_FILES: list[str] = []

    sandbox: Path

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        if not cls.PROJECT:
            raise unittest.SkipTest("no PROJECT set")
        pdir = PATCH_ROOT / alias_for(cls.PROJECT)
        patches = [pdir / name for name in cls.PATCHES]
        cls.sandbox = build_sandbox(cls.PROJECT, patches, cls.EXTRA_FILES)
        cls.addClassCleanup(shutil.rmtree, cls.sandbox, ignore_errors=True)

    # --- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
    def text(self, rel: str) -> str:
        return (self.sandbox / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

    def assert_contains(self, rel: str, *needles: str):
        body = self.text(rel)
        for needle in needles:
            self.assertIn(needle, body, f"{rel} is missing {needle!r}")

    def assert_not_contains(self, rel: str, *needles: str):
        body = self.text(rel)
        for needle in needles:
            self.assertNotIn(needle, body, f"{rel} still contains {needle!r}")

    def assert_java_syntax(self, rel: str):
        errors = java_syntax_errors(self.sandbox / rel)
        self.assertEqual(errors, 0, f"{rel}: {errors} Java parse errors after patching")

    def assert_xml(self, rel: str):
        ET.parse(self.sandbox / rel)

    def assert_balanced(self, rel: str):
        body = self.text(rel)
        for open_c, close_c in (("{", "}"), ("(", ")"), ("[", "]")):
            self.assertEqual(body.count(open_c), body.count(close_c),
                             f"{rel}: unbalanced {open_c}{close_c}")


class SourceTreeTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Assertions over opt-in source files that are not patch-applied."""

    def text(self, rel: str) -> str:
        return (MAIN / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

    def assert_contains(self, rel: str, *needles: str):
        body = self.text(rel)
        for needle in needles:
            self.assertIn(needle, body, f"{rel} is missing {needle!r}")

    def assert_not_contains(self, rel: str, *needles: str):
        body = self.text(rel)
        for needle in needles:
            self.assertNotIn(needle, body, f"{rel} still contains {needle!r}")

    def assert_java_syntax(self, rel: str):
        errors = java_syntax_errors(MAIN / rel)
        self.assertEqual(errors, 0, f"{rel}: {errors} Java parse errors")

    def assert_xml(self, rel: str):
        ET.parse(MAIN / rel)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the lenOS patch test suite.
#   ./run-tests.sh              all tests
#   ./run-tests.sh test_ssaid   one module
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
if [[ -n "${LENOS_WORKSPACE+x}" && ! -d "$LENOS_WORKSPACE" ]]; then
  echo "error: LENOS_WORKSPACE is not a directory: $LENOS_WORKSPACE" >&2
  exit 1
fi
export LENOS_WORKSPACE="${LENOS_WORKSPACE:-$HOME/lineage}"
if [[ ! -d "$LENOS_WORKSPACE" ]]; then
  echo "warning: no LineageOS tree at $LENOS_WORKSPACE; patch-application tests will be skipped" >&2
fi
PY="${LENOS_PYTHON:-$(command -v python3)}"
cd "$HERE"
if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
  set -- discover -s . -p 'test_*.py'
fi
exec "$PY" -m unittest "$@" -v

"""OPSEC: wipe the clipboard when the screen turns off.

AOSP's only automatic clipboard wipe is a DeviceConfig timer (one hour by

down or hands it to someone else. It is opt-in and per-user.

"""Source-level checks for the opt-in bionic hardened thread-stack patch."""

class TestHardenedThreadStacks(LenosPatchTest):

    PATCHES = ["0001-hardened-thread-stacks.patch"]

            '__system_property_get("ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks", value)',

            "value[0] == '1'",
        )
        self.assert_not_contains(SOURCE, "persist.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks")
        self.assert_not_contains(SOURCE, "atoi(")

        self.assert_not_contains(SOURCE, "LENOS_HARDENED_THREAD_STACKS")

    def test_stock_mapping_remains_the_fallback(self):
        self.assert_contains(

            "? __allocate_hardened_thread_mapping(attr->stack_size, attr->guard_size)",
            ": __allocate_thread_mapping(attr->stack_size, attr->guard_size);",
            "? __allocate_hardened_thread_mapping(0, PTHREAD_GUARD_SIZE)",
            ": __allocate_thread_mapping(0, PTHREAD_GUARD_SIZE);",

    def test_thread_metadata_has_a_dedicated_page_above_the_stack(self):
        self.assert_contains(

            "size_t thread_page_size = __builtin_align_up(sizeof(pthread_internal_t), page_size());",
            "result.static_tls = result.libgen_buffers - static_tls_layout_size;",
            "mapping.static_tls - __builtin_align_up(sizeof(pthread_internal_t), page_size())",
            "memset(thread, 0, sizeof(pthread_internal_t));",
        )

    def test_random_gap_is_at_least_one_page(self):
        self.assert_contains(

            "gap_size = __builtin_align_up(arc4random_uniform(max_gap_size), page_size());",
            "if (gap_size == 0) gap_size = page_size();",
            "const size_t non_stack_writeable_offset = stack_guard_size + stack_size + gap_size;",
            "mmap_size - non_stack_writeable_offset - PTHREAD_GUARD_SIZE",
        )
        # The stack and the metadata/TLS region must be made writable separately;
        # the randomized gap in between stays PROT_NONE.
        self.assert_contains(

            "__builtin_add_overflow(mmap_size, thread_page_size, &mmap_size)",

            "__builtin_add_overflow(mmap_size, PTHREAD_GUARD_SIZE, &mmap_size)",
            "__builtin_add_overflow(mmap_size, libgen_buffers_padded_size, &mmap_size)",
        )

            "__builtin_align_down(result.stack_top, 16);",

"""Integration checks for the experimental series.

These are deliberately separate from the per-feature tests: they prove that
each patch applies after the stable series, in series order, and independently.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
import unittest

from harness import (PATCH_ROOT, STABLE_PATCH_ROOT, build_sandbox,
                     project_for, series_for)


class TestImportedSeries(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_experimental_project_applies_after_stable(self):
        projects = set()
        for pdir in sorted(PATCH_ROOT.iterdir()):
            if not pdir.is_dir() or not (pdir / "series").is_file():
                continue
            project = project_for(pdir.name)
            self.assertIsNotNone(project, f"unknown experimental project: {pdir.name}")
            projects.add(project)
            sandbox = build_sandbox(project, series_for(project, PATCH_ROOT))
            self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, sandbox, ignore_errors=True)
        self.assertEqual(projects, {
            "bionic", "frameworks/base", "packages/apps/Settings",
            "packages/apps/SetupWizard", "packages/apps/Seedvault"})

    def test_each_experimental_patch_applies_independently_after_stable(self):
        for pdir in sorted(PATCH_ROOT.iterdir()):
            if not pdir.is_dir() or not (pdir / "series").is_file():
                continue
            project = project_for(pdir.name)
            self.assertIsNotNone(project, f"unknown experimental project: {pdir.name}")
            for patch in series_for(project, PATCH_ROOT):
                sandbox = build_sandbox(project, [patch])
                shutil.rmtree(sandbox, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_no_duplicate_file_blocks_in_a_patch(self):
        # A duplicated new-file diff cannot be reverse-applied, which breaks
        # reset and applied-state checks. Catch it at source level.
        for patch in PATCH_ROOT.rglob("*.patch"):
            seen: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = {}
            for line in patch.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
                if not line.startswith("diff --git "):
                    continue
                parts = line.split()
                if len(parts) >= 4:
                    key = (parts[2], parts[3])
                    seen[key] = seen.get(key, 0) + 1
            duplicates = {k: n for k, n in seen.items() if n > 1}
            self.assertEqual(duplicates, {}, f"{patch}: duplicate file blocks {duplicates}")

    def test_no_stray_experimental_patches(self):
        for pdir in sorted(PATCH_ROOT.iterdir()):
            if not pdir.is_dir():
                continue
            series_file = pdir / "series"
            self.assertTrue(series_file.is_file(), f"{pdir.name} has no series file")
            listed = {ln.strip() for ln in series_file.read_text().splitlines()
                      if ln.strip() and not ln.strip().startswith("#")}
            present = {f.name for f in pdir.glob("*.patch")}
            self.assertEqual(present - listed, set(),
                             f"{pdir.name}: patches not in series: "
                             f"{sorted(present - listed)}")
            self.assertEqual(listed - present, set(),
                             f"{pdir.name}: series lists missing patches: "
                             f"{sorted(listed - present)}")

    def test_stable_series_is_not_changed_by_import(self):
        self.assertFalse((PATCH_ROOT / "vendor_lenos").exists())
        stable_projects = {d.name for d in STABLE_PATCH_ROOT.iterdir()
                           if (d / "series").is_file()}
        self.assertNotIn("packages_apps_SetupWizard", stable_projects)
        self.assertNotIn("packages_apps_Seedvault", stable_projects)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Seedvault GrapheneOS app-id prefix and chunker (Tier 2 #27, experimental).

This is the GrapheneOS-specific part of their Seedvault fork, not a jump to
their Android 17 upstream: internal package names get the ``app.grapheneos``
prefix and the prebuilt chunker is replaced by the GrapheneOS build. The
application id stays ``com.stevesoltys.seedvault`` so the LineageOS product
allowlist and existing app identity keep working.

The source-level tests apply the patch to a throwaway shared clone because it
contains renames and a binary jar. This is still not a build or a restore test;
``docs/verification.md`` lists the required device checks.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from harness import PATCH_ROOT, VENDOR, WORKSPACE

ALIAS = "packages_apps_Seedvault"
PATCH = "0001-grapheneos-app-id-prefix.patch"
PROJECT = "packages/apps/Seedvault"
GOS_CHUNKER_SHA256 = (
    "121735802e8e8c5e558379c9f3cfd5230e1baa60f73cd3905e935d40208148bb"
)


class TestSeedvaultAppIdPrefix(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.patch = PATCH_ROOT / ALIAS / PATCH
        cls.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="lenos-seedvault-"))
        cls.addClassCleanup(shutil.rmtree, cls.tmp, ignore_errors=True)
        cls.repo = cls.tmp / "Seedvault"
        src = WORKSPACE / PROJECT
        if not (src / ".git").is_dir():
            raise unittest.SkipTest(f"workspace project missing: {src}")
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clone", "--shared", "--quiet", str(src), str(cls.repo)],
            capture_output=True, text=True)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise AssertionError(proc.stderr)
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "apply", "--check", str(cls.patch)],
            cwd=cls.repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise AssertionError(f"Seedvault patch does not apply: {proc.stderr}")
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", str(cls.patch)],
            cwd=cls.repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise AssertionError(f"Seedvault patch failed: {proc.stderr}")

    def read(self, rel: str) -> str:
        return (self.repo / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

    def test_internal_packages_use_the_grapheneos_prefix(self):
        self.assertIn(
            'PACKAGE_NAME_CONTACTS = "app.grapheneos.backup.contacts"',
            self.read("app/src/main/java/com/stevesoltys/seedvault/ui/SystemData.kt"))
        self.assertIn(
            "namespace = \"app.grapheneos.seedvault.core\"",
            self.read("core/build.gradle.kts"))
        self.assertIn(
            "namespace = \"app.grapheneos.backup.storage\"",
            self.read("storage/lib/build.gradle.kts"))
        self.assertIn(
            "package app.grapheneos.backup.storage.backup;",
            self.read("storage/lib/src/main/proto/backup_snapshot.proto"))
        self.assertTrue(
            (self.repo / "core/src/main/java/app/grapheneos/seedvault/core/backends/Backend.kt").is_file())
        self.assertFalse(
            (self.repo / "core/src/main/java/org/calyxos/seedvault").exists())

    def test_application_id_is_unchanged(self):
        # Keeping the app id is what makes this compatible with the Lineage
        # allowlist and with an existing Seedvault installation.
        self.assertIn(
            'namespace = "com.stevesoltys.seedvault"',
            self.read("app/build.gradle.kts"))
        self.assertIn(
            'package="com.stevesoltys.seedvault"',
            self.read("app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml"))

    def test_grapheneos_chunker_binary_is_used(self):
        jar = self.repo / "libs/seedvault-chunker-0.1.jar"
        digest = hashlib.sha256(jar.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        self.assertEqual(digest, GOS_CHUNKER_SHA256)
        self.assertIn("GIT binary patch", self.patch.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    def test_no_old_internal_package_references_remain(self):
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["grep", "-RIn", "--include=*.kt", "--include=*.java",
             "--include=*.xml", "--include=*.proto", "--include=*.bp",
             "--include=*.kts", "org.calyxos.seedvault", "."],
            cwd=self.repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
        lines = [line for line in proc.stdout.splitlines()
                 if "BASE_SPLIT" not in line]
        self.assertEqual(lines, [])
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["grep", "-RIn", "--include=*.kt", "--include=*.java",
             "--include=*.xml", "--include=*.proto", "--include=*.bp",
             "--include=*.kts", "org.calyxos.backup", "."],
            cwd=self.repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(proc.stdout.splitlines(), [])

    def test_contacts_backup_permission_file_is_renamed(self):
        self.assertTrue(
            (self.repo / "contactsbackup/default-permissions_app.grapheneos.backup.contacts.xml").is_file())
        self.assertFalse(
            (self.repo / "contactsbackup/default-permissions_org.calyxos.backup.contacts.xml").exists())
        self.assertIn(
            "default-permissions_app.grapheneos.backup.contacts",
            self.read("contactsbackup/Android.bp"))
        self.assertIn(
            'applicationId = "app.grapheneos.backup.contacts"',
            self.read("contactsbackup/build.gradle.kts"))


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""The experimental series must apply after the stable series and stay in sync."""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import shutil
import subprocess
import unittest

from harness import (PATCH_ROOT, STABLE_PATCH_ROOT, VENDOR, build_sandbox,
                     series_for)


class TestExperimentalSeries(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_reset_driver_includes_rename_destinations(self):
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
            "lenos_patch_tool", VENDOR / "tools/lenos-patch.py")
        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
        patch = (PATCH_ROOT / "packages_apps_Seedvault"
                 / "0001-grapheneos-app-id-prefix.patch")
        created = set(module.created_paths(patch))
        self.assertIn(
            "contactsbackup/default-permissions_app.grapheneos.backup.contacts.xml",
            created)
        self.assertIn(
            "storage/lib/src/main/java/app/grapheneos/backup/storage/restore/FileSplitter.kt",
            created)

    def test_settings_series_applies_in_series_order(self):
        """The Settings patches must apply after stable and in series order."""
        project = "packages/apps/Settings"
        experimental = series_for(project, PATCH_ROOT)
        sandbox = build_sandbox(project, experimental, apply_extra=False)
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, sandbox, ignore_errors=True)
        for patch in experimental:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                ["git", "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", str(patch)],
                cwd=sandbox, capture_output=True, text=True)
            self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0,
                             f"{patch.name} failed after earlier Settings patches:\n"
                             f"{proc.stderr}")

    def test_default_root_has_no_experimental_patches(self):
        for name in (
                "0001-system-app-update-verity.patch",
                "0001-crash-log-viewer.patch",
                "0001-bootloader-unlocked-warning.patch",
                "0001-grapheneos-app-id-prefix.patch",
                "0001-hardened-thread-stacks.patch"):
            self.assertEqual(list(STABLE_PATCH_ROOT.rglob(name)), [], name)

"""Static checks for the post-build and read-only device verification scripts."""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import unittest

from harness import VENDOR


class TestVerificationScripts(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_scripts_are_present_and_executable(self):
        for name in ("verify-build.sh", "verify-device.sh"):
            path = VENDOR / "tools" / name
            self.assertTrue(path.is_file(), name)
            self.assertTrue(os.access(path, os.X_OK), f"{name} is not executable")

    def test_scripts_do_not_flash_or_change_the_device(self):
        forbidden = (
            "fastboot", "flash ", "flashall", "erase ", "wipe", "reboot",
            "settings put", "pm clear", "pm uninstall", "am force-stop",
            "cmd usb set", "svc wifi", "svc data", "rm -rf",
        )
        for name in ("verify-build.sh", "verify-device.sh"):
            # Comments explain what the script does not do; only inspect executable lines.
            lines = [line for line in
                     (VENDOR / "tools" / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
                     if not line.lstrip().startswith("#")]
            body = "\n".join(lines).lower()
            for needle in forbidden:
                self.assertNotIn(needle, body, f"{name} contains {needle!r}")

    def test_device_probes_are_read_only(self):
        body = (VENDOR / "tools" / "verify-device.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for needle in ("getprop", "settings get secure", "dumpsys usb", "pm path",
                       "dmesg_restrict", "/proc/config.gz",
                       "ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks"):
            self.assertIn(needle, body)
        self.assertIn("made no changes", body)

    def test_build_script_checks_expected_artifacts(self):
        body = (VENDOR / "tools" / "verify-build.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for needle in ("framework.jar", "Settings/Settings.apk", "LenosOpsec",
                       "Seedvault", "system.img",
                       "ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks"):
            self.assertIn(needle, body)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
