"""Auto reboot to before-first-unlock (init + frameworks/base + vendor/lenos).

Feature contract (see docs/features.md), ported from GrapheneOS:
* init owns the timer (system/core/init/property_service.cpp). The framework
  special-cases ``sys.auto_reboot_ctl`` so system_server can arm it without
  a binder service: the value is the timeout in seconds, or
  ``on_device_unlocked`` to cancel.
* The timer uses CLOCK_BOOTTIME_ALARM (counts through suspend), and on
  expiry init performs a normal ``reboot`` via HandlePowerctlMessage.
* Requests that arrive before the device has been unlocked at least once
  are ignored (BFU handling: the timer must never reboot a device the user
  has not yet used this boot).
* A running timer is not restarted by repeated lock events; durations below
  20 seconds are clamped.
* frameworks/base (AutoReboot.java) translates keyguard showing-state
  changes for the current user into those property writes, using
  ExtSettings.AUTO_REBOOT_TIMEOUT (Settings.Global
  ``settings_reboot_after_timeout``, GrapheneOS-compatible key, 18h default).
* The lenOS security app writes the same key; the product property reports
  the init backend. There is no SettingsProvider def_* seed.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import VENDOR, LenosPatchTest

APP = "app/LenosSecurity/src/org/lenos/security/MainActivity.java"
RRO = "rro/LenosSettingsProviderOverlay/res/values/defaults.xml"
LEGACY_KEY = "lenos_auto_reboot_timeout_ms"


def read_vendor(rel: str) -> str:
    return (VENDOR / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8")

            "SIGEV_THREAD",

        )

    def test_timer_starts_with_the_property_service(self):
        body = self.text(self.SRC)

        call = body.index("auto_reboot_timer_init();", thread)

            "SystemProperties.set(SYS_PROP, Integer.toString(timeoutSeconds));",
        )

            "private final Context mContext;",
            "mContext = context;",
            "AutoReboot.onKeyguardShowingStateChanged(mContext, showing, mKeyguardState.userId);",
        )
        # A17 delivers the keyguard callback per user; the userId check in
        # IKeyguardStateCallback must drop stale callbacks before they reach
        # the forwarding method (and therefore the global timer).
        body = self.text(self.MONITOR)
        self.assertLess(body.index("if (userId != mKeyguardState.userId) return;"),
                        body.index("KeyguardServiceDelegate.this.onShowingStateChanged(showing);"))

    def test_timeout_key_and_default_match_grapheneos(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.EXTSETTINGS,
            "Settings.Global.AUTO_REBOOT_TIMEOUT",
            "TimeUnit.HOURS.toMillis(18)",
        )
        self.assert_contains(
            self.SETTINGS,
            'public static final String AUTO_REBOOT_TIMEOUT = "settings_reboot_after_timeout";',
        )

browser now needs an explicit user grant like any other app.

"""System trust store: distrusted CAs removed (see docs/features.md).

Feature contract (GrapheneOS-faithful port, commit ``14ad6bb`` of
``platform_system_ca-certificates``, June 2025):

* The system CA store ships without the Chunghwa Telecom roots (``HiPKI Root
  CA - G1`` and ``ePKI Root Certification Authority``) and the NetLock
  ``Arany (Class Gold)`` root — the same three files GrapheneOS deletes,
  following Google's 2025 Chrome root-store distrust announcement.
* The files are plain members of the ``Android.bp`` ``files/*`` glob, so the
  removal is a pure file deletion: no build-file or index edits are needed.
* The lineOS 24.0 tree still ships all three files, so this patch is a real
  behavior change, not upstream drift catching up.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest

REMOVED = (
    "files/53a1b57a.0",   # Chunghwa Telecom HiPKI Root CA - G1
    "files/60afe812.0",   # NetLock Arany (Class Gold)
    "files/9d6523ce.0",   # Chunghwa Telecom ePKI Root Certification Authority
)


class TestDistrustedCaRemoval(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "system/ca-certificates"
    PATCHES = ["0001-lenos-remove-distrusted-cas.patch"]
    EXTRA_FILES = ["Android.bp", "files/01419da9.0"]

    def test_distrusted_cas_are_gone(self):
        for rel in REMOVED:
            self.assertFalse(
                (self.sandbox / rel).exists(),
                f"{rel} is still in the system trust store")

    def test_other_cas_untouched(self):
        # Sample of an unrelated CA that must survive the patch.
        self.assertTrue((self.sandbox / "files/01419da9.0").is_file())

    def test_trust_store_glob_unchanged(self):
        self.assert_contains("Android.bp", '"files/*"')

====================================================================================================
"""Call recording baseline (Tier 2 #26).

LineageOS's Dialer already ships the call-recording behaviour the roadmap
wanted from GrapheneOS's Dialer: recording is enabled unconditionally (no
carrier/region gate), no recording tone is played, and files are written
through MediaStore to ``Recordings/Call recordings``. The Dialer is a
privileged, shared-certificate system app whose privapp allowlist grants
``CAPTURE_AUDIO_OUTPUT``, so the ``VOICE_CALL`` audio source works.

GrapheneOS's Dialer adds a larger auto-recording-by-contact subsystem
(preference store, contact modes, stale-contact cleanup jobs); that fork is
not part of the 1.0 series. These checks pin the baseline so upstream drift
cannot silently disable recording.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import unittest
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

from harness import WORKSPACE

DIALER = WORKSPACE / "packages/apps/Dialer"
CONFIG = DIALER / "java/com/android/dialer/callrecord/res/values/config.xml"
SERVICE = DIALER / "java/com/android/dialer/callrecord/impl/CallRecorderService.java"
RECORDING = DIALER / "java/com/android/dialer/callrecord/CallRecording.java"


def git_show(rel: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(DIALER), "show", f"HEAD:{rel}"],
        check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


class TestCallRecording(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_enabled_without_a_region_gate(self):
        root = ET.parse(CONFIG).getroot()
        bools = {b.get("name"): (b.text or "").strip()
                 for b in root.findall("bool")}
        self.assertEqual(bools.get("call_recording_enabled"), "true")
        body = SERVICE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn(
            "public static boolean isEnabled(Context context) {\n"
            "    return context.getResources().getBoolean(R.bool.call_recording_enabled);\n"
            "  }",
            body)

    def test_voice_call_audio_source(self):
        root = ET.parse(CONFIG).getroot()
        ints = {i.get("name"): (i.text or "").strip()
                for i in root.findall("integer")}
        # 4 == MediaRecorder.AudioSource.VOICE_CALL (uplink + downlink).
        self.assertEqual(ints.get("call_recording_audio_source"), "4")

    def test_files_go_to_the_shared_recordings_folder(self):
        body = RECORDING.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn('"Recordings/Call recordings"', body)
        self.assertIn("MediaStore.Audio.Media.RELATIVE_PATH", body)

    def test_no_recording_tone(self):
        for path in (SERVICE, RECORDING):
            self.assertNotIn(
                "ToneGenerator", path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), str(path))

    def test_privileged_dialer_can_capture_call_audio(self):
        manifest = git_show("AndroidManifest.xml")
        self.assertIn("android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO", manifest)
        self.assertIn("android.permission.CAPTURE_AUDIO_OUTPUT", manifest)
        self.assertIn("privileged: true", git_show("Android.bp"))
        whitelist = git_show("privapp_whitelist_com.android.dialer-ext.xml")
        self.assertIn(
            'name="android.permission.CAPTURE_AUDIO_OUTPUT"', whitelist)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

====================================================================================================
"""Clipboard privacy: Secure Paste stage 1 and cross-profile clipboard policy.

Feature contracts (GrapheneOS ports; see docs/graphene-porting.md sections 8,
14 and 18):

* Secure Paste stage 1. When ``ExtSettings.ALLOW_CLIPBOARD_READ_BY_DEFAULT`` is
  off, a package may only read clipboard content it owns. The default IME and
  system apps keep access, and a denied reader still gets the mime types (with
  the label stripped) so paste affordances do not disappear. Stage 1 exposes
  the global default only; GrapheneOS's per-app ``GosPackageState`` switch and
  the SystemUI paste toolbar are follow-ups.
* Cross-profile shared clipboard. The per-user Secure setting
  ``cross_profile_clipboard_access`` (GrapheneOS literal) gates exports in
  ``setPrimaryClipInternalLocked``, imports for each related profile, and
  cross-profile drag-and-drop. Default is ``FOLLOW_DEFAULT`` (stock Android
  behaviour), so the feature is opt-in.

The two features share ``ClipboardService.java`` but are separate patches;
each test class applies only its own patch, which also proves the hunks were
split correctly.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestSecurePaste(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "frameworks/base"
    PATCHES = ["0015-lenos-secure-paste.patch"]

    CLIP = "services/core/java/com/android/server/clipboard/ClipboardService.java"

    def test_gate_uses_gos_setting(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.CLIP,
            "import android.ext.settings.ExtSettings;",
            "return ExtSettings.ALLOW_CLIPBOARD_READ_BY_DEFAULT.get(getContext());",
            "private boolean clipboardReadAllowedForPackage(")

    def test_clip_owner_and_default_ime_exempt(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.CLIP,
            "if (isDefaultIme) {",
            "private static boolean isClipOwnerLocked(",
            "clipboard.primaryClipUid == uid;")

    def test_read_paths_enforce(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.CLIP,
            "final boolean readAllowedForPackage = clipboardReadAllowedForPackage(",
            "if (!readAllowedForPackage && !isClipOwnerLocked(clipboard, intendingUid))",
            "new ClipDescription(null, mimeTypes)",
            "return descriptionWithoutLabel;")

    def test_denied_read_keeps_presence_signal(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.CLIP,
            "does not expose clip content",
            "if (!readAllowedForPackage && !isClipOwnerLocked(clipboard, intendingUid)) {")

    def test_foreign_import_does_not_leak_cross_profile_class(self):
        # The import block belongs to the Secure Paste patch; the cross-profile
        # patch uses fully-qualified names so the two patches stay independent.
        self.assert_not_contains(
            self.CLIP,
            "import android.ext.settings.CrossProfileClipboardAccessSettings;")

    def test_syntax(self):
        self.assert_java_syntax(self.CLIP)


class TestCrossProfileClipboard(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "frameworks/base"
    PATCHES = ["0016-lenos-cross-profile-clipboard.patch"]

    CLIP = "services/core/java/com/android/server/clipboard/ClipboardService.java"
    SETTINGS_CLASS = ("core/java/android/ext/settings/"
                      "CrossProfileClipboardAccessSettings.java")
    DRAG = "services/core/java/com/android/server/wm/DragState.java"

    def test_policy_class_matches_grapheneos(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.SETTINGS_CLASS,
            "Settings.Secure.CROSS_PROFILE_CLIPBOARD_ACCESS",
            "public static final int FOLLOW_DEFAULT = 0;",
            "public static final int ALLOW_IMPORT_DEFAULTS_ONLY = 1;",
            "public static final int ALLOW_EXPORT_DEFAULTS_ONLY = 2;",
            "public static final int BLOCK = 3;",
            "public static boolean isExportAccessAllowed(",
            "public static boolean isImportAccessAllowed(")

    def test_export_gate_runs_before_related_profiles(self):
        self.assert_contains(self.CLIP, "isExportAccessAllowed(getContext(), userId)")
        body = self.text(self.CLIP)
        self.assertLess(body.index("isExportAccessAllowed(getContext(), userId)"),
                        body.index("// Update related users"))

    def test_import_gate_is_per_related_profile(self):
        self.assert_contains(self.CLIP, "isImportAccessAllowed(getContext(), id)")

    def test_drag_and_drop_gate(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.DRAG,
            "isExportAccessAllowed(mCurrentDisplayContent.mAtmService.mContext,",
            "mCrossProfileCopyAllowed = false;")

    def test_syntax(self):
        self.assert_java_syntax(self.CLIP)
        self.assert_java_syntax(self.SETTINGS_CLASS)
        self.assert_java_syntax(self.DRAG)

section 9):

"""Device-tree hardening configuration for the Nothing Phone (3a)/(3a) Pro.

Feature contract (see docs/features.md):
* Enterprise Wi-Fi without certificate validation cannot be configured from
  Settings/SetupWizard.
* Tethering does not advertise a device-identifying SSID.
* Default radio mode has no 2G (stingray/IMSI-catcher attack surface), and does
  not hard-disable any other RAT.
* The default device name (Bluetooth adapter / Wi-Fi Direct) is generic, not
  the commercial model.
* More profiles than stock are allowed (GrapheneOS parity: 32 full users).
* The lenOS product inherits the Lineage device config.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestDeviceConfig(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "device/nothing/asteroids"
    PATCHES = [
        "0001-add-lenos-product.patch",
        "0002-wifi-privacy-hardening.patch",
        "0004-default-network-without-2g.patch",
        "0006-privacy-device-name.patch",
        "0007-multiuser-max-users.patch",
    ]
    PRODUCT = "lenos_asteroids.mk"
    WIFI = "rro_overlays/AsteroidsWifiOverlay/res/values/config.xml"
    PROPS = "system_ext.prop"
    DEVICE_NAME = "rro_overlays/AsteroidsSettingsProviderOverlay/res/values/defaults.xml"
    DEVICE_NAME_PRO = "rro_overlays/AsteroidsProSettingsProviderOverlay/res/values/defaults.xml"
    MULTIUSER = "rro_overlays/FrameworksResCommon_Vendor/res/values/config.xml"

    def test_xml_files_are_well_formed(self):
        self.assert_xml(self.WIFI)
        self.assert_xml(self.DEVICE_NAME)
        self.assert_xml(self.DEVICE_NAME_PRO)
        self.assert_xml(self.MULTIUSER)

    def test_lenos_product_inherits_lineage_and_vendor_config(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.PRODUCT,
            "$(call inherit-product, device/nothing/asteroids/lineage_asteroids.mk)",
            "$(call inherit-product, vendor/lenos/config/lenos.mk)",
            "PRODUCT_NAME := lenos_asteroids",
            "PRODUCT_DEVICE := asteroids",
        )

    def test_minimal_app_set_is_configured_before_inheriting(self):
        # LENOS_STRIP_PACKAGES/TARGET_EXCLUDES_AUDIOFX must be set in the
        # product makefile (before the inherit calls) to be visible to
        # vendor/lineage's app lists.
        body = self.text(self.PRODUCT)
        strip_at = body.index("LENOS_STRIP_PACKAGES :=")
        audiofx_at = body.index("TARGET_EXCLUDES_AUDIOFX := true")
        inherit_at = body.index("$(call inherit-product, device/nothing/asteroids/")
        self.assertLess(strip_at, inherit_at)
        self.assertLess(audiofx_at, inherit_at)
        self.assertIn("Gallery2", body[strip_at:inherit_at])

    def test_product_is_registered_for_lunch(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            "AndroidProducts.mk",
            "$(LOCAL_DIR)/lenos_asteroids.mk",
        )

    def test_product_does_not_change_the_build_fingerprint(self):
        # Device identity must stay stock (attestation/app compatibility).
        self.assert_not_contains(
            self.PRODUCT,
            "PRODUCT_BUILD_PROP_OVERRIDES",
            "BUILD_FINGERPRINT",
            "ro.product.name",
        )

    def test_insecure_enterprise_wifi_is_disabled(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.WIFI,
            '<bool name="config_wifiAllowInsecureEnterpriseConfigurationsForSettingsAndSUW">false</bool>',
        )

    def test_tether_ssid_is_generic(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.WIFI,
            '<string translatable="false" name="wifi_tether_configure_ssid_default">AndroidAP</string>',
        )

    def test_default_network_mode_excludes_2g(self):
        # 28 = NR+LTE+WCDMA: no GSM/2G, WCDMA kept so roaming still works.
        self.assert_contains(self.PROPS, "ro.telephony.default_network=28,28")

    def test_default_device_name_is_generic(self):
        # The device name is what Bluetooth/Wi-Fi Direct neighbour devices see.
        for rel in (self.DEVICE_NAME, self.DEVICE_NAME_PRO):
            self.assert_contains(
                rel,
                '<string name="def_device_name">Android</string>',
                '<string name="def_device_name_simple">Android</string>',

"""GrapheneOS: no DHCP state reuse under per-connection MAC randomization (#14).

The Wi-Fi privacy port (`wifi/0001`) makes per-connection randomized MACs the
default, but AOSP's DHCP client still renews the lease it cached in
``IpMemoryStore`` for the same L2 network (``DhcpClient``'s
``EVENT_CONFIGURATION_OBTAINED`` → ``INIT-REBOOT`` path). The DHCP server then
sees the same requested address from a "new" device and can link the two
connections — which defeats the point of the fresh MAC.

GrapheneOS fixed this in 2021 ("prevent DHCP (IPv4) from reusing state across
connections to the same network when full MAC randomization is enabled") and
still ships the patch on branch 17, so LineageOS 24.0 (which lacks it) gets the
port here:

* when the lease from the memory store has not expired, the client checks the
  connected network's MAC randomization mode; for per-connection randomization
  (``RANDOMIZATION_ALWAYS``) it starts from DISCOVER instead of renewing;
* the check runs inside the NetworkStack process, which holds
  ``NETWORK_STACK`` — the Wi-Fi service grants that a scan-results/location
  bypass, so the configured-network lookup works without location permission;
* any failure (WifiManager missing, lookup denied, network not in the list)
  conservatively avoids reuse, which is privacy-safe but costs an extra DHCP
  exchange, never correctness.

Other randomization modes (device MAC, per-network persistent) keep the
upstream fast-renewal path unchanged.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestDhcpStateReuse(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "packages/modules/NetworkStack"
    PATCHES = ["0001-lenos-dhcp-no-state-reuse.patch"]

    DHCP = "src/android/net/dhcp/DhcpClient.java"

    def test_lease_expiry_check_also_avoids_reuse(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.DHCP,
            "if (currentTime >= attributes.assignedV4AddressExpiry "
            "|| shouldAvoidStateReuse()) {",
            "// Lease has expired.",
            "transitionTo(mDhcpInitState);")

    def test_randomization_always_constant(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.DHCP, "private static final int RANDOMIZATION_ALWAYS = 100;")

    def test_queries_the_connected_networks_mode(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.DHCP,
            "wifiInfo.getNetworkId()",
            "wifiManager.getConfiguredNetworks()",
            "configuration.macRandomizationSetting == RANDOMIZATION_ALWAYS")

    def test_failure_falls_back_to_avoiding_reuse(self):
        # The catch-all must end in `return true` (avoid reuse), otherwise a
        # denied lookup would silently restore the leak.
        self.assert_contains(
            self.DHCP,
            "} catch (Exception e) {",
            'loge("ConfiguredNetworks should contain Connected network id config");',
            "return true;")

    def test_wifi_imports_present(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.DHCP,
            "import android.net.wifi.WifiConfiguration;",
            "import android.net.wifi.WifiInfo;",
            "import android.net.wifi.WifiManager;",
            "import java.util.ArrayList;")

    def test_upstream_lease_handling_kept(self):
        # The upstream store/renew path must still exist: this patch only adds
        # a condition, it does not replace the lease bookkeeping.
        self.assert_contains(
            self.DHCP,
            "mIpMemoryStore.retrieveNetworkAttributes(mConfiguration.l2Key, listener);",
            "transitionTo(mDhcpInitRebootState);",
            "mLastAssignedIpv4Address = attributes.assignedV4Address;")

    def test_balanced(self):
        self.assert_balanced(self.DHCP)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""GrapheneOS: user-installed apps can be disabled (not only system apps).

GrapheneOS's app info screen offers the Disable action for user-installed
apps, so an app can be completely prevented from running without uninstalling
it and losing its data. Disabling is stricter than Force stop, which only
stops an app until something else starts one of its components again.

The feature is a Settings change; the framework already allows it:

* ``PackageManagerService.setEnabledSettings`` has no system-app restriction
  for ``COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DISABLED_USER`` (verified by the second test
  class, which pins that invariant).
* Settings shares ``android.uid.system``, which holds
  ``android.permission.CHANGE_COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE``
  (``signature|privileged``) for other packages.

Ported from GrapheneOS's ``AppDisableButton.kt``:

* ``getActionButton`` no longer returns early for non-system apps; it keys on
  ``app.installed`` like GrapheneOS (archived apps keep using the
  archive/restore flow).
* ``canBeDisabled`` gained GrapheneOS's first branch
  ``!isSystemApp -> appButtonRepository.isAllowUninstallOrArchive(...)``: a
  user app that can be uninstalled or archived can also be disabled, and
  blocks such as ``DISALLOW_APPS_CONTROL`` still apply.
* Clicking Disable on a user app disables it directly (``disable()`` still
  requires user authentication); the confirmation dialog stays for system
  apps, where disabling downgrades to the system version and destroys data.

Documented deviations:

* The SPA app info screen is the one shipped and default on LineageOS 24.0
  (``settings_enable_spa`` defaults to true), which is where GrapheneOS has
  the feature too. The legacy ``AppButtonsPreferenceController`` screen keeps
  its stock behavior of offering Disable only for system apps — it is
  unmodified in GrapheneOS as well.
* GrapheneOS's A17 dialog gained an HSU (headless system user) warning
  title/message; LineageOS 24.0 has that dialog, and user apps skip it
  entirely, so the dialog is unchanged here.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestDisableUserApps(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "packages/apps/Settings"
    PATCHES = ["0002-lenos-disable-user-apps.patch"]

    FILE = "src/com/android/settings/spa/app/appinfo/AppDisableButton.kt"

    def test_button_offered_for_all_installed_apps(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.FILE,
            "import com.android.settingslib.spaprivileged.model.app.installed",
            "if (!app.installed) return null")
        # The stock system-app gate must be gone.
        self.assert_not_contains(self.FILE, "if (!app.isSystemApp) return null")

    def test_user_app_disable_follows_uninstall_rules(self):
        text = self.text(self.FILE)
        self.assert_contains(
            self.FILE,
            "!isSystemApp -> appButtonRepository.isAllowUninstallOrArchive(context, this)")
        # Placed before the system-app safety checks, like GrapheneOS.
        start = text.index("private fun ApplicationInfo.canBeDisabled")
        user_branch = text.index("!isSystemApp ->", start)
        platform_check = text.index("isSignedWithPlatformKey -> false", start)
        self.assertLess(user_branch, platform_check)

    def test_user_app_disable_skips_the_data_loss_dialog(self):
        text = self.text(self.FILE)

        direct = body.index("packageInfoPresenter.disable()", system_branch)
        self.assertLess(system_branch, dialog)
        self.assertLess(dialog, direct)
        # The system-app confirmation dialog itself is untouched.
        self.assert_contains(

            "stringResource(R.string.app_disable_dlg_positive)",
            "R.string.app_disable_dlg_text")

    def test_enable_stays_available_for_disabled_apps(self):

    def test_syntax(self):
        self.assert_balanced(self.FILE)

    generic guards (caller permission, protected packages).

"""lenOS duress credentials (frameworks/base LockSettingsService port).

Feature contract (see docs/features.md):
* Entering the duress PIN or the duress password at any credential prompt
  destroys the KeyMint storage keys + Secretkeeper secrets (user data becomes
  cryptographically inaccessible) and powers the device off. There is no way
  back.
* Only failed verifications are checked, and only typed PIN/password
  credentials: the normal lock credential can never trigger the wipe, and a
  correct credential is ignored.
* Managing the pair (set/check/delete) requires the owner credential; the
  stored form is a scrypt-stretched hash, never the credential itself.
* Ported from GrapheneOS, including the eSIM profile erasure (EuiccWipe) and
  the suppressed carrier removal notification; the eUICC-side contract is
  covered by test_duress_esim.py. The shell test hook
  (cmd lock_settings set-duress-credentials) supports on-device verification.

"""Duress eSIM wipe (GrapheneOS EuiccWipe port).

Feature contract (see docs/features.md):
* Entering a duress credential erases every profile on every eUICC before the
  device powers off. The cryptographic erase (KeyMint keys + Secretkeeper)
  happens regardless and never waits for the eUICC; the eSIM wipe runs on its
  own thread with a 3 second budget.
* EuiccWipe (frameworks/base, internal telephony package) enumerates
  TelephonyManager#getUiccSlotsInfo and, for every eUICC slot, calls
  EuiccCardManager#resetMemory with RESET_OPTION_DELETE_OPERATIONAL_PROFILES |
  RESET_OPTION_DELETE_FIELD_LOADED_TEST_PROFILES, waits for all callbacks and
  reports success only if every reset returned RESULT_OK.
* The @hide EuiccCardManager#resetMemory(..., flags) overload +
  RESET_FLAG_IS_FOR_DURESS_WIPE=1 are the only new surface; the public 4-arg
  API delegates with flags=0.
* EuiccCardController (frameworks/opt/telephony) only honors flags from
  SYSTEM_UID (others get a SecurityException) and, when the duress flag is
  set, skips updateEmbeddedSubscriptions() so the carrier does not receive an
  eSIM removal notification while the device is being wiped.
* The IEuiccCardController AIDL carries the flags argument, keeping the phone
  process implementation and the framework API in sync.
"""

* the driver only applies/installs experimental inputs when
  ``LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL=1``;
* the product makefile only inherits the experimental fragment under the same
  flag, and the default product does not name ``LenosOpsec``.

These are source-level checks. They do not build, boot, flash or validate any
experimental feature.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from harness import VENDOR

TOOL = VENDOR / "tools/lenos-patch.py"
STABLE = VENDOR / "patches"
EXPERIMENTAL = VENDOR / "patches-experimental"
EXPECTED_PROJECTS = {
    "bionic",
    "frameworks/base",
    "packages/apps/Settings",
    "packages/apps/SetupWizard",
    "packages/apps/Seedvault",
}


def series_entries(project_dir: Path) -> list[str]:
    return [line.strip() for line in (project_dir / "series").read_text().splitlines()
            if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("#")]


class TestExperimentalLayout(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_patch_root_exists_and_has_no_stray_patches(self):
        self.assertTrue(EXPERIMENTAL.is_dir(), EXPERIMENTAL)
        actual_projects = set()
        for pdir in sorted(EXPERIMENTAL.iterdir()):
            if not pdir.is_dir():
                continue
            series = pdir / "series"
            self.assertTrue(series.is_file(), f"{pdir.name} has no series file")
            actual_projects.add(pdir.name)
            listed = set(series_entries(pdir))
            present = {p.name for p in pdir.glob("*.patch")}
            self.assertEqual(present - listed, set(),
                             f"{pdir.name}: patches not in series: {sorted(present - listed)}")
            self.assertEqual(listed - present, set(),
                             f"{pdir.name}: series lists missing patches: {sorted(listed - present)}")
        self.assertEqual(actual_projects, {p.replace("/", "_") for p in EXPECTED_PROJECTS})

    def test_no_duplicate_file_blocks_in_experimental_patches(self):
        # A duplicated new-file diff applies once but cannot be reversed: the
        # first reverse deletes the file and the second one fails. That breaks
        # reset/idempotence, so reject it at source level.
        for patch in EXPERIMENTAL.rglob("*.patch"):
            seen: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = {}
            for lineno, line in enumerate(
                    patch.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(), 1):
                if not line.startswith("diff --git "):
                    continue
                parts = line.split()
                if len(parts) >= 4:
                    key = (parts[2], parts[3])
                    seen[key] = seen.get(key, 0) + 1
            duplicates = {k: n for k, n in seen.items() if n > 1}
            self.assertEqual(duplicates, {}, f"{patch}: duplicate file blocks {duplicates}")

    def test_no_experimental_patch_in_the_stable_root(self):
        stable_files = {p.name for p in STABLE.rglob("*.patch")}
        for unexpected in (
                "0001-system-app-update-verity.patch",
                "0001-crash-log-viewer.patch",
                "0001-bootloader-unlocked-warning.patch",
                "0001-grapheneos-app-id-prefix.patch",
                "0001-hardened-thread-stacks.patch"):
            self.assertNotIn(unexpected, stable_files)

    def test_all_experimental_patches_apply_after_stable_context(self):
        # The one conflict found when stacking the series was ClipboardService's
        # import block: stable Secure Paste adds ApplicationInfo. Keep that
        # rebased context explicit so a future regeneration cannot silently
        # drop the stable-base requirement.
        patch = (EXPERIMENTAL / "frameworks_base"
                 / "0004-clipboard-clear-on-screen-off.patch")
        body = patch.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("+import android.content.IntentFilter;", body)
        self.assertIn(" import android.content.pm.ApplicationInfo;", body)

    def test_experimental_setup_wizard_and_seedvault_aliases_are_mapped(self):
        sys.path.insert(0, str(VENDOR / "tools"))
        from lenos_projects import alias_for  # noqa: PLC0415
        self.assertEqual(alias_for("packages/apps/SetupWizard"),
                         "packages_apps_SetupWizard")
        self.assertEqual(alias_for("packages/apps/Seedvault"),
                         "packages_apps_Seedvault")


class TestProductGate(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_default_product_does_not_name_experimental_packages(self):
        body = (VENDOR / "config/lenos.mk").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertNotIn("LenosOpsec", body)
        # The fragment is guarded by the normalized build flag.
        self.assertIn(
            "ifneq ($(filter 1 true yes,$(LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL)),)", body)
        self.assertIn(
            "$(call inherit-product, vendor/lenos/config/lenos-experimental.mk)",
            body)

    def test_experimental_fragment_is_the_only_place_with_the_app(self):
        body = (VENDOR / "config/lenos-experimental.mk").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("LenosOpsec", body)
        self.assertIn("ro.lenos.experimental=1", body)
        self.assertNotIn("LenosOpsec", (VENDOR / "config/lenos.mk").read_text())

    def test_hardened_thread_stacks_are_part_of_the_experimental_series(self):
        fragment = (VENDOR / "config/lenos-experimental.mk").read_text()
        self.assertIn("ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks=1", fragment)
        # It is part of the experimental fragment, not a second build gate.
        self.assertNotIn("LENOS_HARDENED_THREAD_STACKS", fragment)
        # A stable/default build has neither the property nor the bionic gate.
        stable = (VENDOR / "config/lenos.mk").read_text()
        self.assertNotIn("ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks", stable)
        self.assertNotIn("LENOS_HARDENED_THREAD_STACKS", stable)

    def test_driver_reports_hardened_stacks_without_a_second_flag(self):
        body = (VENDOR / "lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh").read_text()
        self.assertNotIn("LENOS_HARDENED_THREAD_STACKS", body)
        for needle in (
                "__allocate_hardened_thread_mapping",
                "ro.lenos.hardened_thread_stacks=1",
                "hardened thread stacks"):
            self.assertIn(needle, body)

    def test_experimental_app_source_is_opt_in_and_local_only(self):
        app = VENDOR / "experimental/app/LenosOpsec"
        self.assertTrue((app / "Android.bp").is_file())
        manifest = (app / "AndroidManifest.xml").read_text()
        self.assertNotIn("android.permission.INTERNET", manifest)
        for rel in (app / "src/org/lenos/opsec").glob("*.java"):
            body = rel.read_text()
            self.assertNotIn("java.net.", body, rel)
            self.assertNotIn("HttpURLConnection", body, rel)
            self.assertNotIn("Socket", body, rel)

    def test_driver_gates_patch_application_and_app_install(self):
        body = (VENDOR / "lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh").read_text()
        for needle in (
                "experimental_enabled()",
                'export LENOS_EXPERIMENTAL="$experimental"',
                "--experimental --reset",
                "--experimental --check",
                "--experimental --apply",
                'cp -a "$VENDOR/experimental/app/." "$SRC/vendor/lenos/app/"',
                "experimental app present in a stable build tree"):
            self.assertIn(needle, body)

    def test_driver_detects_experimental_before_reset_and_validates_stable_first(self):
        body = (VENDOR / "lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh").read_text()
        detect = body.index('exp_status="$(python3 "$VENDOR/tools/lenos-patch.py"')
        wizard_reset = body.index('"$WIZARD" reset hardening')
        stable_gate = body.index('info "patchkit --require-applied"')
        exp_apply = body.index("--experimental --apply")
        self.assertLess(detect, wizard_reset,
                        "experimental state must be detected before the reset")
        self.assertLess(stable_gate, exp_apply,
                        "stable series must be validated before experimental apply")

    def test_driver_is_shell_syntax_clean(self):
        proc = subprocess.run(["bash", "-n", str(VENDOR / "lenos-1.0-shizuku.sh")],
                              capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr)


class TestPatchToolModes(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_list(self, *args: str) -> list[str]:
        proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(TOOL), "--list", *args],
                              capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr)
        return [line for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]

    def test_experimental_list_has_only_opt_in_projects(self):
        lines = self.run_list("--experimental")
        projects = {line.split("\t", 1)[0] for line in lines}
        self.assertEqual(projects, EXPECTED_PROJECTS)
        self.assertEqual(len(lines), 13)
        self.assertIn("bionic\t0001-hardened-thread-stacks.patch", lines)
        self.assertIn("frameworks/base\t0001-system-app-update-verity.patch", lines)
        self.assertIn("packages/apps/Settings\t0005-native-debugging-block.patch", lines)
        self.assertFalse(any(line.startswith("vendor/lenos\t") for line in lines))

    def test_stable_list_does_not_include_experimental_projects(self):
        projects = {line.split("\t", 1)[0] for line in self.run_list()}
        self.assertNotIn("packages/apps/SetupWizard", projects)
        self.assertNotIn("packages/apps/Seedvault", projects)

    def test_experimental_app_is_present_as_source_not_a_patch(self):
        self.assertTrue((VENDOR / "experimental/app/LenosOpsec/Android.bp").is_file())
        self.assertFalse((EXPERIMENTAL / "vendor_lenos").exists())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

FILE 182/217: tests/test_fbe_padding.py
====================================================================================================
"""FBE filename padding of 32 bytes (see docs/features.md).

Feature contract (GrapheneOS-faithful port, commit ``pad filenames to 32
bytes instead of 16 or 4 bytes`` on ``platform_system_extras``):

* Every file-based-encryption policy this build creates requests the maximum
  ``FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_32`` filename padding, instead of AOSP's
  context-dependent 16 (and 4 for pre-R v1 policies). 32-byte padding hides
  filename lengths better. The pre-R compatibility branch is removed
  entirely: the device tree pins ``PRODUCT_SHIPPING_API_LEVEL := 35`` so it
  could never be taken, and lenOS has no shipped installs to stay compatible
  with.
* The lock-library consumers (`vold` links ``libfscrypt``) pick the flags up
  through ``ParseOptionsForApiLevel``; the padding is derived, never parsed
  from or serialized into the options string, so option-string round trips
  are unaffected.
* The in-tree ``fscrypt_test`` expectations are updated to ``PAD_32`` to
  match the ported behavior. GrapheneOS's fork changed the code but left its
  copy of the test file stale — documented, no behavior delta.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestFbePadding(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "system/extras"
    PATCHES = ["0001-lenos-fbe-pad-32.patch"]
    SRC = "libfscrypt/fscrypt.cpp"
    TEST = "libfscrypt/tests/fscrypt_test.cpp"

    def test_every_policy_requests_pad32(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.SRC,
            "options->flags |= FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_32;")
        self.assert_not_contains(
            self.SRC,
            "FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_16",
            "FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_4",
            "first_api_level <= __ANDROID_API_Q__ && options->version == 1")

    def test_unit_test_expectations_match(self):
        self.assert_contains(self.TEST, "FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_32")
        self.assert_not_contains(
            self.TEST,
            "FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_16",
            "FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_4")

    def test_block_size_selection_unchanged(self):
        # The v1/v2 policy-version selection (first_api_level vs Q) is
        # untouched; only the padding branch is replaced.
        self.assert_contains(
            self.SRC,
            "options->version = first_api_level > __ANDROID_API_Q__ ? 2 : 1;")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""GrapheneOS firmware-security visibility (engineering-unit warning, bootloader field).

Ported from GrapheneOS's "Other features":

* "Engineering/Prototype ("EVT", "PVT" or "DVT") device warning as these devices
  typically have relaxed security controls for development" — a persistent
  notification posted from ``ActivityManagerService`` at boot.
* "Improved user visibility into persistent firmware security" — the
  bootloader version field in Settings > About phone > Firmware version.

Documented deviations from GrapheneOS:

* GrapheneOS detects prototypes on Pixels via ``ro.revision`` and
  ``ro.boot.secure_boot`` and returns early for every other OEM. lenOS keeps
  that Pixel logic verbatim and adds a phase-marker path for other OEMs
  (Nothing/Qualcomm): an explicit EVT/PVT/DVT marker in one of the bootloader
  hardware-phase properties. Unknown or plain revision values never warn, so
  the notification cannot false-positive on retail units.
* The AOSP "Serial console is enabled" notification already ships in LineageOS,
  so only the prototype notification is added.
* The pre-Treble ``ro.build.expect.bootloader`` / ``ro.build.expect.baseband``
  build-consistency checks GrapheneOS enabled in 2017 were removed upstream
  once devices became Treble/VINTF-verified; ``Build.isBuildConsistent()`` and
  the ``showSystemReadyErrorDialogsIfNeeded`` mismatch dialog already exist in
  LineageOS, so there is nothing to port for the "version and fingerprint
  checks" part beyond the visibility field.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestPrototypeWarning(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "frameworks/base"
    PATCHES = ["0023-lenos-prototype-device-warning.patch"]

    STRINGS = "core/res/res/values/strings.xml"
    PROTO = "proto/src/system_messages.proto"
    AMS = "services/core/java/com/android/server/am/ActivityManagerService.java"

    def test_notification_strings(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.STRINGS,
            '<string name="prototype_device_notification_title">'
            "Device is an engineering prototype</string>",
            '<string name="prototype_device_notification_message">'
            "Device security may be affected.</string>")

    def test_system_message_id(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.PROTO,
            "// Inform the user that the device appears to be a prototype.",
            "NOTE_PROTOTYPE_DETECTED = 400;")
        # The new note is registered after the last stock note and before the
        # legacy-ID boundary of that same block, like the other post-O notes,
        # so ids stay stable.
        text = self.text(self.PROTO)
        start = text.index("NOTE_PROTOTYPE_DETECTED = 400;")
        self.assertLess(text.index("NOTE_WRONG_HSUM_STATUS = 77;"), start)
        self.assertGreater(
            text.index("ADD_NEW_IDS_ABOVE_THIS_LINE", start), start)

    def test_grapheneos_pixel_logic_verbatim(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.AMS,
            "private static boolean isPrototypeDevice() {",
            'switch (Build.BRAND) {',
            'case "google":',
            "// Other OEMs may deal with hardware revisions differently",
            'if (!SystemProperties.get("ro.revision").contains("MP")) {',
            'if (!SystemProperties.get("ro.boot.secure_boot").equals("PRODUCTION")) {')

    def test_non_pixel_phase_markers(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.AMS,
            '"ro.boot.hwlevel",',
            '"ro.boot.hardware.revision",',
            '"ro.boot.device_release",',
            'value.contains("EVT") || value.contains("PVT") '
            '|| value.contains("DVT")')

    def test_call_site_is_boot_completion(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.AMS,
            "// UART is on if init's console service is running, "
            "send a warning notification.",
            "showConsoleNotificationIfActive();\n"
            "        showMteOverrideNotificationIfActive();\n"
            "        // If device is not a mass production (MP) variant, "
            "send a warning notification.\n"
            "        showPrototypeNotificationIfPrototype();")

    def test_notification_is_persistent_and_public(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.AMS,
            "private void showPrototypeNotificationIfPrototype() {",
            "getString(com.android.internal.R.string."
            "prototype_device_notification_title)",
            "getString(com.android.internal.R.string."
            "prototype_device_notification_message)",
            "new Notification.Builder(mContext, "
            "SystemNotificationChannels.DEVELOPER)",
            ".setOngoing(true)",
            ".setVisibility(Notification.VISIBILITY_PUBLIC)",
            "SystemMessage.NOTE_PROTOTYPE_DETECTED, notification, "
            "UserHandle.ALL);")

    def test_console_notification_untouched(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.AMS,
            'if (!SystemProperties.get("init.svc.console").equals("running")) {',
            "SystemMessage.NOTE_SERIAL_CONSOLE_ENABLED, notification, "
            "UserHandle.ALL);")
        # lenOS does not add a second cmdline-based UART heuristic: AOSP's
        # init-service check is already accurate on every device, including
        # Nothing/Qualcomm units whose bootloaders don't use the Pixel-style
        # "console=null" convention.
        self.assert_not_contains(self.AMS, "/proc/cmdline")
        self.assertEqual(
            self.text(self.AMS).count(
                "private void showConsoleNotificationIfActive() {"), 1)

    def test_syntax(self):
        self.assert_java_syntax(self.AMS)
        self.assert_xml(self.STRINGS)

* ``core/java/android/ext/settings/GnssSettings.java`` — the SUPL and PSDS

  PSDS downloads when PSDS is disabled.

* GrapheneOS defaults SUPL and PSDS to its own privacy proxies and lets users
  choose "GrapheneOS proxy"; lenOS has no such infrastructure, so only
  "Off" and "Standard server" are offered.
* Both settings default to **Off**. With no proxy, disabling is the only
  privacy-preserving default; the user can opt back into the standard servers.
* The location-screen rows live in their own "Network assistance" category
  instead of GrapheneOS's advanced category, which LineageOS removes when the
  new recent-location UI is disabled.

``gps.supl_host``) was removed: the framework setting now owns SUPL, so the
"Standard server" choice is not silently defeated by an empty host.

from harness import LenosPatchTest

        "0021-lenos-gnss-network-assistance.patch",

            self.GNSS,
            "SUPL_SERVER_STANDARD = 0",
            "SUPL_DISABLED = 1",
            "PSDS_SERVER_STANDARD = 1",
            "PSDS_DISABLED = 2",
            "SUPL_SETTING = new IntSetting(",
            "STANDARD_PSDS_SETTING = new IntSetting(",

"""Kernel hardening fragment (Tier 3 #32).

lenOS ships an additive 6.6 GKI config fragment for the portable subset of
GrapheneOS's kernel hardening. It is merged last by ``TARGET_KERNEL_CONFIG``
and only enables options that need no vendor firmware, module re-signing or
device-specific validation. The larger pieces (48-bit VA / 4-level page
tables, forced module signing + lockdown, GrapheneOS's allocator canaries and
MTE-for-apps) remain out of scope and are documented in
``docs/graphene-porting.md`` section 19.

These tests pin the option set, prove each symbol exists in the pinned kernel
tree, and check that the fragment is wired into the device build.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import subprocess
import unittest

from harness import VENDOR, WORKSPACE, LenosPatchTest, patch_paths
from lenos_projects import alias_for, project_for

KERNEL = WORKSPACE / "kernel/nothing/sm7635"
DEVICE = WORKSPACE / "device/nothing/asteroids"

FRAGMENT = "arch/arm64/configs/vendor/lenos_hardening.config"
KERNEL_PATCH = "0001-lenos-kernel-hardening-config.patch"
DEVICE_PATCH = "0008-kernel-hardening-config.patch"

#: option -> Kconfig file that defines it (cross-checked with ``git show``).
EXPECTED = {
    "CONFIG_INIT_ON_FREE_DEFAULT_ON": "security/Kconfig.hardening",
    "CONFIG_RANDOM_KMALLOC_CACHES": "mm/Kconfig",
    "CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_KSTACK_OFFSET_DEFAULT": "arch/Kconfig",
    "CONFIG_SECURITY_DMESG_RESTRICT": "security/Kconfig",
    "CONFIG_ZERO_CALL_USED_REGS": "security/Kconfig.hardening",
}

BASE_CONFIGS = (
    "arch/arm64/configs/gki_defconfig",
    "arch/arm64/configs/vendor/pineapple_perf.config",
    "arch/arm64/configs/vendor/asteroids_perf.config",
)


class TestKernelHardeningFragment(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "kernel/nothing/sm7635"
    PATCHES = [KERNEL_PATCH]

    def options(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        body = self.text(FRAGMENT)
        return dict(re.findall(r"(?m)^(CONFIG_[A-Z0-9_]+)=(.*)$", body))

    def test_fragment_enables_exactly_the_portable_subset(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.options(), {opt: "y" for opt in EXPECTED})

    def test_fragment_is_additive_only(self):
        body = self.text(FRAGMENT)
        self.assertIn("# lenOS kernel hardening (Tier 3 #32)", body)
        self.assertNotIn("# CONFIG_", body, "fragments must not disable options")
        for forbidden in (
            "CONFIG_KASAN",
            "CONFIG_KASAN_STACK",
            "CONFIG_DEBUG_KERNEL",
            "CONFIG_MODULE_SIG",
            "CONFIG_SECURITY_LOCKDOWN",
            "CONFIG_ARM64_VA_BITS",
        ):
            self.assertNotIn(forbidden, body)

    def kconfig(self, rel: str) -> str:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(KERNEL), "show", f"HEAD:{rel}"],
            capture_output=True, text=True)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            self.skipTest(f"cannot read {rel} from the pinned kernel")
        return proc.stdout

    def test_each_option_is_defined_in_this_kernel(self):
        for opt, kconfig in EXPECTED.items():
            self.assertIn(f"config {opt.removeprefix('CONFIG_')}",
                          self.kconfig(kconfig),
                          f"{opt} is not defined in {kconfig}")

    def test_stack_zeroing_is_an_upstream_default_not_a_fragment_option(self):
        # 6.6 already defaults INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO on when the compiler
        # supports auto-var-init (the GKI Clang does), so the fragment must
        # not claim it as a lenOS delta.
        self.assertIn(
            "default INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO if CC_HAS_AUTO_VAR_INIT_ZERO",
            self.kconfig("security/Kconfig.hardening"))
        self.assertNotIn("CONFIG_INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO", self.text(FRAGMENT))

    def test_none_of_the_options_are_already_on_in_the_baseline(self):
        for rel in BASE_CONFIGS:
            body = (KERNEL / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            for opt in EXPECTED:
                self.assertNotRegex(body, rf"(?m)^{opt}=y\b",
                                    f"{opt} is already enabled in {rel}")

    def test_patch_creates_only_the_fragment(self):
        patch = VENDOR / "patches" / alias_for(self.PROJECT) / KERNEL_PATCH
        self.assertEqual(patch_paths(patch), [FRAGMENT])

    def test_kernel_project_is_registered_for_apply_and_reset(self):
        self.assertEqual(project_for("kernel_nothing_sm7635"),
                         "kernel/nothing/sm7635")


class TestKernelHardeningBoardConfig(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "device/nothing/asteroids"
    PATCHES = [DEVICE_PATCH]

    def config_lines(self) -> list[str]:
        body = self.text("BoardConfig.mk")
        match = re.search(r"(?m)^TARGET_KERNEL_CONFIG := \\\n((?:    .*\n?)+)", body)
        self.assertIsNotNone(match, "TARGET_KERNEL_CONFIG block is missing")
        return [line.rstrip(" \\") for line in match.group(1).splitlines()]

    def test_fragment_is_merged_after_the_vendor_configs(self):
        lines = self.config_lines()
        self.assertEqual(lines[-1], "    vendor/lenos_hardening.config")
        self.assertGreater(
            lines.index("    vendor/lenos_hardening.config"),
            lines.index("    vendor/asteroids_perf.config"))

    def test_patch_touches_only_boardconfig(self):
        patch = VENDOR / "patches" / alias_for(self.PROJECT) / DEVICE_PATCH
        self.assertEqual(patch_paths(patch), ["BoardConfig.mk"])

    def test_patch_is_the_last_entry_in_the_device_series(self):
        series = (VENDOR / "patches" / alias_for(self.PROJECT) / "series").read_text()
        self.assertEqual(
            [ln.strip() for ln in series.splitlines() if ln.strip()][-1],
            DEVICE_PATCH)

    def test_kernel_series_contains_the_fragment(self):
        series = (VENDOR / "patches" / alias_for("kernel/nothing/sm7635")
                  / "series").read_text()
        self.assertIn(KERNEL_PATCH, series.splitlines())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

FILE 190/217: tests/test_media_no_dir_listing.py
====================================================================================================
"""MediaProvider does not expose directory listings to apps without storage access.

GrapheneOS commit ``72492da1c`` ("Storage Scopes feature", 2022) closes a
metadata leak in the FUSE readdir path: upstream MediaProvider returns the
files a caller can see from its database, but the native FUSE daemon then
appends **every** directory name from the lower file system. An app with no
storage permission can therefore enumerate all user-created directory names
even though it cannot open them.

The GrapheneOS fix does two things:

* ``getFilesInDirectoryForFuse`` appends an empty-string separator followed by
  the directory names that actually contain files visible to the caller
  (computed from the media database). Apps with a read-media permission and
  the ``Android/`` directory keep the upstream behavior.
* ``MediaProviderWrapper.cpp`` treats entries after the separator as
  directories and skips appending lower-file-system directories.

lenOS ports the directory-listing part only; GrapheneOS's Storage Scopes
(per-app scopes, ``StorageScope``/``GosPackageState``) are not ported yet, so
``StorageScopesHooks`` only implements this hook. The class keeps GrapheneOS's
name and shape so the future Storage Scopes port can extend it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestMediaNoDirectoryListing(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "packages/providers/MediaProvider"
    PATCHES = ["0001-lenos-no-directory-listing.patch"]

    JAVA = "src/com/android/providers/media/MediaProvider.java"
    HOOKS = "src/com/android/providers/media/StorageScopesHooks.java"
    NATIVE = "jni/MediaProviderWrapper.cpp"

    def test_apps_with_media_permissions_keep_upstream_behavior(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.JAVA,
            'if (relativePath.equals("Android/")',
            "callingIdentity.hasPermission(PERMISSION_READ_AUDIO)",
            "callingIdentity.hasPermission(PERMISSION_READ_IMAGES)",
            "callingIdentity.hasPermission(PERMISSION_READ_VIDEO)",
            "return fileNamesList.toArray(new String[0]);")

    def test_other_apps_use_restricted_listing(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.JAVA,
            "return StorageScopesHooks.obtainDirContents(this, path, volumeUri, relativePath,",
            "callingIdentity, fileNamesList);")

    def test_hook_returns_only_directories_with_visible_files(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.HOOKS,
            "MediaColumns.MIME_TYPE + \" not like 'null'\"",
            "QUERY_ARG_SQL_GROUP_BY, MediaColumns.RELATIVE_PATH",
            'maybeAddDirEntry("Android", dirEntries, dirNamesList);',
            '// separator between files and dirs',
            'fileNamesList.add("");',
            "maybeExtractChildDirNameFromRelativePaths(")

    def test_native_skips_lower_fs_directories(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.NATIVE,
            "const string& path, bool* skip_add_dirs)",
            "int de_type = DT_REG;",
            "if (d_name.c_str()[0] == 0) { // see StorageScopesHooks#obtainDirContents",
            "de_type = DT_DIR;",
            "*skip_add_dirs = true;",
            "if (!skip_add_dirs) {")

    def test_single_empty_entry_still_means_no_access(self):
        # The upstream "no access to this path" contract must survive: a
        # one-element [""] array is handled before the separator logic.
        text = self.text(self.NATIVE)
        no_access = text.index("// Calling package has no storage permissions.")
        separator = text.index("if (d_name.c_str()[0] == 0) {")
        self.assertLess(no_access, separator)
        self.assert_contains(self.NATIVE, 'std::make_shared<DirectoryEntry>("", EPERM)')

    def test_javadoc_matches(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.JAVA,
            "<p>When the app has a storage permission, directory names are obtained from lower "
            "file system.")

    def test_syntax(self):
        for f in (self.JAVA, self.HOOKS):
            self.assert_java_syntax(f)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

====================================================================================================
"""GrapheneOS memory hygiene on lock (full compacting GC for both processes).

GrapheneOS runs a full compacting garbage collection for SystemUI and
system_server when the device is locked:

* SystemUI: ``KeyguardViewMediator.handleShowInner`` ends with
  ``System.gc(); System.runFinalization(); System.gc();`` right before the
  show wake lock is released (line-level port).
* system_server: GrapheneOS triggers it from
  ``KeyguardServiceDelegate.onShowingStateChanged``, which runs on a binder
  thread when the keyguard service reports ``showing``.

system_server runs the same three calls on the ``setLockScreenShown`` binder
thread — gated on the false→true transition and placed after the global lock
is released. This is equivalent to where GrapheneOS's callback runs (binder
thread, no WMS lock held).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestMemoryHygieneOnLock(LenosPatchTest):

"""GrapheneOS: the network (INTERNET) permission is a runtime permission.

Tier 1 feature #1 of the lenOS roadmap: port GrapheneOS's "special runtime
permissions" (SRT) framework and use it to make ``android.permission.INTERNET``
revocable by the user, without breaking apps that were written for stock
Android (where INTERNET could not be revoked):

* INTERNET is declared as ``dangerous|instant`` and is *granted by default*
  (auto-granted at install, and to pre-installed system apps on evaluation).
* When the user revokes it, the app keeps running in "internet compat" mode:
  the OS pretends that the network is down (ConnectivityManager/DownloadManager
  return empty results, NSD gets a stubbed connector) and the app's own
  ``checkPermission(INTERNET)`` self-checks are spoofed as granted, so badly
  written apps do not crash with SecurityException.
* The kernel-level block is AOSP's existing netd BPF per-UID socket filtering,
  driven by ``PermissionMonitor`` — no extra plumbing is needed.

The tests pin the patch contents (framework, Connectivity module, permission UI)
and the framework invariants the feature relies on.
"""

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest

"""GrapheneOS parity hardening tweaks (frameworks/base, see docs/features.md).

Small line-level ports from GrapheneOS that close specific gaps:

* ``0012`` flips the seeded default of ``LOCK_SCREEN_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NOTIFICATIONS``
  to ``false``: lockscreen notifications hide their content until the user
  explicitly allows it (new installs/users only; upgraded devices keep the
  stored value).
* ``0011`` PendingIntent immutability warp: apps that forget to pass
  FLAG_IMMUTABLE/FLAG_MUTABLE no longer crash with IllegalArgumentException
  once the S+ compat change is enforced; the framework logs and forces
  FLAG_IMMUTABLE, and all four creation paths honour the returned flags.
  Passing both flags still throws.
* ``0010`` tightens the system-clock paranoia threshold from 2 s to 250 ms so
  unexpected clock changes are logged sooner.
* ``0009`` hardens credential limits to GrapheneOS values: fingerprint
  permanent lockout after 5 failed attempts (was 20) and a maximum password
  length of 128 (was 64).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestCredentialHardening(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "frameworks/base"
    PATCHES = ["0009-lenos-credential-hardening.patch"]
    LOCKOUT = ("services/core/java/com/android/server/biometrics/sensors/"
               "fingerprint/hidl/LockoutFrameworkImpl.java")
    DPM = "core/java/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.java"

        self.assert_contains(

        self.assert_not_contains(
            self.LOCKOUT,
            "MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS_LOCKOUT_PERMANENT = 20;",
        )
        self.assert_java_syntax(self.LOCKOUT)

    def test_maximum_password_length_is_128(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.DPM,
            "public static final int MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 128;",
        )
        self.assert_not_contains(
            self.DPM,
            "public static final int MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 64;",
        )
        self.assert_java_syntax(self.DPM)

"""The patchkit `--reset` mode: return projects to their pinned revision.

`--reset` exists because plain `git checkout` is not enough to undo a patch
series: files the series *creates* (e.g. the device tree's
`lenos_asteroids.mk`) are untracked, survive a checkout, and then make
`git apply --check` fail forever ("already exists"). `--reset` must restore
tracked files, delete the files the series creates, and verify the result.

These tests build a small git repository from the pinned device tree files,
apply a real patch from the series, and run the real tool against it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from harness import VENDOR, WORKSPACE, patch_created_paths, patch_paths

TOOL = VENDOR / "tools" / "lenos-patch.py"
PROJECT = "device/nothing/asteroids"
PATCH_NAME = "0001-add-lenos-product.patch"
PATCH = VENDOR / "patches" / "device_nothing_asteroids" / PATCH_NAME
CREATED = "lenos_asteroids.mk"


def hermetic_env() -> dict:
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = "/dev/null"
    env["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"] = "/dev/null"
    return env


@unittest.skipUnless(WORKSPACE.is_dir(), f"workspace missing: {WORKSPACE}")
class TestPatchkitReset(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="lenos-reset-")
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.pdir = self.root / PROJECT
        self.pdir.mkdir(parents=True)

        created = patch_created_paths(PATCH)
        for rel in patch_paths(PATCH):
            if rel in created:
                continue  # created by git apply; must not exist beforehand
            src = WORKSPACE / PROJECT / rel
            if not src.is_file():
                continue
            dst = self.pdir / rel
            dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            dst.write_bytes(src.read_bytes())

        self.git("init", "--quiet")
        self.git("add", "-A")
        self.git("-c", "user.email=lenos@test", "-c", "user.name=lenos",
                 "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "--quiet", "-m", "pinned")
        self.apply_patch()

    def git(self, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        proc = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=self.pdir,
                              capture_output=True, text=True, env=hermetic_env())
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, f"git {' '.join(args)}: {proc.stderr}")
        return proc

    def apply_patch(self) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        return subprocess.run(
            ["git", "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", str(PATCH)],
            cwd=self.pdir, capture_output=True, text=True, env=hermetic_env())

    def run_reset(self) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(TOOL), "--tree", str(self.root),
             "--reset", "--project", PROJECT],
            capture_output=True, text=True, env=hermetic_env())

    def test_reset_removes_created_files_and_restores_tracked(self):
        self.assertTrue((self.pdir / CREATED).is_file(),
                        "the patch should have created the file")
        products = self.pdir / "AndroidProducts.mk"
        products.write_text(products.read_text(encoding="utf-8") + "\n# stray edit\n",
                            encoding="utf-8")

        proc = self.run_reset()
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr)
        self.assertIn("discarding tracked edits", proc.stdout)
        self.assertIn("AndroidProducts.mk", proc.stdout)
        self.assertFalse((self.pdir / CREATED).exists(),
                         f"--reset must delete the created file {CREATED}")
        self.assertNotIn("# stray edit", products.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        status = self.git("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no")
        self.assertEqual(status.stdout.strip(), "")

    def test_reset_is_idempotent(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_reset().returncode, 0)
        again = self.run_reset()
        self.assertEqual(again.returncode, 0, again.stderr)

    def test_reset_then_apply_works_repeatedly(self):
        # The normal cycle: reset -> apply must keep working, not just once.
        for _ in range(2):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_reset().returncode, 0)
            applied = self.apply_patch()
            self.assertEqual(applied.returncode, 0, applied.stderr)
        self.assertTrue((self.pdir / CREATED).is_file())

    def test_reset_refuses_when_a_created_file_is_tracked(self):
        # Safety: if the pinned tree already contains a file the series claims
        # to create, something is wrong with the patch set - do not delete blindly.
        self.assertEqual(self.run_reset().returncode, 0)
        (self.pdir / CREATED).write_text("// tracked in the pinned tree\n",
                                         encoding="utf-8")
        self.git("add", CREATED)
        self.git("-c", "user.email=lenos@test", "-c", "user.name=lenos",
                 "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "--quiet", "-m", "tracked")
        proc = self.run_reset()
        self.assertNotEqual(proc.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("tracked", proc.stderr)
        self.assertTrue((self.pdir / CREATED).is_file(), "must not be deleted")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""PIN-entry scrambling (GrapheneOS-faithful port).

Feature contract (see docs/features.md):
* The PIN pad is scrambled with java.security.SecureRandom whenever it is set
  up, so shoulder surfing reveals neither the digits nor their positions; the
  digit -> view map keeps hardware-key presses on the correct shuffled key.
* The keyguard PIN honours ExtSettings.SCRAMBLE_LOCKSCREEN_PIN_LAYOUT_PRIMARY;
  SIM PIN/PUK views use SCRAMBLE_SIM_PIN_LAYOUT, which inherits the keyguard
  value by default.
* lenOS hardening deviation (documented): the primary scramble default is ON,
  where GrapheneOS ships the toggle default-OFF. The value stays a normal
  Settings.Secure user setting, exposed through GrapheneOS's
  PinScramblingPrefController and the SIM switch in the ICC lock screen.
* The old LineageOS scramble implementation (KeyguardPINView +
  LineageSettings.System.LOCKSCREEN_PIN_SCRAMBLE_LAYOUT) is fully replaced.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestPinScrambleSetting(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "frameworks/base"

    SETTINGS = "core/java/android/provider/Settings.java"

        self.assert_java_syntax(self.EXT)
        self.assert_java_syntax(self.SETTINGS)

    def test_secure_keys_match_grapheneos(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.SETTINGS,
            '"lockscreen_scramble_pin_layout"',
            '"lockscreen_scramble_pin_layout_secondary"',
            '"scramble_sim_pin_layout"',
        )

    def test_primary_default_is_on_for_lenos(self):
        body = self.text(self.EXT)
        m = re.search(
            r"SCRAMBLE_LOCKSCREEN_PIN_LAYOUT_PRIMARY = new BoolSetting\((.*?)\);",
            body, re.S)
        self.assertIsNotNone(m, "primary scramble setting missing")
        args = m.group(1)
        self.assertIn("Settings.Secure.SCRAMBLE_PIN_LAYOUT_PRIMARY", args)
        self.assertRegex(args, r"\btrue\s*$")

        self.assertIn("SCRAMBLE_LOCKSCREEN_PIN_LAYOUT_PRIMARY::get", m.group(1))

"""Package updates preserve the enabled setting of the package.

Direct port of GrapheneOS commit ``bff727d`` ("always preserve package enabled
setting after package update", 2026-07-29) plus its feature flag. AOSP
implicitly re-enables packages on update in three places:

* system packages when the updated package is installed for a user,
* the calling user after ``pm install``,
* users that already had the package installed.

That behavior is a user-hostile default: an app the user disabled (or a
component the OEM disabled) silently comes back after an update. GrapheneOS
removed all three implicit re-enable paths; the explicit
``setApplicationEnabledSettingPersistent`` session flag and its plumbing stay
in place (the API is still used by ``PackageInstallerSession``/metrics), but
updates no longer consult the flag — they simply never touch the enabled
state.

The GrapheneOS feature name is kept verbatim so apps that probe
``PackageManager.hasSystemFeature("grapheneos.package_update_preserves_package_enabled_setting")``
behave the same as on GrapheneOS.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import LenosPatchTest


class TestPreserveEnabledState(LenosPatchTest):
    PROJECT = "frameworks/base"
    PATCHES = ["0022-lenos-preserve-enabled-state.patch"]

    HELPER = "services/core/java/com/android/server/pm/InstallPackageHelper.java"
    REQUEST = "services/core/java/com/android/server/pm/InstallRequest.java"
    SYSTEM_CONFIG = "services/core/java/com/android/server/SystemConfig.java"
    SESSION = "services/core/java/com/android/server/pm/PackageInstallerSession.java"

    def test_no_implicit_reenable_on_update(self):
        self.assert_not_contains(
            self.HELPER,
            "installRequest.isApplicationEnabledSettingPersistent()",
            "ps.setEnabled(COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DEFAULT,")

    def test_install_request_getter_removed(self):
        self.assert_not_contains(
            self.REQUEST, "public boolean isApplicationEnabledSettingPersistent()")

    def test_feature_flag_matches_grapheneos(self):
        self.assert_contains(
            self.SYSTEM_CONFIG,
            'addFeature("grapheneos.package_update_preserves_package_enabled_setting", 0);')

    def test_unrelated_enable_path_kept(self):
        # The initial system-stub install still has to enable the package.
        self.assert_contains(
            self.HELPER,
            "ps.setEnabled(PackageManager.COMPONENT_ENABLED_STATE_DEFAULT,\n"
            "                        UserHandle.USER_SYSTEM, \"android\");")

    def test_syntax(self):
        for f in (self.HELPER, self.REQUEST, self.SYSTEM_CONFIG):
            self.assert_java_syntax(f)

"""lenOS product configuration (vendor/lenos itself, no upstream patches).

Feature contract (see docs/features.md):
* The product ships a minimal app set plus the lenOS security companion app.
* Privacy-critical resource defaults live in static RROs, not in patched
  upstream files: framework-res NTP fallback, SettingsProvider first-boot
  defaults, NetworkStack connectivity-check endpoints.
* No Google infrastructure is referenced by any lenOS-shipped resource.
* The security app is built against the platform API surface with an explicit,
  least-privilege permission allowlist. Wi-Fi privacy defaults are
  GrapheneOS-faithful per-network defaults (packages/modules/Wifi patch), so
  the app needs no Wi-Fi permissions and carries no global hostname switch.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unittest
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

from harness import VENDOR, java_syntax_errors

ANDROID_NS = "{http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android}"

RROS = {
    "LenosFrameworksOverlay": "android",
    "LenosSettingsProviderOverlay": "com.android.providers.settings",
    "LenosNetworkStackOverlay": "com.android.networkstack",
}


def strip_xml_comments(body: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", "", body, flags=re.S)


def strip_bp_comments(body: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"(?m)^\s*//.*$", "", body)


class ProductConfigTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def text(self, rel: str) -> str:
        path = VENDOR / rel
        self.assertTrue(path.is_file(), f"missing file: {rel}")
        return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


class TestProductMakefile(ProductConfigTestCase):
    MK = "config/lenos.mk"

    def test_ships_the_security_app_and_the_three_overlays(self):
        self.assertIn("LenosSecurity", self.text(self.MK))
        for overlay in RROS:
            self.assertIn(overlay, self.text(self.MK))

    def test_product_properties_are_privacy_hardening(self):
        body = self.text(self.MK)
        for needle in (
            "ro.lenos.version=1.0.0",
            "ro.lenos.base=lineage-24.0",
            "persist.traced.enable=0",
            "persist.logd.size.radio=64K",
            "persist.vendor.radio.adb_log_on=0",
        ):
            self.assertIn(needle, body)

    def test_no_removed_build_variables_or_legacy_props(self):
        body = self.text(self.MK)
        # PRODUCT_PACKAGES_REMOVE does not exist in Lineage 24.0 build/make;
        # app removal is done where the app lists are declared.
        self.assertNotIn("PRODUCT_PACKAGES_REMOVE", body)
        # net.hostname is dead in the modern network stack and must not come
        # back through the product props.
        self.assertNotIn("net.hostname", body)
        # ExactCalculator is already part of the Lineage common app set.
        self.assertNotIn("ExactCalculator", body)

    def test_compressed_apex_is_disabled(self):
        # GrapheneOS parity. updatable_apex.mk is inherited earlier, through
        # lineage_asteroids.mk -> full_base_telephony.mk -> generic_system.mk,
        # and sets PRODUCT_COMPRESSED_APEX := true; lenos.mk is inherited
        # afterwards, so the last (this) assignment wins.
        body = self.text(self.MK)
        self.assertEqual(
            len(re.findall(r"(?m)^PRODUCT_COMPRESSED_APEX := false$", body)), 1)
        # And no other assignment that could win later (comments mention the
        # upstream "true" default, so anchor to line starts).
        self.assertEqual(
            len(re.findall(r"(?m)^PRODUCT_COMPRESSED_APEX\s*:?=", body)), 1)

    def test_build_time_overlay_approach_is_gone(self):
        # Replaced by input RROs: PRODUCT_ENFORCE_RRO_TARGETS := * in the
        # device tree converts product overlays to RROs anyway, and the RROs
        # are explicit about target packages and priority.
        self.assertFalse((VENDOR / "overlay").exists(),
                         "vendor/lenos/overlay must not exist anymore")

            self.assertIn(f'name: "{overlay}"', body)
            self.assertIn("device_specific: true", body)

            self.assertEqual(root.tag, "manifest", rel)
            self.assertTrue(root.get("package"), rel)
            node = root.find("overlay")
            self.assertIsNotNone(node, rel)
            self.assertEqual(node.get(f"{ANDROID_NS}targetPackage"), target, rel)
            self.assertEqual(node.get(f"{ANDROID_NS}isStatic"), "true", rel)
            application = root.find("application")
            self.assertIsNotNone(application, f"{rel}: hasCode declaration missing")
            self.assertEqual(application.get(f"{ANDROID_NS}hasCode"), "false", rel)

            node = root.find("overlay")

            if overlay == "LenosNetworkStackOverlay":
                self.assertEqual(target_name, "NetworkStackConfig")
            else:

            self.assertNotIn(banned, body)

        self.assertIn("ntp://pool.ntp.org", body)
        for banned in ("google", "android.com", "grapheneos"):
            self.assertNotIn(banned, body)

    def test_settings_defaults_are_hardened_and_do_not_overlap_device_rros(self):
        body = self.text("rro/LenosSettingsProviderOverlay/res/values/defaults.xml")
        for needle in (
            '<string name="def_lenos_private_dns_mode" translatable="false">hostname</string>',
            '<string name="def_lenos_private_dns_specifier" translatable="false">dns.quad9.net</string>',
            '<string name="def_lenos_ntp_server" translatable="false">pool.ntp.org</string>',
            '<bool name="def_bluetooth_on">false</bool>',
            '<bool name="def_wifi_wakeup_enabled">false</bool>',
            '<bool name="def_networks_available_notification_on">false</bool>',
            '<integer name="def_location_mode">0</integer>',
            '<bool name="def_usb_mass_storage_enabled">false</bool>',
            '<bool name="def_lock_screen_show_qr_code_scanner">false</bool>',
        ):
            self.assertIn(needle, body)
        # Wi-Fi privacy defaults are carried by the Wi-Fi module patch
        # (packages_modules_Wifi/0001) since the GrapheneOS-fidelity redo; the
        # RRO must not define a competing value.
        self.assertNotIn("def_lenos_wifi_force_non_persistent_mac_randomization", body)
        # def_device_name is owned by the device RROs (patched by
        # device_nothing_asteroids/0006-privacy-device-name.patch); defining
        # it here as well would create two competing static overlays.
        self.assertNotIn("def_device_name", body)


class TestSecurityApp(ProductConfigTestCase):

"""Quick settings unlock gating (frameworks/base SystemUI patch).

Feature contract (see docs/features.md), ported from GrapheneOS:
* Every tile action (click, secondary click, long click) is routed through
  QSTileImpl#handleAction. Tiles opt in to lock-screen use by overriding
  isAllowedWhenLocked; the default is "not allowed".
* When a secure keyguard is showing, a non-allowed action does not run and
  is not silently dropped: the keyguard is dismissed with
  ActivityStarter#postQSRunnableDismissingKeyguard, so the user is asked to
  authenticate and the action runs only after a successful unlock.
* Devices without a secure lock, and the normal unlocked case, are
  unaffected.
* The allow-list matches GrapheneOS: flashlight (incl. brightness-level
  variant), QR code scanner, color inversion, color correction, Night Light,
  reduce bright colors, dark theme, rotation lock, battery saver or device
  controls. Sensitive tiles (radios, connectivity, camera, hotspot, DND,
  data saver) are deliberately not allow-listed.
* Stock paths are preserved: policy-disabled tiles still open the
  admin-support dialog first, and metrics logging still happens before the
  gate, as upstream.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from harness import VENDOR, LenosPatchTest
